Changes Since 2023.100.0.273

Signed Distance Field ("SDF") Font Support

  • You can now use font_add() to load a font and then draw it using the SDF method, which allows more advanced rendering of your fonts
  • There are two new GML functions to enable\disable rendering using SDFs:
  • font_enable_sdf(font, true/false) - allows enabling or disabling SDF rendering for that font
  • font_get_sdf_enabled(font) - queries whether SDF rendering is currently enabled for that font
  • Note that the font must be loaded via font_add() in-game to use this functionality - fonts added inside the IDE are not supported
  • Note also that at this time HTML5 is not supported - the functionality will be ignored

New "Tremolo" Audio Effect

  • This is a gain modulation effect, with modulation being driven by a separate low-frequency oscillator (LFO) for each channel. This allows for effects from gentle gain fluctuations all the way to stuttering with ping-pong panning
  • The effect has the following parameters:
  • type - A read-only member which is set to AudioEffectType.Tremolo (a new member of the AudioEffectType enum)
  • bypass - A flag which can be set to bypass the effect
  • rate - The frequency of the LFO modulating the gain (0.0-20.0 Hz)
  • intensity - The proportion of the input signal which should be modulated by the LFO (0.0-1.0)
  • offset - The proportion of a waveform's period that the right-hand channel's LFO should be offset by, compared to the left-hand channel (0.0-1.0)
  • shape - The waveform shape that the LFO should output

Ability To Add All Sprite Types To Texture Groups

  • Spine, SWF, and those with "Separate Texture Page" selected now appear in the Texture Groups Editor inside the IDE and can be added as part of your other groups
  • Whilst these images still have thir own texture pages, you can now load/unload them at the same time as the rest of the group using the existing in-game functions
  • (Note: This was previously announced in Beta 1's notes, but is operational now)

Added HTML5 obfuscation settings in Preferences

  • As the HTML5 runner has now been open-sourced, you can use these new settings to help track down issues in your games more easily:
  • Obfuscate (or not), Pretty Print, Remove Unused Functions, and Verbose (or not)
  • These can be found in the Platform Settings section for HTML5

Misc New Functions

  • array_get_index() and array_contains() can now be used to find values in an array
  • move_and_collide() can now be used for moving to a new location and detecting collisions with other instances along the way (tile collisions are not supported)
  • And the recently-added array_shuffle() now has optional offset and length parameters you can use

Changes To Behaviours Of Statics

  • Improved handling of static values so it is more intuitive, by introducing the idea of a static chain (via inheritance) - so when using FuncName.varname syntax the entire chain is checked when varname is looked up
  • Introduces a few new functions also:
  • is_instanceof(struct, FuncName) returns true if struct has anywhere in its static chain
  • static_get(struct or FuncName) returns the static struct for a given struct or FuncName, or “undefined” if it has no static
  • static_set(struct, struct) sets the static for a struct to point at another struct (Note: You should be very careful using this one, as it is provided for deserialisation use-cases only)

Additional Functions

  • array_shuffle() works the same as ds_list_shuffle() in that this new function will randomly reorder elements of an array - note that the existing array is modified and you do not get a new copy returned
  • tileset_get_info() works the same as spite/font_get_info() and returns a struct containing lots of information about this tileset (or "undefined" if the argument is not a valid tileset)
  • audio_effect_create() now has an optional second argument for passing in a struct to be used to initialise the effect parameters immediately

2023.100.0.264

Changes to the “Base” runtime module, so you only download the tools for that IDE

  • In all older runtimes, the “Base” module has always included all the tools required for Windows, Mac, and Ubuntu IDEs, so the download size has grown over time
  • Now, the “base” entry in the Runtime Modules dialog within the IDE will only download the tools relevant for the IDE you’re using, saving you time downloading and space on disk (and the same happens if you’re using Igor via command line tools to download your runtimes)

Changes To Behaviours Of Statics

  • Improved handling of static values so it is more intuitive, by introducing the idea of a static chain (via inheritance) - so when using FuncName.varname syntax the entire chain is checked when varname is looked up
  • Introduces a few new functions also:
  • is_instanceof(struct, FuncName) returns true if struct has anywhere in its static chain
  • static_get(struct or FuncName) returns the static struct for a given struct or FuncName, or “undefined” if it has no static
  • static_set(struct, struct) sets the static for a struct to point at another struct (Note: You should be very careful using this one, as it is provided for deserialisation use-cases only)

Additional Functions

  • array_shuffle() works the same as ds_list_shuffle() in that this new function will randomly reorder elements of an array - note that the existing array is modified and you do not get a new copy returned
  • tileset_get_info() works the same as spite/font_get_info() and returns a struct containing lots of information about this tileset (or "undefined" if the argument is not a valid tileset)
  • audio_effect_create() now has an optional second argument for passing in a struct to be used to initialise the effect parameters immediately

November’s release includes several new in-game filter effects for you to use and a lot of new or improved functions for audio, arrays, Spine, string-manipulation, and others. It updates the libraries used for gamepads, websockets and Gradle to fix a number of issues already resolved by these external tools. On consoles, these runtimes introduce the ability for PS5 players to use their existing PS4 saves for the same game, plus adds support for Xbox developers to determine users who are streaming the game on mobile devices. Along with all of that, there are fixes for a large number of other bugs as well - including some quite important changes to HTML5 behaviours, which you can read more about below.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.9.1 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since 2022.11.0

  • PS4 - The SDK version required is now 10.00.94, which is a slight increase over the older-but-still-"10.000" SDK which 2022.11.0 requires
  • Building Projects: Texture pages no longer get overlapping sprites in some cases (was only an issue in 2022.11.0 builds)
  • Debugger: Fixed an issue where GameMaker locks up (and potentially RAM usage jumps up also) when hovering over any object instance values in a debugger event window which has hit a breakpoint/been paused
  • In-Game: Fixed that games sometimes failed to start in 2022.11.0 builds due to an audio thread initialisation issue (typically blamed either a collision event time error or just stopped on AudioInit() in the compiler log), which was a source of ANRs on Google Play and inconsistent Steam startups

2022.11.0

Added More Filter Layer Types

  • Old Film, Hue, Ripples, Blocks Background, Panorama Background and Parallax Background have all now been added for you to use in your games
  • Also fixed an issue with the existing Boxes filter which meant it didn't work on HTML5

Audio Filters/Effects Support

  • We have now added support for calling a number of new audio filters in your games and modifying their values in real time
  • audio_bus_create(), audio_effect_create(), audio_emitter_bus(), and audio_emitter_get_bus() are all new and allow you to call your choice of the following effects:
  • Bitcrusher (which is a form of distortion), Delay, Gain, HPF2 (a high-pass filter), LPF2 (a low-pass filter), and Reverb1

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • Because there are a lot of them, we will just quickly list the basics here, but of course more on all of these can be found in the manual (along with all the other existing array functions)
  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array

Added More Functions For Spine

  • skeleton_attachment_exists() can be used to check if an attachment with the given name has already been created
  • skeleton_attachment_replace() and skeleton_attachment_destroy() can now be used to modify the attachments on your skeletons
  • And the existing function skeleton_attachment_create() will now return an error if you try to reuse an attachment name without destroying it first

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation:
  • string_format(string, arg0. arg1, ...) allows you to insert values dynamically into your strings by replacing numbers in braces with the arguments you specify - e.g. string_format("Hello {0}, this is my cool new {1}". “World”, “string functions”);
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) is the same as above, but takes an array as the argument
  • string_trim(string) returns a string which has removed all leading and trailing whitespace from the source string
  • string_trim_start(string) / string_trim_end(string) do the same as above, but for only one end of the string
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) returns true/false for whether the string starts with the specified substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) the same as above, but at the end of the string
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) splits the string into an array using the delimiter you provide
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) is the same as above, but takes an array of delimiter values and will split for all of them
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) / string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity)the opposite of the two above and creates a spring using the delimiter to join all given arguments
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) / string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) do basically the same as string_join(), but using a fixed value of "" (empty string) as the delimiter
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) iterates over each character in the string, executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(string, arg0. arg1, ...) the previous functionality will still work, so there is no need to edit your code, but be aware this function now accepts brace arguments the same as string_format()
  • show_debug_message_ext(string, arg_array) and a new version, which works as above but using an argument array

Multi-Touch Input For GDK games

  • Touch inputs can now be read from devices while using Xbox Game Streaming by using the following new functions:
  • xboxone_streaming_is_enabled() - returns 1 if the game is currently being streamed, or 0 if it isn't
  • xboxone_streaming_set_show_controls(enable) - note that this overlay is always disabled if a physical controller is being used with the streaming device
  • xboxone_streaming_get_show_controls() - returns whether the overlay is currently showing
  • xboxone_streaming_get_info() - returns a struct containing a variety of information about the current state of the streaming state

Changes To HTML5 Step Event And Instance Creation Behaviours

  • All runners keep lists of the active instances and these are sorted by their depth, but HTML5 had them sorted in the opposite direction which caused a different order of event execution. E.g. on other platforms if the Step event of instance A was executed first, B second and C third, then on HTML5 it would be C/B/A - HTML5 now behaves the same as the other platforms
  • Additionally, on all other platforms if you created an instance in the Step event (for example), then that new instance's Step event wouldn't be executed until the next frame, but on HTML5 it would be executed immediately - again, HTML5 now behaves the same as the other platforms
  • This fixes a number of projects that have had issues on HTML5 and means HTML5 now has more behaviour parity with the other platforms, but may have a negative effect if you relied on these particular HTML5 behaviours in your games

Misc Changes To Be Aware Of

  • The order of elements in the colourMultiply array in the activeTracks member of the sequence instance struct is now ARGB, which is consistent with how it has always been described in the manual, but this will cause incorrect results in projects which expected the order to be RGBA (as was incorrectly used in previous GM releases)
  • Gamepad mappings library for Windows/macOS/Ubuntu/Android was getting quite old, so it has now been updated to the latest database release - this should fix a variety of pad issues
  • CPU-side "frustum" culling was not being performed correctly, but has now been fixed for regular sprites [we are aware some issues remain with Spine sprites and tiles]
  • Cleanup events are no longer repeated if using a with() to destroy an object inside a second object's Cleanup event
  • Fixed that behaviours when calling event_inherited() from a script differed between VM and YYC - VM projects would incorrectly “fix the issue” and run anyway, so VM has now been changed to give a coding error dialog the same as YYC always has
  • Updated the LibreSSL version used by the websockets functionality on some platforms
  • Gradle version has been updated to match the requirements of Android APIs 32+
  • libvorbis error codes when creating .ogg files are now accompanied with a description - this will help with understanding some audio errors that may come up
  • audio_group_get_gain(groupName) has been added to return the current gain value of a specified audio group
  • audio_sync_group_is_paused(groupName) has been added to check if an audio sync group is paused or not
  • matrix_transform_vertex() now can take an optional 4th argument
  • os_is_network_connected() has two new constants you can use ("network_connect_active", which is the existing/previous behaviour and will show prompts when no connection has been found, and "network_connect_passive" which is the new behaviour and will not show the prompts)
  • shader_set_uniform_f_buffer() has been added to allow sending a buffer directly to a shader
  • time_source_destroy() now takes an optional argument to destroy the whole tree at once
  • We are aware of an intermittent and machine-dependant issue where the very first run of a new project sometimes fails with a collision event time error in Nov22 Beta 3 and newer, and so we have added more logging for this - if you do get this issue, please file a ticket with your output log

Jan’s release sees a number of tools changes designed to speed up project-loading, importing assets, and reduce install sizes for the runtimes. There are also a number of important fixes for the Debugger crashing and using up too much memory, plus for the MQTT server if you happen to be offline or have GameMaker behind a firewall.

Some new functions have been added/changed also, so you can find details of these below.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.11.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes to the “Base” runtime module, so you only download the tools for that IDE

  • In all older runtimes, the “Base” module has always included all the tools required for Windows, Mac, and Ubuntu IDEs, so the download size has grown over time
  • Now, the “base” entry in the Runtime Modules dialog within the IDE will only download the tools relevant for the IDE you’re using, saving you time downloading and space on disk (and the same happens if you’re using Igor via command line tools to download your runtimes)

Changes To Behaviours Of Statics

  • Improved handling of static values so it is more intuitive, by introducing the idea of a static chain (via inheritance) - so when using FuncName.varname syntax the entire chain is checked when varname is looked up
  • Introduces a few new functions also:
  • is_instanceof(struct, FuncName) returns true if struct has anywhere in its static chain
  • static_get(struct or FuncName) returns the static struct for a given struct or FuncName, or “undefined” if it has no static
  • static_set(struct, struct) sets the static for a struct to point at another struct (Note: You should be very careful using this one, as it is provided for deserialisation use-cases only)

Additional Functions

  • array_shuffle() works the same as ds_list_shuffle() in that this new function will randomly reorder elements of an array - note that the existing array is modified and you do not get a new copy returned
  • tileset_get_info() works the same as spite/font_get_info() and returns a struct containing lots of information about this tileset (or "undefined" if the argument is not a valid tileset)
  • audio_effect_create() now has an optional second argument for passing in a struct to be used to initialise the effect parameters immediately

<ul>
• Up until this release, you were unable to use GameMaker offline if you had migrated your account and signed-in using the Opera Account single sign-in method
• You now can sign-in to a saved Opera Account session and carry on offline for the usual must-go-online-once-a-month requirement that GameMaker Accounts have long used
Pinch-To-Zoom Has Been Re-Implemented
<ul>
• The Workspace can now be zoomed in and out on devices with touch inputs (like trackpads)
• Windows IDE, this is done via Ctrl plus one finger on the trackpad; Mac IDE, it’s a two-finger pinch gesture
• There is a new Preference to disable this feature if you don’t want it
Image Editor Support For Pasting As A New Layer
<ul>
• The Image Editor now allows you to paste directly from your clipboard to a new layer
• This new layer will be automatically placed above the currently-selected layer and the pan tool will be auto-selected to immediately allow you to control the pasted content as you wish
• This is the default behaviour now, as there was a lot of feedback in favour of this change, but the previous “Paste-As-Brush” behaviour can be enabled again in Preferences if you want it
Implemented Case-Insensitive Compatibility Mode For The Mac IDE
<ul>

• There has been an ongoing issue with case-sensitivity when working across different operating systems and changing an asset's character case when renaming it (and how this change of case might then effect external tools, such as git)
• An option has been added to allow you to disable these extra renaming checks, as it is quite performance-heavy
• (The same changes affect the Ubuntu IDE Beta also, as it behaves the same as the Mac IDE)
Feather Additions
<ul>
• Feather Now reparses scripts whenever they are edited outside GameMaker
• The new rule GM2064 will validate that initialiser struct variables have variable definitions for the target object (and its Quick Fixes will now create Variable Definitions for missing fields)
• GM1013’s Quick Fix behaviour has now been modified for creating an instance variable
Device Manager Support For Opera GX Mobile Devices
<ul>
• You will likely see a new firewall prompt for this the first time you start this new version, so for more information on this functionality and how to use it, please see our new FAQ all about it
• Added a new MQTT server for discovering Opera GX Mobile devices on your network, allowing you to just as easily test your GX games on your phone or tablet as you can on your desktop
• Simply scan the QR code inside Device Manager to connect the mobile device to GameMaker in seconds
• Note that your devices are only linked to that one instance of GameMaker and will be forgotten the next time you close GameMaker
More Room Editor Layers Functionality
<ul>
• Old Film, Hue, Ripples, Blocks Background, Panorama Background and Parallax Background have all now been added into the Room Editor for you to use in your games
• Also added an indicator into the Layers Panel to show when any filter/effect has been used on a layer
Code Editor Support For Binary Literals And Underscores In Numbers
<ul>
• Binary literals can now be declared in the form 0b…. (same as the hex literal 0x… that GameMaker has supported for a while). For example: var six = 0b0110; or var thirteen = 0b0100 | 0b1001;

• Also, integer, floating point, hex, and binary literals may now take an underscore to act as a visual separator. For example: var integer = 100_000_000; or var float = 3_141.59; or var hexadec = 0xDEAD_BEEF; or var binary = 0b01101000_01101001;
• Note that this is a Code Editor and Compiler change only - there is no support for this in-game

November’s release includes several new in-game filter effects for you to use and a lot of new or improved functions for audio, arrays, Spine, string-manipulation, and others. It updates the libraries used for gamepads, websockets and Gradle to fix a number of issues already resolved by these external tools. On consoles, these runtimes introduce the ability for PS5 players to use their existing PS4 saves for the same game, plus adds support for Xbox developers to determine users who are streaming the game on mobile devices. Along with all of that, there are fixes for a large number of other bugs as well - including some quite important changes to HTML5 behaviours, which you can read more about below.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.9.1 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Added More Filter Layer Types

  • Old Film, Hue, Ripples, Blocks Background, Panorama Background and Parallax Background have all now been added for you to use in your games
  • Also fixed an issue with the existing Boxes filter which meant it didn't work on HTML5

Audio Filters/Effects Support

  • We have now added support for calling a number of new audio filters in your games and modifying their values in real time
  • audio_bus_create(), audio_effect_create(), audio_emitter_bus(), and audio_emitter_get_bus() are all new and allow you to call your choice of the following effects:
  • Bitcrusher (which is a form of distortion), Delay, Gain, HPF2 (a high-pass filter), LPF2 (a low-pass filter), and Reverb1

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • Because there are a lot of them, we will just quickly list the basics here, but of course more on all of these can be found in the manual (along with all the other existing array functions)
  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array

Added More Functions For Spine

  • skeleton_attachment_exists() can be used to check if an attachment with the given name has already been created
  • skeleton_attachment_replace() and skeleton_attachment_destroy() can now be used to modify the attachments on your skeletons
  • And the existing function skeleton_attachment_create() will now return an error if you try to reuse an attachment name without destroying it first

Added support for reading PS4 save files in a PS5 game

  • Your PS5 games can now see and read PS4 saves for the same title (note that this is not supported PS5-to-PS4)

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation:
  • string_format(string, arg0. arg1, ...) allows you to insert values dynamically into your strings by replacing numbers in braces with the arguments you specify - e.g. string_format("Hello {0}, this is my cool new {1}". “World”, “string functions”);
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) is the same as above, but takes an array as the argument
  • string_trim(string) returns a string which has removed all leading and trailing whitespace from the source string
  • string_trim_start(string) / string_trim_end(string) do the same as above, but for only one end of the string
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) returns true/false for whether the string starts with the specified substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) the same as above, but at the end of the string
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) splits the string into an array using the delimiter you provide
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) is the same as above, but takes an array of delimiter values and will split for all of them
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) / string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity)the opposite of the two above and creates a spring using the delimiter to join all given arguments
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) / string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) do basically the same as string_join(), but using a fixed value of "" (empty string) as the delimiter
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) iterates over each character in the string, executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(string, arg0. arg1, ...) the previous functionality will still work, so there is no need to edit your code, but be aware this function now accepts brace arguments the same as string_format()
  • show_debug_message_ext(string, arg_array) and a new version, which works as above but using an argument array

Multi-Touch Input For GDK games

  • Touch inputs can now be read from devices while using Xbox Game Streaming by using the following new functions:
  • xboxone_streaming_is_enabled() - returns 1 if the game is currently being streamed, or 0 if it isn't
  • xboxone_streaming_set_show_controls(enable) - note that this overlay is always disabled if a physical controller is being used with the streaming device
  • xboxone_streaming_get_show_controls() - returns whether the overlay is currently showing
  • xboxone_streaming_get_info() - returns a struct containing a variety of information about the current state of the streaming state

Changes To HTML5 Step Event And Instance Creation Behaviours

  • All runners keep lists of the active instances and these are sorted by their depth, but HTML5 had them sorted in the opposite direction which caused a different order of event execution. E.g. on other platforms if the Step event of instance A was executed first, B second and C third, then on HTML5 it would be C/B/A - HTML5 now behaves the same as the other platforms
  • Additionally, on all other platforms if you created an instance in the Step event (for example), then that new instance's Step event wouldn't be executed until the next frame, but on HTML5 it would be executed immediately - again, HTML5 now behaves the same as the other platforms
  • This fixes a number of projects that have had issues on HTML5 and means HTML5 now has more behaviour parity with the other platforms, but may have a negative effect if you relied on these particular HTML5 behaviours in your games

Misc Changes To Be Aware Of

  • The order of elements in the colourMultiply array in the activeTracks member of the sequence instance struct is now ARGB, which is consistent with how it has always been described in the manual, but this will cause incorrect results in projects which expected the order to be RGBA (as was incorrectly used in previous GM releases)
  • Gamepad mappings library for Windows/macOS/Ubuntu/Android was getting quite old, so it has now been updated to the latest database release - this should fix a variety of pad issues
  • CPU-side "frustum" culling was not being performed correctly, but has now been fixed for regular sprites [we are aware some issues remain with Spine sprites and tiles]
  • Cleanup events are no longer repeated if using a with() to destroy an object inside a second object's Cleanup event
  • Fixed that behaviours when calling event_inherited() from a script differed between VM and YYC - VM projects would incorrectly “fix the issue” and run anyway, so VM has now been changed to give a coding error dialog the same as YYC always has
  • Updated the LibreSSL version used by the websockets functionality on some platforms
  • Gradle version has been updated to match the requirements of Android APIs 32+
  • libvorbis error codes when creating .ogg files are now accompanied with a description - this will help with understanding some audio errors that may come up
  • audio_group_get_gain(groupName) has been added to return the current gain value of a specified audio group
  • audio_sync_group_is_paused(groupName) has been added to check if an audio sync group is paused or not
  • matrix_transform_vertex() now can take an optional 4th argument
  • os_is_network_connected() has two new constants you can use ("network_connect_active", which is the existing/previous behaviour and will show prompts when no connection has been found, and "network_connect_passive" which is the new behaviour and will not show the prompts)
  • shader_set_uniform_f_buffer() has been added to allow sending a buffer directly to a shader
  • time_source_destroy() now takes an optional argument to destroy the whole tree at once
  • We are aware of an intermittent and machine-dependant issue where the very first run of a new project sometimes fails with a collision event time error in Nov22 Beta 3 and newer, and so we have added more logging for this - if you do get this issue, please file a ticket with your output log

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array
  • More on all of these can be found in the manual, along with all the other existing array functions

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array
  • More on all of these can be found in the manual, along with all the other existing array functions

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

Beta Runtime 248

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array
  • More on all of these can be found in the manual, along with all the other existing array functions

November will include a lot of functionality for audio, arrays, Spine, and others. Plus, it also introduces the ability for PS5 players to use their existing PS4 saves for the same game. It also fixes a number of issues to do with filters and effects, and many other bugs as well.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.9.1 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since Beta Runtime 219

Enhanced String Functions

  • Some older string functions have been changed to allow for far more control over formatting as well as many new functions for easier string manipulation
  • string(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → String - Creates a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the arguments
  • string_ext(format, arg_array) → String - Same as above but takes an array argument
  • string_trim_start(string) → String - Returns a string removing leading white space
  • string_trim_end(string) → String - Returns a string removing trailing white space
  • string_trim(string) → String - Returns a string removing all leading and trailing white space
  • string_starts_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns true if string starts with substring
  • string_ends_with(string, substr) → Bool - Returns false is string ends with substring
  • string_split(string, delimiter, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Splits the string into an array using delimeter
  • string_split_ext(string, delimit_array, remove_empty = false, max_splits = infinity) → Array - Same as above but can take an array of delimeter values
  • string_join(delimit, arg0, arg1, arg2, ...) → String - Using the delimeter to join all given arguments
  • string_join_ext(delimit, array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes an array
  • string_concat(arg0, arg1, arg2, arg3) → String - Basically the same as string_join but using "" (empty string) as the delimeter
  • string_concat_ext(string_array, offset = 0, length = infinity) → String - Same as above but takes a string array
  • string_foreach(string, function, pos = 1, length = infinity) → Undefined - Iterates over each character executing the given callback function
  • show_debug_message(format, arg0. arg1, ...) → undefined - The previous functionality will still work but now it accepts formatting: Logs a new string from a format of type: "string {0} with some value {1}". Where {0} and {1} are value placeholders for the followed arguments
  • show_debug_message_ext(format, arg_array) → undefined - As above but with an argument array

Beta Runtime 210

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array
  • More on all of these can be found in the manual, along with all the other existing array functions

Added More Functions For Spine

  • skeleton_attachment_exists() can be used to check if an attachment with the given name has already been created
  • skeleton_attachment_replace() and skeleton_attachment_destroy() can now be used to modify the attachments on your skeletons
  • And the existing function skeleton_attachment_create() will now return an error if you try to reuse an attachment name without destroying it first

Added support for reading PS4 save files in a PS5 game

  • Your PS5 games can now see and read PS4 saves for the same title (note that this is not supported PS5-to-PS4)

November will include a lot of functionality for audio, arrays, Spine, and others. Plus, it also introduces the ability for PS5 players to use their existing PS4 saves for the same game. It also fixes a number of issues to do with filters and effects, and many other bugs as well.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.9.1 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since Beta Runtime 214

Multi-Touch Input for GDK games

  • Touch inputs can now be read from devices while streaming (using Xbox Game Streaming)
  • xboxone_streaming_is_enabled() - returns 1 if the game is currently being streamed, or 0 if it isn't
  • xboxone_streaming_set_show_controls(enable) - Note that this overlay is always disabled if a physical controller is being used with the streaming device.
  • xboxone_streaming_get_show_controls() / xboxone_streaming_set_show_controls()
  • xboxone_streaming_get_info() - returns a struct containing a variety of information

HTML5 Step Event and Instance Creation

  • Step Event and Instance creation on HTML5 now has more behaviour parity with the other platforms
  • The order of execution of Step events per instance is now the same order, and newly created instances step events will wait until the next frame on HTML5 to execute
  • This fixes a number of projects that have had issues on HTML5 but may have a negative effect if you relied on this particular HTML5 behaviour

Misc Changes To Be Aware Of

  • libvorbis error codes are now accompanied with a description - this will help with understanding some audio errors that may come up

Bugs Fixed

  • In-Game: [HTML5] Inconsistent behaviour of step event of newly created instances
  • In-Game: [HTML5] structs report that they contain x and y variables
  • In-Game: Inconsistent behaviour when requesting a track position beyond the end of a sound asset's duration.
  • In-Game: The built-in variable font_texture_page_size has an odd default value (4652218415073722368)
  • Output Console: Creating an audio stream with a file other than a .ogg file will produce a less than useful error

Beta Runtime 214

Audio Filters/Effects Support

  • We have now added support for calling a number of new audio filters in your games

  • Bitcrusher (which is a form of distorsion), Delay, Gain, HPF2 (a high-pass filter), LPF2 (a low-pass filter), and Reverb1

  • array_join() is now called array_concat() (and the old name from Beta 1 will no longer work, so you will need to edit your code accordingly)

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool

• Feather: Now alerts you when two functions are declared with the same name in a single script/event, as this has always been a compile fail
• Feather: Code referencing asset names is now updated correctly when those asset are renamed in the Asset Browser (if you have this Preference enabled)
Opera Account Settings Migration
<ul>

• In previous releases, if you used one email address for your GameMaker account and a different email for your Opera Account and you have already converted your GameMaker account to be an Opera account on our website, then this would cause your Preferences and Recent Projects, etc., to be “lost”, because GameMaker is now looking in a new folder for them

• This version will rename the original folder for you and avoid you having to “migrate” your settings manually; however, it will only do this if you have not converted already - if you have already converted your account and so this issue applies to you, please see our FAQ for how to quickly and easily recover your settings
Changes To The Default Project Layout
<ul>

• The default project layout now includes the Inspector as a new left-hand dock (but of course it is freely movable and dockable) and no longer includes Recent Windows as a panel inside the right-hand dock
• Though the Inspector has been around for a long time already, we are now bringing it to the front and making it more relevant inside other editors

• Please note that any existing layouts in your projects are of course unaffected by this change, and so if you want to see the changes you can use Layout -> Reset Layout menubar option. (If you have a highly customised layout you use in your projects you may also want to use Save Layout and ensure you backup your current layout.)
• Recent Windows can still be opened from the Windows menubar entry and added to your project layout again if you wish
Changes To How GameMaker Loads/Saves Game Options
<ul>

• Up until now, GameMaker always treated the licence of the last person to open a project as the definitive list of game options that project requires - so if one team member has a lot of targets on their licence all of them would be configured and if the project was then shared with a new team member who only had Test, a lot of those options would be removed again
• Now, your options will “merge” - so if you have team members who have different licence types, the Game Options values will remain in the project and cover everyone’s licences
New Room Inspector And Changes To The Room Editor Layout
<ul>
• The new Room Inspector is how you will now access many of the settings for rooms

• Before, all of a room’s settings and its layers were cramped into a single panel; now, all of the settings are handled as part of the Inspector and the Layers panel is a dockable panel which can be detached and placed where you want

• The Inspector UI is also more dynamic/responsive and only shows certain functionality if it’s relevant (e.g., Inheritance settings are only shown in the Inspector if you are in a child room, rather than always being shown in the old Room Editor layout)
”Opera GX” Target Rebranded As “GX.games”
<ul>
• The target has always been part of a whole ecosystem of releasing your games on the GX.games site and sharing them with others (for free or as paid content), so this new name clarifies that
• If you have not had a look at GX.games and what it offers, please do check it out and play a few games, see if it’s a route you would like to take also
• You already have access to publish games on it (for free) as part of your Opera Account and you can also see our tutorial about what publishing on GX.games involves if you want more info
• Also added a new "os_gxgames" constant (which duplicates the existing "os_operagx", so you do not need to change existing code) in order to be consistent in-game with this branding change
New Options For Texture Group Management
<ul>

• You will now find the texture groups editor has new controls for whether you want to split textures off into their own data files on disk during your builds, as this can be required by bigger games on some platforms which have memory caps on how much data you can have loaded at any moment (e.g., GX.games only allows 2GB)
• You can then use the matching 2022.9 runtimes to load/unload these groups in-game as you require
New Visual Node “Add Motion”
<ul>

• This new function takes a direction and speed and modifies the in-built hspeed and vspeed values accordingly - so you have the one node to manage, but can change several values at once behind-the-scenes (the node performs the following code: hspeed += speed * dcos(direction); vspeed += speed * -dsin(direction);)
• The new node will be part of an upcoming tutorial, so please keep an eye on our tutorials website for more information

• The micro web server is now always stopped when the main IDE is closed, which stops a number of issues (such as “GameMaker is already running” when trying to install an update), but please be aware of this if you’re testing your games after closing GM itself

The feature set for this release is based off 2022.9.1 and so will always look and feel very similar to that one; however, we will periodically update this release with just the essential bug fixes or SDK updates, so that you can continue using this version in confidence that it won't change dramatically over time.

2022.9.1.66

Windows Games Now Have Multitouch Support

  • Windows now supports multitouch (just the same as UWP did in older releases)
  • Please note that this does not apply to Windows 7 - it's only supported by Windows 8.0 and newer

Windows Games Now Report DLL Load Errors More Effectively

  • Currently, most DLL load errors on Windows look something like LoadLibraryW ...\Some.dll failed with error code 126
  • This has now been extended so that the message will display the function name (so that an incompatible DLL doesn't display multiple identical errors), whether the DLL has a valid header, and whether the DLL has been built correctly for this Runner's architecture - this last one will help greatly in identifying when you are accidentally using a 32bit extension, etc.

New Options For Texture Group Management

  • You will now find the texture groups editor in the 2022.9 IDE has new controls for whether you want to split textures off into their own data files on disk during your builds, as this can be required by bigger games on some platforms which have memory caps on how much data you can have loaded at any moment (e.g., GX.games only allows 2GB)
  • You can then use these matching runtimes to load/unload these groups in-game as you require - using the new texturegroup_get_status() to query the current state

PlayStation SDK Updates And Additions

  • PS4 building now requires SDK v10.0 to be installed
  • PS5 building now requires SDK v6.0 to be installed
  • On PS4 only, added "succeeded" and "padindex" keys to the async map for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_MSG
  • On PS4 only, added a "succeeded" key to the async map generated for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_RANGE_MSG,PSN_LEADERBOARD_FRIENDS_SCORES_MSG and PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_POSTED_MSG

Xbox GDK Additions

  • os_type now has a new "os_gdk" constant you can refer to - it's the same value internally as the existing "os_xboxseriesxs" would return, but reflects that GDK supports more device models than just Xbox Series X/S
  • Info on which model of Xbox is currently running the game can now be found by using os_get_info() and checking the new "device_type" key in the map you are returned
  • xboxone_update_recent_players(user_id, recent_user_id) is a new function to add the players with the specified ID(s) to the recent players list of the local player "user_id", which can be a submission requirement when making multiplayer games ("recent_user_id" can be either a single user ID or an array of user IDs)

Added More Functions For Searching/Manipulating Arrays

  • array_all(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_any(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Bool
  • array_copy_while(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_create_ext(size, function) → Array
  • array_filter(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_find_index(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_first(array) → Real
  • array_foreach(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Undefined
  • array_intersection(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_join(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_last(array) → Real
  • array_map(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • array_reduce(array, function, init = array[offset], offset = 0, length = infinity) → Any
  • array_union(array1, array2, ...) → Array
  • array_unique(array, output, offset = 0, length = infinity) → Array
  • All of the above functions will leave the original array(s) untouched and return you a new array of the end results of the operation; however, there are also some new …_ext() functions for if you do want to modify the original array:
  • array_filter_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_map_ext(array, function, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_unique_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • array_reverse_ext(array, offset = 0, length = infinity)
  • The return value from all of these …_ext() functions is just a real to give you the new size of the modified array
  • More on all of these can be found in the manual, along with all the other existing array functions

Added More Functions For Spine

  • skeleton_attachment_exists() can be used to check if an attachment with the given name has already been created
  • skeleton_attachment_replace() and skeleton_attachment_destroy() can now be used to modify the attachments on your skeletons
  • And the existing function skeleton_attachment_create() will now return an error if you try to reuse an attachment name without destroying it first

Added support for reading PS4 save files in a PS5 game

  • Your PS5 games can now see and read PS4 saves for the same title (note that this is not supported PS5-to-PS4)

Opera Account Settings Migration
<ul>

<ul>

<ul>

<ul>

September’s release gives you the ability to control your texture groups more precisely in the texture groups editor, so that you can manage in-game loading times and memory usage, plus adds touch support in Windows games and raises the SDK version supported on a few console platforms - so please do read the runtime release notes carefully, as you may now need to change your setup. There are also quite a few important bug-fixes and several new functions (mostly on consoles).

Changes Since 2022.9.0.63

Bugs Fixed

  • In-Game: Fix for some extensions not being able to find their functions correctly in 2022.9.0.63
  • In-Game: [Windows] Fix for some extensions which initialise graphics very early during startup (e.g., Steamworks) were not working in 2022.9.0.63

2022.9.0.63

Windows Games Now Have Multitouch Support

  • Windows now supports multitouch (just the same as UWP did in older releases)
  • Please note that this does not apply to Windows 7 - it's only supported by Windows 8.0 and newer

Windows Games Now Report DLL Load Errors More Effectively

  • Currently, most DLL load errors on Windows look something like LoadLibraryW ...\Some.dll failed with error code 126
  • This has now been extended so that the message will display the function name (so that an incompatible DLL doesn't display multiple identical errors), whether the DLL has a valid header, and whether the DLL has been built correctly for this Runner's architecture - this last one will help greatly in identifying when you are accidentally using a 32bit extension, etc.

New Options For Texture Group Management

  • You will now find the texture groups editor in the 2022.9 IDE has new controls for whether you want to split textures off into their own data files on disk during your builds, as this can be required by bigger games on some platforms which have memory caps on how much data you can have loaded at any moment (e.g., GX.games only allows 2GB)
  • You can then use these matching runtimes to load/unload these groups in-game as you require - using the new texturegroup_get_status() to query the current state

PlayStation SDK Updates And Additions

  • PS4 building now requires SDK v10.0 to be installed
  • PS5 building now requires SDK v6.0 to be installed
  • On PS4 only, added "succeeded" and "padindex" keys to the async map for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_MSG
  • On PS4 only, added a "succeeded" key to the async map generated for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_RANGE_MSG,PSN_LEADERBOARD_FRIENDS_SCORES_MSG and PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_POSTED_MSG

Xbox GDK Additions

  • os_type now has a new "os_gdk" constant you can refer to - it's the same value internally as the existing "os_xboxseriesxs" would return, but reflects that GDK supports more device models than just Xbox Series X/S
  • Info on which model of Xbox is currently running the game can now be found by using os_get_info() and checking the new "device_type" key in the map you are returned
  • xboxone_update_recent_players(user_id, recent_user_id) is a new function to add the players with the specified ID(s) to the recent players list of the local player "user_id", which can be a submission requirement when making multiplayer games ("recent_user_id" can be either a single user ID or an array of user IDs)

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • The "Opera GX" target is now called "GX.games" inside the IDE and the release notes lower down
  • The Animation Update event has been fixed to not be invoked repeatedly when calculating collision bounds, as this would cause Spine sprites to perform their animations at 2x speed
  • Fixed the fallback image not being found by the asset compiler (e.g., when you have an empty Sprite asset)

September’s release gives you the ability to control your texture groups more precisely in the texture groups editor, so that you can manage in-game loading times and memory usage, plus adds touch support in Windows games and raises the SDK version supported on a few console platforms - so please do read the runtime release notes carefully, as you may now need to change your setup. There are also quite a few important bug-fixes and several new functions (mostly on consoles).

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2022.8.1 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Windows Games Now Have Multitouch Support

  • Windows now supports multitouch (just the same as UWP did in older releases)
  • Please note that this does not apply to Windows 7 - it's only supported by Windows 8.0 and newer

Windows Games Now Report DLL Load Errors More Effectively

  • Currently, most DLL load errors on Windows look something like LoadLibraryW ...\Some.dll failed with error code 126
  • This has now been extended so that the message will display the function name (so that an incompatible DLL doesn't display multiple identical errors), whether the DLL has a valid header, and whether the DLL has been built correctly for this Runner's architecture - this last one will help greatly in identifying when you are accidentally using a 32bit extension, etc.

New Options For Texture Group Management

  • You will now find the texture groups editor in the 2022.9 IDE has new controls for whether you want to split textures off into their own data files on disk during your builds, as this can be required by bigger games on some platforms which have memory caps on how much data you can have loaded at any moment (e.g., GX.games only allows 2GB)
  • You can then use these matching runtimes to load/unload these groups in-game as you require - using the new texturegroup_get_status() to query the current state

PlayStation SDK Updates And Additions

  • PS4 building now requires SDK v10.0 to be installed
  • PS5 building now requires SDK v6.0 to be installed
  • On PS4 only, added "succeeded" and "padindex" keys to the async map for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_MSG
  • On PS4 only, added a "succeeded" key to the async map generated for PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_RANGE_MSG,PSN_LEADERBOARD_FRIENDS_SCORES_MSG and PSN_LEADERBOARD_SCORE_POSTED_MSG

Xbox GDK Additions

  • os_type now has a new "os_gdk" constant you can refer to - it's the same value internally as the existing "os_xboxseriesxs" would return, but reflects that GDK supports more device models than just Xbox Series X/S
  • Info on which model of Xbox is currently running the game can now be found by using os_get_info() and checking the new "device_type" key in the map you are returned
  • xboxone_update_recent_players(user_id, recent_user_id) is a new function to add the players with the specified ID(s) to the recent players list of the local player "user_id", which can be a submission requirement when making multiplayer games ("recent_user_id" can be either a single user ID or an array of user IDs)

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • The "Opera GX" target is now called "GX.games" inside the IDE and the release notes lower down
  • The Animation Update event has been fixed to not be invoked repeatedly when calculating collision bounds, as this would cause Spine sprites to perform their animations at 2x speed
  • Fixed the fallback image not being found by the asset compiler (e.g., when you have an empty Sprite asset)

  • Building Projects: Macro definitions which contain pre-increment operations no longer return a compile error
  • Building Projects: Fixed that some 2022.8 projects failed to build/clean due to "Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'key')" asset compiler error in GMRoom
  • Building Projects: Fixed that Supura… no longer builds in recent versions due to SWF files which worked in older GM versions now being marked as incompatible
  • In-Game: Nullish operator no longer requires whitespace either side of it in the code editor in order to function correctly in-game
  • In-Game: Spine animations no longer runs faster in their Animation Update event whilst colliding with another object [see the note higher up]
  • In-Game: [YYC] No longer creates a duplicate of all strings at startup, reducing memory usage levels throughout the lifetime of the game
  • In-Game: [YYC] Fixed a crash when referencing deactivated instances
  • In-Game: [Android YYC] Fixed a crash when accessing a variable which was initialised by an expression containing a negative number
  • In-Game: [GX.games] Games with a viewport size of specifically 640x480 will now render correctly in local runs (previously, they would only work when published to the site)
  • In-Game: [GX.games] Ogg streams are no longer appended with unwanted data

  • In-Game: [GX.games] application_get_position() no longer returns the wrong value
  • In-Game: [PS5] audio_channel_num() no longer causes a game crash
