• Windows x86 (32bit support) architecture has been removed from Game Options, so now only 64bit executables are available
• Xbox One Legacy (XDK) target has been removed entirely, as GDK has been available for a while
Project Format Changes For Tile Layers In Rooms
<ul>

• We have introduced a new, much faster method for storing tile data in your rooms and passing this information into your builds - which fixes a long-time issue where rooms with lots of tile slots could see a pause on the line "Found Project Format 2" in their output log

• However, this new format is not compatible with older IDEs/runtimes and so accordingly we have introduced a new safeguard in this version, should you attempt to open a project in an older IDE again.
• On opening the project in any version newer than 2022.6 GameMaker will raise the project version automatically to be 1.6

• The next time a room containing a tile layer is edited in the newer IDE, this will potentially upgrade all the tile data and save it in a "TileCompressedData" variable in the room’s own .yyp file - at this point, this project cannot be loaded into previous IDEs as it won’t understand it. (The project would also lack all the tiles information if you used a current IDE but with a runtime from 2022.6 or older.)

• Please note if the room wouldn't benefit from the compression, GameMaker will continue to store the data in the old-style "TileSerialiseData" variable - this is the same format as before and previous IDEs can open it if you need to; however, you will need to follow the steps in our FAQ for opening “too new” projects in older IDEs

<ul>
• New functions and a rollback event have been added for providing chat functionality to your players
• New Visual nodes have been added for the above, plus some others which were missing from earlier Betas - and Toolbox icons have been fixed for the existing rollback nodes
Additional Feather Functionality
<ul>
• Naming Rules now have a new value of "Unconstrained", which you can set to tell Feather to allow any naming convention when dealing with certain aspects of your code

Changes Since Monthly Runtimes 2022.6.0.23

Lots Of Audio Fixes

  • audio_play_sound...() now has new optional arguments for "gain", "offset", "pitch" and "listener_mask" - which means these values will reliably take effect immediately when the sound plays
  • These values are also remembered and reused each time the instance is played again or resumed after pausing
  • HTML5 now records audio at the same sample rate as other platforms, so you no longer need to code for different-sized buffer lengths if using this target
  • Fixed cases of audio “crackling” or “popping” on Opera GX

August Betas feature a lot of clean-up as we head towards an LTS release later in the year - some old or underused platforms have now been removed, new audio functions/arguments have been added so you can control playback more easily, more platforms now support virtual keys, Ubuntu 22 LTS is now much better supported when building your projects, and we have made a big improvement to tile-encoding in rooms which requires the use of these newer runtimes as well as the matching IDE (so please do read the IDE release notes carefully also).

See below for runtime changes/fixes since Beta Runtimes 2022.600.0.133 and then check the IDE Release Notes

Lots Of Audio Fixes

  • audio_play_sound...() now has new optional arguments for "gain", "offset", "pitch" and "listener_mask" - which means these values will reliably take effect immediately when the sound plays
  • These values are also remembered and reused each time the instance is played again or resumed after pausing
  • HTML5 now records audio at the same sample rate as other platforms, so you no longer need to code for different-sized buffer lengths if using this target
  • Fixed cases of audio “crackling” or “popping” on Opera GX
  • Several other audio functions have received fixes also, so please see the bugs list below for more info

Support For Clipboard Functionality On More Targets

  • Added support for macOS and iOS - note that tvOS itself does not have any clipboard

Support For Virtual Keys In Browser-Based Targets

  • Added support for virtual keys in the Opera GX and HTML5 targets

Additional Extension Options Functionality

  • Added support for native-language Android/iOS extensions to access your extension options values, as set in the IDE

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: Switch builds again contain the IDE version number in their metadata, fixes a potential submission fail
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Embedding games in another page no longer causes mouse_y values to be offset by the scroll amount of the parent page, so if you had code in your website to work around this it is no longer needed

Feather Now Available
<ul>
• Feather is now available to all users to use and give feedback about - however, for the next while it will default to being OFF in Preferences
• If you want to use Feather, please enable it in your Preferences

• Also fixed a number of Syntax Errors issues which have been in Betas since Feather was introduced - so now if you do turn Feather off, the “old” errors are more reliable and the dialog populates itself automatically whenever you open it
Additions To Feather
<ul>
• Feather now supports basic type narrowing using "object_index", "typeof", "instanceof", and the built-in "is_" functions. E.g. if (is_string(a) && typeof(b) == "number")
• Changed Feather's tooltips to combine different tooltips into the one, so overlapping tooltips no longer occur for autocomplete, JSDoc content, and rules
• Also changed Feather's tooltips to limit the number of struct fields if there are too many to show at once (and added a Preference for saying how many is "too many" for you)
• Implemented that autocomplete highlights/prioritises in-scope variables at the top of the suggestion list
• Fixed some performance issues also - in particular, significant improvements to "Analysing Project..." times when opening projects
• The following types have been renamed: “Resource” is now “Asset”, “Mixed” is now “Any”, and “ArgumentIdentity” is now “Any*”. Element Types are also now shown inside trailing angle brackets
• Please see the full changelist lower down, as there are a lot more to be aware of!
More Room Editor Filter Layer Types
<ul>
• Boxes - Creates a tiled boxes effect with optional animation
• Colour Balance - Allows you to balance the highlights, midtones and shadows of the game
• RGB Noise - Displays coloured noise with optional animation
• Vignette - Displays a vignette around your game, with the ability to change the texture displayed on the Vignette
• Zoom Blur - Displays a zooming motion blur filter
• You can find more information on all of these, plus a little example of what each one looks like in-game, on the manual page “FX Types & Parameters”
Additional Control For Extensions
<ul>
• Added a new system called Extension Options, which allows you to declare new fields in a dedicated new “Options” window in the Extension Editor
• These new fields then appear to everyone using your extension on the main window of the Extension Editor, so they can be filled in very much like Instance Variables in the Object Editor
• In this way, people using your extension can set their in-game values inside the Extension Editor and their values are then saved per-Configuration, etc., by GameMaker
• Added the ability to exclude extension functions from appearing in the Code Editor auto-complete pop-up
• [Android] Implemented the ability to inject into gradle.properties
• And all code injection values are now saved independently per-Configuration also
Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
<ul>
• M1 Mac IDEs will now use native ARM runtime binaries when building projects for all the targets

• Opera GX's Game Options have been modified to make selecting which game is to be updated much easier, as GameMaker will now automatically retrieve information from the GX website - however, if you have previously uploaded any games, then you will likely need to check these values are set correctly in those projects before attempting to do your next builds, otherwise you might get a “Bad Data” error when uploading

• Android YYC - The runner is now built using NDK 24, so we would recommend that you use this NDK version for all builds (NDK 24 is supported by earlier GM releases and indeed is already our recommended NDK on the setup FAQ, so you may be using this anyway)
• PS5 SDK support updated to version 5.00 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
• PS4 SDK support updated to version 9.50 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
• Xbox GDK support updated to the "March 2022" version - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
• Switch SDK support updated to version 14.3.0 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match

• The Dark and Light skins have been changed so they use a new, cleaner system - if you find you have issues when using a custom skin please try the default ones and confirm if you now need to update yours

• Building Projects: Importing a new Spine image no longer causes the next compile to get stuck
• Building Projects: [Windows] Non-ASCII named projects no longer result in an NSIS script error "aborting creation process" during Create Exe
• Building Projects: [HTML5] If GM opened the browser, the Stop button or starting a new run no longer kills the browser process if you have subsequently opened other tabs or closed the game tab

June Runtimes include a large number of bug fixes (particularly for collisions) and also introduce several new functions for controlling your extensions and time sources; add microphone functionality on Opera GX; and change crash-reporting on Switch to use Nintendo’s own system.

Be aware that this release updates the SDK versions you will need for a number of platforms - almost all consoles require newer versions now and also you might need to update your NDK for Android YYC - so please do see the Required SDKs FAQ for further information.

Please also review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Ability To Detect An Extension Exists

  • extension_exists() has been added, so you can now query if an extension is available in-game before acting accordingly
  • This will return a real to say whether the extension is currently loaded at that point in the game - so if it’s an empty extension or if its been selected in the IDE to not load on the current target platform, this will return false

Changes For Nintendo Switch

  • Implemented Nintendo's native crash-reporting system - now in-game errors will trigger the console’s own error system, rather than GM’s own, and so will also create a crash dump which can be submitted for your analysis
  • Be aware that the above may require changes to your metadata next time you submit
  • Also implemented new functions to create blocking/non-blocking network requests as required

Microphone Support On Opera GX

  • Added a new capture device for use by the runner, so now the microphone/recording functions which have worked on other targets for a long time now work on Opera GX also
  • Note that the microphone count will always be 1, as this is all the browser allows
  • Please see the manual for more specifics on the recording functions

Time Source Functions Updated

  • Added a new time_source_resume(), which differs from the existing time_source_start() as this new one will not restart any already-finished time sources
  • Added a new optional argument to time_source_destroy() to say whether to destroy all chained timers at the same time or not

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Changed new collisions to only consider overlapping bound boxes that cover a pixel centre as a collision, which gives better compatibility between precise and non-precise collisions when using the new system
  • On HTML5 specifically the new collision system was not being used in the last couple of releases (so precise collisions could give different results to Windows, etc.), but it is being used now
  • In-Game: [Android] Now sets 60hz mode on startup to avoid display issues on devices which support refresh rates greater than 60
  • M1 Mac IDEs will now use native ARM runtime binaries when building projects for all the targets
  • Android YYC - The runner is now built using NDK 24, so we would recommend that you use this NDK version for all builds (NDK 24 is supported by earlier GM releases and indeed is already our recommended NDK on the setup FAQ, so you may be using this anyway)
  • PS5 SDK support updated to version 5.00 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
  • PS4 SDK support updated to version 9.50 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
  • Xbox GDK support updated to the "March 2022" version - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match
  • Switch SDK support updated to version 14.3.0 - you will need to change your SDK installation and GameMaker Preferences to match

June Runtime Betas include a large number of bug fixes and also introduce microphone functionality on Opera GX and a different crash-reporting system on Switch.

More features will be coming in future Betas.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes since runtime 110

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Xbox GDK support updated to the "March 2022" version - you will need to change your SDK installation to match
  • Switch SDK support updated to version 14.3.0 - you will need to change your SDK installation to match
  • Fixed issues with collisions for all objects, regardless of if they are marked as "Managed" or not, so you no longer need to edit any .yy files to remove the key

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: [Xbox XDK YYC] Fixed an issue with the AppxManifest.xml file which could cause builds to fail when setting up title memory
  • Building Projects: [Xbox GDK] Fixed an issue with shaders not building correctly in recent Betas
  • In-Game: draw_text() and most variants do not correctly apply halign/valign values on all targets except HTML5

Runtime 110

Ability To Detect An Extension Exists

  • extension_exists() has been added, so you can now query if an extension is available in-game before acting accordingly
  • This will return a real to say whether the extension was found

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • M1 Mac IDEs will now use the ARM runtime binaries again - please do let us know asap if you have issues building projects in the Mac IDE and you did not have this issue in the previous Beta!
  • Fixed issues with collisions for any objects you had created in the previous Beta IDE

Other Bugs Fixed

  • In-Game: [HTML5] Framerate can drop significantly on iOS devices while waiting for the audio context
  • In-Game: [PS4] Fix for split-screen rendering not using the correct x/y offsets for each view
  • In-Game: collision_rectangle() and collision_line() no longer detect collisions in 600 Betas
  • In-Game: draw_text() and most variants do not correctly apply halign/valign values on all targets except HTML5
  • In-Game: image_speed with a negative number does not trigger Animation End Event in 600 Betas
  • In-Game: mouse_x/y values incorrect if game is ran fullscreen on a secondary monitor using a different resolution to the primary monitor

Runtime 105

Time Source Update

  • time_source_resume() - differs from existing time_source_start() as this new one will not restart finished time sources

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Changed new collisions to only consider overlapping bound boxes that cover a pixel centre as collisions - gives better compatibility between precise and non-precise collisions when using new collision system

  • PS5 SDK support updated to version 5.00 - you will need to change your SDK installation to match
  • PS4 SDK support updated to version 9.50 - you will need to change your SDK installation to match

  • Building Projects: Cannot find metadata for object of type: Keyframe going to assume it's Keyframe`1

  • In-Game: gesture_double_tap_time off by a factor of 10

Changes Since 2022.5.1.14
<ul>
• There are no IDE changes in this release - it's simply to release the Mac permissions fix mentioned on the new runtime's release notes
Changes Since 2022.5.0.8
<ul>
• Code Editor: Highlight showing warning/error line is always an incorrect bright red colour

• Syntax Errors: Results do not open the error location when double-clicked (in most cases)
.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline
<ul>
• We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make GameMaker installers and also the runtimes you use (more on the runtimes a bit further down...)

• This involves the use of .NET 6 to build the installer and IDE, meaning we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android

• We have also moved to a new build system in order to get even more rapid turnaround on our new versions and confirming bug fixes, etc., also to support the future LTS versions talked about on our recent 2022 update video

• NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”
"Windblown Particle" Effect Layer Type
<ul>

• As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
• Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list

• Note that as it says in the Effect dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release
Alternate DNS Server Support When Checking The Runtimes Feed
<ul>
• Some users have had issues for a while where for whatever reason their system DNS would either not give them the runtime feed properly or it might use a cached copy for a lot longer than expected
• If this applies to you, then you can now set an alternative DNS server IP address in Preferences > Runtime Feeds and this will then be used instead of your system's default
• You can then go onto the “Master” feed’s own page and click the refresh button to hopefully see the list update immediately
Sound Inspector Support
<ul>
• Allows you to set all the values in the usual editor, plus introduces the ability to see the waveform of your sound (so now you can spot unwanted silence in your sounds, etc.)
Additions For Go To (Ctrl+T)
<ul>
• Added a new option to search all of Preferences, but ignoring all Redefine Keys matches, so that the matches you are shown are only the ones you wanted

<ul>
• For more information on getting the Beta version and trying out Feather, etc., please see our guide to GM Beta releases

• "Find All References" is now added via F3 when you have your cursor on a word in the Code Editor - you can step through matches by pressing F3 again or there is a little window in the top-right of the workspace to further control this and show the number of matches (Shift+F3 will also list all matches in the Output Window)
• "// feather" directive controls can now disable GM1100 errors and also allow you to apply the directive to a whole folder of scripts

Welcome to the new May 2022.5 release! We hope you find it worth the wait since March. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since 2022.5.1.11

  • Fix a permissions issue which meant Mac IDE users would see unwanted "Unable to obtain permission to execute" messages when building for several targets (for example: iOS, HTML5, macOS YYC)

Changes Since 2022.5.0.8

  • Building Projects: [GDK] Asset Compiler licensing check can cause unexpected "Unable to obtain permission to execute" message
  • Building Projects: [PS5 YYC] Unable to build in 5.0.8 due to linker error
  • In-Game: Playing a sound asset which shares part of its name with another sound asset may play the incorrect asset

2022.5.0.8

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source
  • Note that chained time sources tick all sources before any are actually processed, which is a big difference versus chained alarms (Alarms will continue to fire each alarm as they are encountered, like they have always done, as it could break a lot of games if we changed this long-time behaviour)

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Changed Audio Output For Opera GX Target

  • Opera GX now uses the same audio output system used on most other native platforms, so you should find better performance
  • Let us know if you do have any major issues - but be aware by default it uses quite small buffers, so please do file a bug with a small sample project attached if you hear "crackling" in your sounds
  • This affects all sound playback, including video support

Support for the new "Windblown Particle" Effect Layer type

  • As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
  • Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list
  • Note that as it says in that dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release

Added Clipboard Functionality Support Into HTML5 And OperaGX Targets

  • Both of these platforms now support the clipboard_has_text() and clipboard_get_text() functions
  • However, it is worth noting that Firefox does not allow pages to access the clipboard via JavaScript, so that browser will not work by default (you need to install browser extensions), and IE is too old to support the standard used and will not work at all

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

<ul>
• We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make GameMaker installers and also the runtimes you use (more on the runtimes a bit further down...)

• This involves the use of .NET 6 to build the installer and IDE, meaning we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android

• We have also moved to a new build system in order to get even more rapid turnaround on our new versions and confirming bug fixes, etc., also to support the future LTS versions talked about on our recent 2022 update video

• NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”

Alternate DNS Server Support When Checking The Runtimes Feed
<ul>
• Some users have had issues for a while where for whatever reason their system DNS would either not give them the runtime feed properly or it might use a cached copy for a lot longer than expected
• If this applies to you, then you can now set an alternative DNS server IP address in Preferences > Runtime Feeds and this will then be used instead of your system's default
• You can then go onto the “Master” feed’s own page and click the refresh button to hopefully see the list update immediately
Sound Inspector Support
<ul>
• Allows you to set all the values in the usual editor, plus introduces the ability to see the waveform of your sound (so now you can spot unwanted silence in your sounds, etc.)

<ul>

Welcome to the new May 2022.5 release! We hope you find it worth the wait since March. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since 2022.5.0.8

  • Building Projects: [GDK] Asset Compiler licensing check can cause unexpected "Unable to obtain permission to execute" message
  • Building Projects: [PS5 YYC] Unable to build in 5.0.8 due to linker error
  • In-Game: Playing a sound asset which shares part of its name with another sound asset may play the incorrect asset

2022.5.0.8

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source
  • Note that chained time sources tick all sources before any are actually processed, which is a big difference versus chained alarms (Alarms will continue to fire each alarm as they are encountered, like they have always done, as it could break a lot of games if we changed this long-time behaviour)

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Changed Audio Output For Opera GX Target

  • Opera GX now uses the same audio output system used on most other native platforms, so you should find better performance
  • Let us know if you do have any major issues - but be aware by default it uses quite small buffers, so please do file a bug with a small sample project attached if you hear "crackling" in your sounds
  • This affects all sound playback, including video support

Support for the new "Windblown Particle" Effect Layer type

  • As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
  • Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list
  • Note that as it says in that dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release

Added Clipboard Functionality Support Into HTML5 And OperaGX Targets

  • Both of these platforms now support the clipboard_has_text() and clipboard_get_text() functions
  • However, it is worth noting that Firefox does not allow pages to access the clipboard via JavaScript, so that browser will not work by default (you need to install browser extensions), and IE is too old to support the standard used and will not work at all

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

<ul>

• If this applies to you, then you can now set an alternative DNS server IP address in Preferences > Runtime Feeds and this will then be used instead of your system's default
• You can then go onto the “Master” feed’s own page and click the refresh button to hopefully see the list update immediately

Welcome to the new May 2022.5 release! We hope you find it worth the wait since March. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source
  • Note that chained time sources tick all sources before any are actually processed, which is a big difference versus chained alarms (Alarms will continue to fire each alarm as they are encountered, like they have always done, as it could break a lot of games if we changed this long-time behaviour)

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Changed Audio Output For Opera GX Target

  • Opera GX now uses the same audio output system used on most other native platforms, so you should find better performance
  • Let us know if you do have any major issues - but be aware by default it uses quite small buffers, so please do file a bug with a small sample project attached if you hear "crackling" in your sounds
  • This affects all sound playback, including video support

Support for the new "Windblown Particle" Effect Layer type

  • As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
  • Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list
  • Note that as it says in that dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release

Added Clipboard Functionality Support Into HTML5 And OperaGX Targets

  • Both of these platforms now support the clipboard_has_text() and clipboard_get_text() functions
  • However, it is worth noting that Firefox does not allow pages to access the clipboard via JavaScript, so that browser will not work by default (you need to install browser extensions), and IE is too old to support the standard used and will not work at all

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline
<ul>
• We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make GameMaker installers and also the runtimes you use (more on the runtimes a bit further down...)

• This involves the use of .NET 6 to build the installer and IDE, meaning we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android

• We have also moved to a new build system in order to get even more rapid turnaround on our new versions and confirming bug fixes, etc., also to support the future LTS versions talked about on our recent 2022 update video

• NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”
"Windblown Particle" Effect Layer Type
<ul>

• As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
• Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list

• Note that as it says in the Effect dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release
Alternate DNS Server Support When Checking The Runtimes Feed
<ul>
• Some users have had issues for a while where for whatever reason their system DNS would either not give them the runtime feed properly or it might use a cached copy for a lot longer than expected
• If this applies to you, then you can now set an alternative DNS server IP address in Preferences > Runtime Feeds and this will then be used instead of your system's default
• You can then go onto the “Master” feed’s own page and click the refresh button to hopefully see the list update immediately
Sound Inspector Support
<ul>
• Allows you to set all the values in the usual editor, plus introduces the ability to see the waveform of your sound (so now you can spot unwanted silence in your sounds, etc.)
Additions For Go To (Ctrl+T)
<ul>
• Added a new option to search all of Preferences, but ignoring all Redefine Keys matches, so that the matches you are shown are only the ones you wanted
Added New Feather Functionality In The Beta Releases
<ul>
• For more information on getting the Beta version and trying out Feather, etc., please see our guide to GM Beta releases

• "Find All References" is now added via F3 when you have your cursor on a word in the Code Editor - you can step through matches by pressing F3 again or there is a little window in the top-right of the workspace to further control this and show the number of matches (Shift+F3 will also list all matches in the Output Window)
• "// feather" directive controls can now disable GM1100 errors and also allow you to apply the directive to a whole folder of scripts
• The “@context” scoping decoration now also has “@self” added as an alias, as some users expected this name
• Similarly “@ignore” can also now be used to achieve the same as “@disable” has done in previous releases
• There are also a large number of other bug fixes, which are listed below for informational purposes but only apply if you’re using a Beta version

Welcome to the new May 2022.5 release! We hope you find it worth the wait since March. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in this new release. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE, otherwise you will see your builds get stuck with the timer carrying on endlessly and in your ui.log you will simply be told “your runtime tools are missing or corrupt”

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source
  • Note that chained time sources tick all sources before any are actually processed, which is a big difference versus chained alarms (Alarms will continue to fire each alarm as they are encountered, like they have always done, as it could break a lot of games if we changed this long-time behaviour)

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Changed Audio Output For Opera GX Target

  • Opera GX now uses the same audio output system used on most other native platforms, so you should find better performance
  • Let us know if you do have any major issues - but be aware by default it uses quite small buffers, so please do file a bug with a small sample project attached if you hear "crackling" in your sounds
  • This affects all sound playback, including video support

Support for the new "Windblown Particle" Effect Layer type

  • As we will showcase in our forthcoming new "Windy Woods" platformer Template, you can now choose a sprite and control the settings to be used for a wind-blown rain/snow/leaves type Effect in the Room Editor
  • Add a new Filter/Effect layer into the Layers panel and then you will find the new effect type at the bottom of the drop-down list
  • Note that as it says in that dropdown list, "Effects" differ from "Filters" in that you currently cannot preview an Effect in the Room Editor and you will have to run your game to see it - although, this will be changed in a future release

Added Clipboard Functionality Support Into HTML5 And OperaGX Targets

  • Both of these platforms now support the clipboard_has_text() and clipboard_get_text() functions
  • However, it is worth noting that Firefox does not allow pages to access the clipboard via JavaScript, so that browser will not work by default (you need to install browser extensions), and IE is too old to support the standard used and will not work at all

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Obsolete in-built Push Notifications functions have been removed from the runner, which fixes issues reported when using the notifications extension, but it’s worth reviewing any old code you may have in your projects for notifications

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline
<ul>
• We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the GameMaker installers and also the runtimes you use (more on the runtimes a bit further down...)

• This involves the use of .NET 6 to build the installer and the IDEs, meaning we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android

Welcome to the new May 2022.500 runtime betas! We hope you find them worth the wait. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in these new Betas. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 58

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

Fixes/Changes to Time Sources

  • time_period_to_bpm() is now called time_seconds_to_bpm()
  • time_bpm_to_period() is now called time_bpm_to_seconds()
  • time_source_create() being passed an empty array as args parameter no longer gives an unexpected result
  • time_source_get_time_remaining() now returns 0 after the source has expired and until the source is reset manually (previously, it immediately returned the original starting value again)

Beta Runtime 25

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Chained alarms do not work as expected, as not all alarms are ticked/fired before the first is processed [Now, all alarms are ticked in order to work out which need to fire this frame and then they are processed in order - the same thing applies to Time Sources also]
  • In-Game: Obsolete in-built Push Notifications functions need to be removed from the runner [fixes issues reported when using the notifications extension, but worth reviewing any old code you may have for notifications]

Welcome to the new May 2022.500 runtime betas! We hope you find them worth the wait. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in these new Betas. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 64+

Changed Audio Output For Opera GX Target

  • Opera GX now uses the same audio output system used on most other native platforms, so you should find better performance
  • Let us know if you do have any major issues - but be aware by default it uses quite small buffers, so you might need to change your code to use larger buffers if you hear "crackling" in your sounds
  • This affects all sound playback, including video support

Added Clipboard Functionality Support Into HTML5 And OperaGX Targets)

  • Both of these platforms now support clipboard functionality, much like other targets do already

  • Building Projects: SWF images will cause project runs to fail with "Could not find or load a specific file" error
  • Building Projects: [PS4 YYC] Builds do not link properly in Beta runtime 63
  • In-Game: [Xbox GDK] Doesn't handle viewports with offset x,y coordinates
  • In-Game: "id" is now a read-only compile error in recent 500 Betas
  • In-Game: instance_create_* was not binding methods to the instance correctly

Beta Runtime 58

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

Fixes/Changes to Time Sources

  • time_period_to_bpm() is now called time_seconds_to_bpm()
  • time_bpm_to_period() is now called time_bpm_to_seconds()
  • time_source_create() being passed an empty array as args parameter no longer gives an unexpected result
  • time_source_get_time_remaining() now returns 0 after the source has expired and until the source is reset manually (previously, it immediately returned the original starting value again)

Beta Runtime 25

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Chained alarms do not work as expected, as not all alarms are ticked/fired before the first is processed [Now, all alarms are ticked in order to work out which need to fire this frame and then they are processed in order - the same thing applies to Time Sources also]
  • In-Game: Obsolete in-built Push Notifications functions need to be removed from the runner [fixes issues reported when using the notifications extension, but worth reviewing any old code you may have for notifications]

Welcome to the new May 2022.500 runtime betas! We hope you find them worth the wait. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in these new Betas. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 58

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

Fixes/Changes to Time Sources

  • time_period_to_bpm() is now called time_seconds_to_bpm()
  • time_bpm_to_period() is now called time_bpm_to_seconds()
  • time_source_create() being passed an empty array as args parameter no longer gives an unexpected result
  • time_source_get_time_remaining() now returns 0 after the source has expired and until the source is reset manually (previously, it immediately returned the original starting value again)

Beta Runtime 25

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Chained alarms do not work as expected, as not all alarms are ticked/fired before the first is processed [Now, all alarms are ticked in order to work out which need to fire this frame and then they are processed in order - the same thing applies to Time Sources also]
  • In-Game: Obsolete in-built Push Notifications functions need to be removed from the runner [fixes issues reported when using the notifications extension, but worth reviewing any old code you may have for notifications]

Welcome to the new May 2022.500 runtime betas! We hope you find them worth the wait. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

You will notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in these new Betas. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 53+

Fix/Change to Spine memory-management

  • Games which constantly reset a character's animation every frame do not allow the animation time to advance, which meant that in previous releases redundant queued animations were piling up
  • Now, if the game is trying to set an animation with a zero length mix duration (which means that no blending will occur anyway), the runner will clear all existing queued animations from the track before setting the new one, avoiding a memory build-up which eventually slowed down the game

Fixes/Changes to Time Sources

  • time_period_to_bpm() is now called time_seconds_to_bpm()
  • time_bpm_to_period() is now called time_bpm_to_seconds()
  • time_source_create() being passed an empty array as args parameter no longer gives an unexpected result
  • time_source_get_time_remaining() now returns 0 after the source has expired and until the source is reset manually (previously, it immediately returned the original starting value again)

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Project: [HTML5] Games are not loading in HTML5, white browser page with error
  • Building Projects: [macOS YYC] Fails to compile due to missing InitMultiplayerFunctions
  • In-Game: Runner description (and therefore Windows ANR messages) still uses old GMS2 branding
  • In-Game: [YYC] int64 division by zero causes runs to fail with "exited with non-zero status" message
  • In-Game: [Windows YYC] Colt C... crashes without an error message when loading a save game in 500.52 [fixed the lack of a code error message]

Beta Runtime 52

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Welcome to the new May 2022.500 runtime betas! We hope you find them worth the wait. This is a very comprehensive and exciting change to a lot of the underlying GameMaker tooling and functionality - although, if all goes to plan you perhaps won’t even notice most of our hard work.

Please note this first 500 Beta release is for Windows IDE only, but future 500 Betas will restore the macOS and Ubuntu/linux versions also.

You will also notice that the last bit of the version number is much lower than it was previously - this is correct and simply a result of the new build system.

Please review the whole of the IDE and the runtime notes carefully, as there are a lot of changes and things to be aware of in these new Betas. See below for runtime changes/fixes and then check the IDE Release Notes

.NET 6 Core Support and New Build Pipeline

  • We have changed pretty much everything on our end as to how we make the IDE and the runtimes, and in the process we have in almost all instances done away with things like the 260-character file path limit on Windows and the use of the subst tool is now pretty much limited to when building for Android
  • NOTE: As part of this massive update to all of our toolchain, you cannot use runtimes from these new versions with older IDEs / older runtimes with these newer IDEs - you must be using a current runtime with the current IDE

Time Sources

  • Time sources are like alarms which are not tied to an object. These are generic timers, of which any number can exist, and so you can now…
  • Create a time source which will expire after a given period, expressed in either seconds or game frames
  • Start, stop, pause, resume, restart and reconfigure the time source
  • Specify whether time sources should repeat, and how many times (including indefinitely)
  • Query the current status of a time source

Extensions Support New Features

  • Added the ability to embed a framework in a generated iOS app
  • Added the ability to pass GML struct keys to Extensions

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Chained alarms do not work as expected, as not all alarms are ticked/fired before the first is processed [Now, all alarms are ticked in order to work out which need to fire this frame and then they are processed in order - the same thing applies to Time Sources also]
  • In-Game: Obsolete in-built Push Notifications functions need to be removed from the runner [fixes issues reported when using the notifications extension, but worth reviewing any old code you may have for notifications]

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: [macOS] Builds lack a proper warning/error for missing provisioning profiles, can confuse failure reason
  • Building Projects: [iOS] Attempting to build a project that has a display name with an & symbol will fail
  • Building Projects: [OperaGX YYC] Does not apply Game Name to the browser tab

  • Building Projects: [Ubuntu] Unpack the AppImage before launching the game, stops issues with extensions
  • Building Projects: Attached project fails to run from Steam IDE (using the alternative launcher), just see empty cmd window
  • Garbage Collection: [YYC] Context stack error can cause crashes
  • In-Game: Memory is not always fully released when a video finishes playing

  • In-Game: [OperaGX YYC] Tank_R... returns an Uncaught RuntimeError when a bullet hits an enemy
  • In-Game: [Ubuntu] No "Code Error" window appears if a game crashes on startup - differs from Windows, etc.

Renamed “GML” And “DnD” And Added New Control Options
<ul>
• “GML” is now “GML Code” (or simply “Code”)
• “Drag and Drop” (or “DnD”) is now “GML Visual” (or just “Visual”)
• This is a naming change we've wanted to make for a while, as “Drag and Drop” has not been a great label for our visual GML coding paradigm within GameMaker
• The new names better represent to new users the difference between the code and visual editors, whilst confirming it’s always GML regardless of which interface you’re using

• We also want to help bridge the gap between the two ways of working and bring them closer together, and so the Start Page no longer asks you to make a choice of editor style before you create your project. Instead, when creating your scripts you will get a little explanation dialog and the choice between Visual or Code

• Your choice of editor style can be saved per-project, or if you already know which style you prefer and you don’t ever want to be asked about the other one you can simply set the Preference on this dialog and it won’t show again
• The values can always be modified again later either in Game Options > Main (for that project) or Preferences > Languages > GML (for all new code editors going forward)

This month’s runtime update introduces Opera GX YYC support for everyone; enables video playback functionality on almost all platforms (UWP is not being implemented); two new audio falloff models have been added: audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled; and all Ubuntu builds have changed to use Steam’s new Linux runtime tools and so you can now create a more consistent cross-distro “AppImage” package if you wish

Accordingly, OperaGX has a brand new setup guide so you can configure YYC builds and the Ubuntu guide has been updated to state the extra packages you need. Please see their guides and the Required SDKs FAQ before attempting to build for these platforms.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Support For Opera GX Builds Using YYC

  • We have added the ability for everyone to run games on Opera GX using YYC, improving the in-game performance compared to the VM output type
  • Your build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the new setup guide before attempting any builds
  • Be aware that using YYC to build your game will automatically disable subst during that build (it simply ignores whatever your Preference is currently set to), as this would otherwise cause an error with the Emscripten SDK

Added Support For Video Playback

  • You can now play video on all platforms apart from UWP and Xbox One using XDK (using GDK is fine) - you can also pause, resume, seek to a specific moment, get the duration/current position, and modify the volume, amongst other things
  • Note that before including any videos in your games you must ensure that you have valid licensing rights to distribute videos in that file/codec format!
  • Please see the manual for the full information, as there are a number of new functions and constants which have been added, plus you will now get async events for when videos start/stop playing
  • Also be aware that not all platforms render the colours of videos in the same way, so you need to check which format is correct for the current platform in-game and draw the video accordingly, otherwise your picture will probably be coloured red - again, see the manual page for video_get_format() for the full info

Changed Ubuntu Builds To Use The Steam Runtime

  • Building any non-ARM projects for the Ubuntu target now uses the Steam Runtime as part of this process
  • This removes a lot of the library/dependency issues that come from different Linux distributions and updates
  • You will be required to install the Steam SDK on your Ubuntu build machine, so please see the Required SDKs FAQ and the Ubuntu setup guide that page links to before trying to do any builds

Added Support For Ubuntu AppImage Packages

  • Further to the above Ubuntu change, we have added a new option to build AppImage packages when building for Ubuntu (you can still build a .zip also)
  • An AppImage is a distribution-agnostic means of distributing software on Linux and your Appimage will automatically contain all the libraries and binaries to run your game on the system, so players just need to run the one file you give them (akin to a macOS .app bundle package)
  • The AppImage type has become the default choice when clicking Run/Create Exe; however, ARM is not currently supported and so the runtime will fall back to old build system and a .zip
  • Your Ubuntu build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the setup guide before attempting any builds

More Audio Falloff Options

  • Two new audio falloff models have been added for use with the function audio_falloff_set_model):
  • audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled
  • These behave similarly to audio_falloff_inverse_distance_clamped and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_clamped, but have been scaled in such a way that sounds are guaranteed to fall off entirely by the maximum distance

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: [tvOS] GameCenter extension now works on tvOS [Note that you need the new version of the extension also to get the full fix]

Renamed “GML” And “DnD” And Added New Control Options
<ul>
• “GML” is now “GML Code” (or simply “Code”)
• “Drag and Drop” (or “DnD”) is now “GML Visual” (or just “Visual”)
• This is a naming change we've wanted to make for a while, as “Drag and Drop” has not been a great label for our visual GML coding paradigm within GameMaker
• The new names better represent to new users the difference between the code and visual editors, whilst confirming it’s always GML regardless of which interface you’re using

• We also want to help bridge the gap between the two ways of working and bring them closer together, and so the Start Page no longer asks you to make a choice of editor style before you create your project. Instead, when creating your scripts you will get a little explanation dialog and the choice between Visual or Code

• Your choice of editor style can be saved per-project, or if you already know which style you prefer and you don’t ever want to be asked about the other one you can simply set the Preference on this dialog and it won’t show again
• The values can always be modified again later either in Game Options > Main (for that project) or Preferences > Languages > GML (for all new code editors going forward)

This month’s runtime update introduces Opera GX YYC support for everyone; enables video playback functionality on almost all platforms (UWP is not being implemented); two new audio falloff models have been added: audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled; and all Ubuntu builds have changed to use Steam’s new Linux runtime tools and so you can now create a more consistent cross-distro “AppImage” package if you wish

Accordingly, OperaGX has a brand new setup guide so you can configure YYC builds and the Ubuntu guide has been updated to state the extra packages you need. Please see their guides and the Required SDKs FAQ before attempting to build for these platforms.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Support For Opera GX Builds Using YYC

  • We have added the ability for everyone to run games on Opera GX using YYC, improving the in-game performance compared to the VM output type
  • Your build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the new setup guide before attempting any builds
  • Be aware that using YYC to build your game will automatically disable subst during that build (it simply ignores whatever your Preference is currently set to), as this would otherwise cause an error with the Emscripten SDK

Added Support For Video Playback

  • You can now play video on all platforms apart from UWP and Xbox One using XDK (using GDK is fine) - you can also pause, resume, seek to a specific moment, get the duration/current position, and modify the volume, amongst other things
  • Note that before including any videos in your games you must ensure that you have valid licensing rights to distribute videos in that file/codec format!
  • Please see the manual for the full information, as there are a number of new functions and constants which have been added, plus you will now get async events for when videos start/stop playing
  • Also be aware that not all platforms render the colours of videos in the same way, so you need to check which format is correct for the current platform in-game and draw the video accordingly, otherwise your picture will probably be coloured red - again, see the manual page for video_get_format() for the full info

Changed Ubuntu Builds To Use The Steam Runtime

  • Building any non-ARM projects for the Ubuntu target now uses the Steam Runtime as part of this process
  • This removes a lot of the library/dependency issues that come from different Linux distributions and updates
  • You will be required to install the Steam SDK on your Ubuntu build machine, so please see the Required SDKs FAQ and the Ubuntu setup guide that page links to before trying to do any builds

Added Support For Ubuntu AppImage Packages

  • Further to the above Ubuntu change, we have added a new option to build AppImage packages when building for Ubuntu (you can still build a .zip also)
  • An AppImage is a distribution-agnostic means of distributing software on Linux and your Appimage will automatically contain all the libraries and binaries to run your game on the system, so players just need to run the one file you give them (akin to a macOS .app bundle package)
  • The AppImage type has become the default choice when clicking Run/Create Exe; however, ARM is not currently supported and so the runtime will fall back to old build system and a .zip
  • Your Ubuntu build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the setup guide before attempting any builds

More Audio Falloff Options

  • Two new audio falloff models have been added for use with the function audio_falloff_set_model):
  • audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled
  • These behave similarly to audio_falloff_inverse_distance_clamped and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_clamped, but have been scaled in such a way that sounds are guaranteed to fall off entirely by the maximum distance

    New Functions

  • video_pause() Pause the video and change the status to: video_status_paused
  • video_resume() Resume the video and change the status to: video_status_playing

  • video_get_duration() Return the duration in milliseconds of the current video
  • video_get_position() Return the current position of the video in milliseconds
  • video_get_status() return the status of the video: video_status_closed, video_status_preparing, video_status_playing or video_status_paused
  • video_get_format() return the format of the surface: video_format_rgba or video_format_yuv
  • video_is_looping() Return true if loop is enabled if not return false
  • video_get_volume() Return the current volumen from 0 - 1

    • New constants

  • video_format_rgba: 0 - If surface is RGBA
  • video_format_yuv: 1 - If surfaces are YUV
  • video_status_closed: 0 - if video never was started, was closed or ended
  • video_status_preparing: 1 - set at video_open() waiting to video_status_playing
  • video_status_playing: 2 - When video playback is running, after preparting or after resume
  • video_status_paused: 3 - if video playback was paused using video_pause()

    • Async Social Callback

  • "type","video_start" - Triggered when video start playing (when changes from preparing to playing)

Renaming 'Drag and Drop (DnD)' to 'Visual'
<ul>
This is a naming change we've wanted to make for a while. Drag and Drop has not been a great label for our visual GML coding paradigm inside GMS2.
This change is being made to better represent to new users the difference between coding and visual GML.
We want to help bridge the gap between the two ways of working and we want to bring them closer together.
This no longer forces new users to make a choice a project creation without a full understanding.
Users will no longer be asked at project creation what type of project will be made.
Instead when creating a script, they will get the choice between Visual or Code.

Video playback status and control functions and constants - these are only availble for the PS4, Android and Apple platforms currently

    New Functions

  • video_pause() Pause the video and change the status to: video_status_paused
  • video_resume() Resume the video and change the status to: video_status_playing
  • video_enable_loop( bool ) If enabled the video repeats at the end (even if you enabled the loop when video wasn't started/prepared/initialized/playing )
  • video_seek_to( milliseconds ) Move the position of the video, only works correctly when the video is paused
  • video_get_duration() Return the duration in milliseconds of the current video
  • video_get_position() Return the current position of the video in milliseconds
  • video_get_status() return the status of the video: video_status_closed, video_status_preparing, video_status_playing or video_status_paused
  • video_get_format() return the format of the surface: video_format_rgba or video_format_yuv
  • video_is_looping() Return true if loop is enabled if not return false
  • video_get_volume() Return the current volumen from 0 - 1

    • New constants

  • video_format_rgba: 0 - If surface is RGBA
  • video_format_yuv: 1 - If surfaces are YUV
  • video_status_closed: 0 - if video never was started, was closed or ended
  • video_status_preparing: 1 - set at video_open() waiting to video_status_playing
  • video_status_playing: 2 - When video playback is running, after preparting or after resume
  • video_status_paused: 3 - if video playback was paused using video_pause()

    • Async Social Callback

  • "type","video_start" - Triggered when video start playing (when changes from preparing to playing)
  • "type","video_end" - Triggered when video end (not triggered when looping)
