Changes Since 2022.2.0
<ul>
• Project Load: Added a "This project is being opened Read-Only" message for whenever the project being opened requires this protection because it's too new for the IDE you're using
• This dialog also links to a Helpdesk guide about how you can edit your project so it will open in the older version (if you actually need to stick with the old IDE for some reason)
Added Text Tracks In Sequences
<ul>

• You can now add text tracks/instances into your sequences by clicking the "T" text tool in the canvas toolbox, edit the text via the new text layer inspector (which will open automatically when creating a new text item in your sequence) and animate it via the dope sheet, then draw it in-game later on
• Note that at this time there is no ability to later override the contents of the text in-game, but this will come sometime in the future
Updated SDL2 Version To Fix Various UI/UX Issues
<ul>
• Fixed various bugs with Non-Microsoft IMEs not giving the expected results when typing in the Windows IDE (such as Baidu and others)
• If you use an IME it would be great to get your feedback on whether this version is better for you now and if any major issues still exist
Added A Toggle For If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write
<ul>
• There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games

• Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)
Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values
<ul>
• You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue

• Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than the #F0F8FF you might have expected
• Note that this format is usable any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour
New Functionality Within Xbox Builds
<ul>
• Game Options for the GDK target now has a new checkbox for enabling “Simplified User Model” functionality (defaults to off), which will then toggle the user model in your games

• Game Options labels for the Xbox stat-system names have been reworded to match Microsoft’s current naming conventions, plus the settings have been expanded to allow mixing systems (again, to match what Microsoft allowed nowadays)
• Please see the Xbox docs for more information
Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions
<ul>
• Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworks SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
• This means that your games do not always ship with Steam built-in now, regardless of whether you were using it or not
• For this reason, many of the IDE settings for enabling and configuring Steamworks are now gone, in favour of you editing these values inside the extension once it is added to your project

• The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - again, to be clear: you will require this extension in your project and to configure some of its setup values if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward
Refinement Of The IDE Translations Process
<ul>

• You should not see any negative impact from this change - however, be aware that the tools used to generate translations are being changed and also we are performing clean-up on several of the language .csv files
• This will allow the quality of the translations to improve and also for more of the product to be localised, plus for the translations to arrive more quickly after a new feature has been added
• If you do see any issues in your chosen translation, please do file a bug report for this

2022.2 introduces a new ability to create text tracks/instances and animate these within your sequences, then draw the text later in-game. It also changes a long-time GameMaker behaviour that arrays will make and edit a copy when you pass an array into a function, and so we have added an option to maintain the old way if you want. As well as these two important additions, there is the ability to send text to a secure websocket, to define colours in the code editor using CSS web standard values and for this to appear correctly in your game, and also a range of important bug fixes.

Steamworks users: Please also be aware that you now need to use our Steamworks extension from the Marketplace and include this inside your projects if you wish to publish games to Steam - the runner has been cleaned of all its old in-built functions, and so there are no longer Game Options or most Preferences for Steam setup, as this is all now configured for your project within the extension once you have added it.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since 2022.2.0

  • In-Game: [Windows] Fixed that Windows 7 users would get a MFCreateDXGISurfaceBuffer error in Runner.exe when using 2022.2.0 runtimes to build their project

2022.2.0

Added Support For Text Tracks In Sequences

  • You can now add text tracks/instances into your sequences by clicking the "T" text tool in the canvas toolbox, edit the text via the new text layer inspector (which will open automatically when creating a new text item in your sequence) and animate it via the dope sheet, then draw it in-game later on
  • Note that at this time there is no ability to later override the contents of the text in-game, but this will come sometime in the future

Added A Toggle For If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write

  • There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games
  • Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)

Added Support For "text" WebSocket messages

  • network_send_raw() now has an optional "options" parameter which can be set to "network_send_binary" or "network_send_text"
  • This will force that mode when sending messages on a WebSocket socket (Binary remains the default if the parameter is not specified)
  • Similarly, the matching async_load map has a new "message_type" field for all received WebSocket messages, which will also be set to network_send_binary or network_send_text

Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values

  • You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue
  • Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than the #F0F8FF you might have expected
  • Note that this format is usable any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour

New Functionality Within Xbox Builds

  • Game Options for the GDK target now has a new checkbox for enabling “Simplified User Model” functionality (defaults to off), which will then toggle the user model in your games
  • Game Options labels for the Xbox stat-system names have been reworded to match Microsoft’s current naming conventions, plus the settings have been expanded to allow mixing systems (again, to match what Microsoft allows nowadays)
  • xboxone_get_achievement(user, achievement) can now be called to query the progress of the chosen achievement - this one works on XDK and GDK
  • Added 120Hz support for Xbox Series X/S
  • Please see the Xbox docs for more information on all of these

Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions

  • Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworks SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
  • This means the runner now does not always ship with this functionality, regardless of whether you were using Steam in your games or not
  • For this reason, many of the IDE settings for enabling and configuring Steamworks are now gone, in favour of you editing these values inside the extension once it is added to your project
  • The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - again, to be clear: you will require this extension in your project and to configure some of its setup values if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: Splash screen images would only work in previous versions if it was a genuine .png file you supplied in Game Options (as opposed to some other format, but renamed “.png”); however, GMS2 will now detect a mismatch and convert incorrect file types
  • In-Game: Precise collisions on instances with bounds extending beyond their image size now return a hit when overlapping just the bbox [note that compatibility mode is deliberately unchanged and so "still has this bug"]
  • In-Game: HTML5's json_encode() will now write out bools values as bools rather than as the strings "true" and "false" (with the quotes) - this is so it can be read easily by Windows' json_decode(), but you may need to revise your own code here if you were expecting a string
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Instances created in-game now have the same draw order as Windows, etc.
  • In-Game: Added interpolation across audio_queue_sound() buffer boundaries, which avoids "ticks" when one sound stops and the next begins

Added Text Tracks In Sequences
<ul>

• You can now add text tracks/instances into your sequences by clicking the "T" text tool in the canvas toolbox, edit the text via the new text layer inspector (which will open automatically when creating a new text item in your sequence) and animate it via the dope sheet, then draw it in-game later on
• Note that at this time there is no ability to later override the contents of the text in-game, but this will come sometime in the future

<ul>
• Fixed various bugs with Non-Microsoft IMEs not giving the expected results when typing in the Windows IDE (such as Baidu and others)

Added A Toggle For If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write
<ul>
• There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games

• Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)
Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values
<ul>
• You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue

• Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than the #F0F8FF you might have expected
• Note that this format is usable any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour
New Functionality Within Xbox Builds
<ul>
• Game Options for the GDK target now has a new checkbox for enabling “Simplified User Model” functionality (defaults to off), which will then toggle the user model in your games

• Game Options labels for the Xbox stat-system names have been reworded to match Microsoft’s current naming conventions, plus the settings have been expanded to allow mixing systems (again, to match what Microsoft allowed nowadays)
• Please see the Xbox docs for more information
Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions
<ul>
• Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworks SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
• This means that your games do not always ship with Steam built-in now, regardless of whether you were using it or not
• For this reason, many of the IDE settings for enabling and configuring Steamworks are now gone, in favour of you editing these values inside the extension once it is added to your project

• The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - again, to be clear: you will require this extension in your project and to configure some of its setup values if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward
Refinement Of The IDE Translations Process
<ul>

• You should not see any negative impact from this change - however, be aware that the tools used to generate translations are being changed and also we are performing clean-up on several of the language .csv files
• This will allow the quality of the translations to improve and also for more of the product to be localised, plus for the translations to arrive more quickly after a new feature has been added
• If you do see any issues in your chosen translation, please do file a bug report for this

2022.2 introduces a new ability to create text tracks/instances and animate these within your sequences, then draw the text later in-game. It also changes a long-time GameMaker behaviour that arrays will make and edit a copy when you pass an array into a function, and so we have added an option to maintain the old way if you want. As well as these two important additions, there is the ability to send text to a secure websocket, to define colours in the code editor using CSS web standard values and for this to appear correctly in your game, and also a range of important bug fixes.

Steamworks users: Please also be aware that you now need to use our Steamworks extension from the Marketplace and include this inside your projects if you wish to publish games to Steam - the runner has been cleaned of all its old in-built functions, and so there are no longer Game Options or most Preferences for Steam setup, as this is all now configured for your project within the extension once you have added it.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Support For Text Tracks In Sequences

  • You can now add text tracks/instances into your sequences by clicking the "T" text tool in the canvas toolbox, edit the text via the new text layer inspector (which will open automatically when creating a new text item in your sequence) and animate it via the dope sheet, then draw it in-game later on
  • Note that at this time there is no ability to later override the contents of the text in-game, but this will come sometime in the future

Added A Toggle For If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write

  • There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games
  • Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)

Added Support For "text" WebSocket messages

  • network_send_raw() now has an optional "options" parameter which can be set to "network_send_binary" or "network_send_text"
  • This will force that mode when sending messages on a WebSocket socket (Binary remains the default if the parameter is not specified)
  • Similarly, the matching async_load map has a new "message_type" field for all received WebSocket messages, which will also be set to network_send_binary or network_send_text

Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values

  • You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue
  • Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than the #F0F8FF you might have expected
  • Note that this format is usable any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour

New Functionality Within Xbox Builds

  • Game Options for the GDK target now has a new checkbox for enabling “Simplified User Model” functionality (defaults to off), which will then toggle the user model in your games
  • Game Options labels for the Xbox stat-system names have been reworded to match Microsoft’s current naming conventions, plus the settings have been expanded to allow mixing systems (again, to match what Microsoft allows nowadays)
  • xboxone_get_achievement(user, achievement) can now be called to query the progress of the chosen achievement - this one works on XDK and GDK
  • Added 120Hz support for Xbox Series X/S
  • Please see the Xbox docs for more information on all of these

Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions

  • Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworks SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
  • This means the runner now does not always ship with this functionality, regardless of whether you were using Steam in your games or not
  • For this reason, many of the IDE settings for enabling and configuring Steamworks are now gone, in favour of you editing these values inside the extension once it is added to your project
  • The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - again, to be clear: you will require this extension in your project and to configure some of its setup values if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: Splash screen images would only work in previous versions if it was a genuine .png file you supplied in Game Options (as opposed to some other format, but renamed “.png”); however, GMS2 will now detect a mismatch and convert incorrect file types
  • In-Game: Precise collisions on instances with bounds extending beyond their image size now return a hit when overlapping just the bbox [note that compatibility mode is deliberately unchanged and so "still has this bug"]
  • In-Game: HTML5's json_encode() will now write out bools values as bools rather than as the strings "true" and "false" (with the quotes) - this is so it can be read easily by Windows' json_decode(), but you may need to revise your own code here if you were expecting a string
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Instances created in-game now have the same draw order as Windows, etc.
  • In-Game: Added interpolation across audio_queue_sound() buffer boundaries, which avoids "ticks" when one sound stops and the next begins

  • Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than #F0F8FF
  • Note that this format can be used any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour

Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions

  • Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworkd SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
  • This means the runner now does not always ship with this functionality, even if you're not using Steam in your games
  • The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - be aware that you will require this if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Windows 7 does not support secure websockets, causes games built with 2022.1.0 to crash on startup

Beta Runtime 446

Added Support For Toggling If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write

  • There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games
  • Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)

Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values

  • You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue
  • Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than #F0F8FF
  • Note that this format can be used any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour

Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions

  • Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworkd SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
  • This means the runner now does not always ship with this functionality, even if you're not using Steam in your games
  • The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - be aware that you will require this if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward

The 2022.1 runtime changes the format of all images in-game to lower build times and package sizes, adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, fixes a performance issue building large projects on the Mac IDE and enables simulator use on an M1-equipped Mac, as well as raising the version of Gradle used during Android builds and introducing support for the newest SDK/NDK versions.

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs. You should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix; however, there is also a new compatibility mode in Game Options for if your existing projects need to maintain the old way. More information on this change can be found on its page in the manual.

As well as all of the above, this version includes new functions to apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer and to toggle this effect on/off at runtime, and enables fx_create() to dynamically add your chosen filters into your game builds without you having to create a matching layer in your room first. The new runtimes also remove more stale code for old extensions/features no longer supported and accordingly trims down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7

Be aware that this release ends support for our Remote Worker tool and so this is not part of the IDE installer any more. Going forward, please just use the Windows and Mac IDEs directly on your machines.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

  • Note: Windows 7 itself does not support secure websockets, so whilst the fix above allows all games to start up again, you will always need to confirm in your code that your player is not using Win 7 before attempting to connect to a secure socket, as this would not work (and you will get a line in your log saying it was blocked)

2022.1.0

Changed Bounding Box Values To Be Floats And Added A Compatibility Collisions Mode

  • There is quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs (see below for some of the bugs fixed), but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.
  • See the manual page for this change for more information
  • However, for existing projects where you do not wish to make the change or it’s not practical to refactor, there is a new Game Option (so you need to enable this in the IDE to get the fix) which tells the runner to treat bounding boxes as inclusive and round() them to .000 so they act as if integers, which is how collisions worked in previous GMS2 releases
  • Note that we would recommend going forward that you use the newer float bounding box calculations system and generate your sprites and code accordingly, rather than always ticking this option in new projects

Changed In-Game Sprites To Use QOI Image Format

  • Games now use the QOI image format with BZ2 compression, which is smaller than PNG (we saw in our testing that game packages are now around 80% of the size they would be in 2.3.7) and quicker to decompress
  • You should also see your project build times are quite a bit shorter in this release (again, we saw potentially around 50% quicker, but quite how much depends on the size of your project and the number of sprites, obviously)
  • If for some reason your game now fails to build or takes noticeably longer than 2.3.7 requires, please let us know via a bug report ticket and remember to attach a download of your project so we can check why it has an issue

Updated the version of Gradle that Android builds will use

  • Should offer better support for some extensions (particularly for those writing new extensions themselves), but we have also added support for a compatibility mode with older versions of Gradle/Java also
  • Please note that Gradle installs its own updates and this change may require a download during your first/next Android build - ensure you have internet access if your compiler log says Gradle needs this
  • Our current Marketplace assets do not require this change and so are not being updated at this time, but eventually some may require it in future

Added Functions For Toggling Filters In-Game

  • Added new functions to enable\disable the existing fx values on layers (without having to remove the filter from the layers) and also to toggle whether a filter on that layer applies to only the one layer or to all below it also - these functions are:
  • layer_enable_fx(layer_name_or_id, bool) enables\disables the filter on the specified layer
  • layer_fx_is_enabled(layer_name_or_id) returns whether any filter is enabled on the specified layer
  • fx_set_single_layer("filterName", true/false) controls whether that filter affect just this one layer (true) or all underneath it (false)
  • fx_get_single_layer("filterName") returns the value of the above function again later on

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Changed The Application Oven To Also Support M1 Architecture

  • You shouldn't see any difference when building projects, etc., but this means the app with now run natively on these Macs

Added support for targeting iOS and tvOS simulators on M1 CPU Macs

  • Updated the Xcode project to allow VM and YYC builds to run on simulators launched on an M1 architecture Mac
  • (Intel Macs worked fine already)

Removed the Remote Worker

  • Whilst there are a small number of worker users and so we appreciate this might affect your workflow, the usage levels are so low that continuing to ship the installer as part of the download to everyone and support the worker each release is not effective
  • Please use the regular Windows and Mac IDEs for all your platform builds now

• In order to avoid any confusion with similar build numbers between beta and stable releases, Betas will call themselves release "100" of that year - if you took part in January's Betas, you would have seen this version became 2022.100.0.buildnumber
Licensing Change To Reduce Your Session Count When Using Multiple Installs
<ul>
• Sessions are now simply "one for the host machine" instead of "one per-IDE install on that machine"

• This means if you're using (for example) a Stable and a Beta install or Steam and non-Steam installs on a single physical machine, then this will only create one session going forward, rather than multiple as GMS2 has done to this point
• Note: This change will invalidate your current IDE session and so you will need to log in again one time, the next time you start GMS2
• You may also need to revoke your old sessions on your account's web panel one time if you receive errors about having too many sessions active
More Robust Runtime Download And Activation Processes
<ul>
• As well as fixing some RSS downloading crashes, we have added multiple fixes for when for some reason your runtime download has not been set as active
• If feed errors occur, GMS2 will still look for the matching runtime in your download folder, but will now more reliably activate it and allow the IDE to start up correctly

• Additionally, as of this release, if you do not have the correct matching runtime in your install, but you do have an older one, then GMS2 will activate that one just so it can start up safely (and then prompt you to update)
Changes To Build Tools So In-Game Sprites Now Use QOI Image Format
<ul>

• See the runtime notes for more information, but games now use a modified version of the QOI image format with BZ2 compression, which is smaller than PNG (we saw in our testing that game packages are now around 80% of the size they would be in 2.3.7) and quicker to decompress

• You should also see your project build times are quite a bit shorter in this release (again, we saw potentially around 50% quicker, but quite how much depends on the size of your project and the number of sprites, obviously)

• If for some reason your game now fails to build or takes noticeably longer than 2.3.7 requires, please let us know via a bug report ticket and remember to attach a download of your project so we can check why it has an issue
Added the Room Layer Inspector
<ul>
• When in the Room Editor you can now open the Inspector and make changes to the properties of your room layers
• Using this new Inspector functionality you can control whether a room layer has a single-layer effect applied to it
• Note that this is a "phase 1" implementation and so not all settings for all layer types are inspectable - more will be enabled in future releases
Added more into the Room Instance Inspector
<ul>
• Implemented support for editing Instance Variables and also Inheritance values
Added A Game Option For Compatibility Collision Calculations
<ul>

• See the runtime notes and its page in the manual for more information, but bounding boxes have changed as of this release to be floats rather than ints, so that we could fix a number of longstanding bugs with testing collisions against rotated/scaled sprites

• Accordingly, there is a new setting in Game Options > Main which tells the runner to maintain the old calculations, so that existing projects which show problems with the new collision calculations going forward can maintain the old way and not require refactoring

• Note that we would recommend going forward that you use the newer float bounding box calculations system and generate your sprites and code accordingly, rather than always ticking this option in new projects
Added Preference "Never Enable Laptop Mode"
<ul>

Added the Font Inspector
<ul>
• Implemented support for editing your fonts in the Inspector

Removed the Remote Worker
<ul>

• Please use the regular Windows and Mac IDEs for all your platform builds now

<ul>
• Should resolve a number of poor performance issues and graphics card memory crashes seen in the last couple of releases

The 2022.1 runtime changes the format of all images in-game to lower build times and package sizes, adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, fixes a performance issue building large projects on the Mac IDE and enables simulator use on an M1-equipped Mac, as well as raising the version of Gradle used during Android builds and introducing support for the newest SDK/NDK versions.

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs. You should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix; however, there is also a new compatibility mode in Game Options for if your existing projects need to maintain the old way. More information on this change can be found on its page in the manual.

As well as all of the above, this version includes new functions to apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer and to toggle this effect on/off at runtime, and enables fx_create() to dynamically add your chosen filters into your game builds without you having to create a matching layer in your room first. The new runtimes also remove more stale code for old extensions/features no longer supported and accordingly trims down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7

Be aware that this release ends support for our Remote Worker tool and so this is not part of the IDE installer any more. Going forward, please just use the Windows and Mac IDEs directly on your machines.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Changed Bounding Box Values To Be Floats And Added A Compatibility Collisions Mode

  • There is quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs (see below for some of the bugs fixed), but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.
  • See the manual page for this change for more information
  • However, for existing projects where you do not wish to make the change or it’s not practical to refactor, there is a new Game Option (so you need to enable this in the IDE to get the fix) which tells the runner to treat bounding boxes as inclusive and round() them to .000 so they act as if integers, which is how collisions worked in previous GMS2 releases
  • Note that we would recommend going forward that you use the newer float bounding box calculations system and generate your sprites and code accordingly, rather than always ticking this option in new projects

Changed In-Game Sprites To Use QOI Image Format

  • Games now use the QOI image format with BZ2 compression, which is smaller than PNG (we saw in our testing that game packages are now around 80% of the size they would be in 2.3.7) and quicker to decompress
  • You should also see your project build times are quite a bit shorter in this release (again, we saw potentially around 50% quicker, but quite how much depends on the size of your project and the number of sprites, obviously)
  • If for some reason your game now fails to build or takes noticeably longer than 2.3.7 requires, please let us know via a bug report ticket and remember to attach a download of your project so we can check why it has an issue

Updated the version of Gradle that Android builds will use

  • Should offer better support for some extensions (particularly for those writing new extensions themselves), but we have also added support for a compatibility mode with older versions of Gradle/Java also
  • Please note that Gradle installs its own updates and this change may require a download during your first/next Android build - ensure you have internet access if your compiler log says Gradle needs this
  • Our current Marketplace assets do not require this change and so are not being updated at this time, but eventually some may require it in future

Added Functions For Toggling Filters In-Game

  • Added new functions to enable\disable the existing fx values on layers (without having to remove the filter from the layers) and also to toggle whether a filter on that layer applies to only the one layer or to all below it also - these functions are:
  • layer_enable_fx(layer_name_or_id, bool) enables\disables the filter on the specified layer
  • layer_fx_is_enabled(layer_name_or_id) returns whether any filter is enabled on the specified layer
  • fx_set_single_layer("filterName", true/false) controls whether that filter affect just this one layer (true) or all underneath it (false)
  • fx_get_single_layer("filterName") returns the value of the above function again later on

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Changed The Application Oven To Also Support M1 Architecture

  • You shouldn't see any difference when building projects, etc., but this means the app with now run natively on these Macs

Added support for targeting iOS and tvOS simulators on M1 CPU Macs

  • Updated the Xcode project to allow VM and YYC builds to run on simulators launched on an M1 architecture Mac
  • (Intel Macs worked fine already)

Removed the Remote Worker

  • Whilst there are a small number of worker users and so we appreciate this might affect your workflow, the usage levels are so low that continuing to ship the installer as part of the download to everyone and support the worker each release is not effective
  • Please use the regular Windows and Mac IDEs for all your platform builds now

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • A number of old packages have now been removed from various platform runners - old social features like ads/achievements/challenges and also some push notifications packages. You should not see any change, as these things were long ago replaced with our Marketplace asset extensions, but just be aware that if you do still reference these in old projects, then you will need to remove that code now.
  • In-Game: Persistent objects now fire their Clean Up event after their Game End event when the runner is closed, like non-Persistent objects do
  • In-Game: pointer_null no longer always returns true if the string/number compared against starts with a 0 [note that pointers can only be compared successfully against other pointers - previous releases incorrectly appeared to allow comparisons with other types]
  • In-Game: pointer_null has been made "false-y", following community feedback

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer and to toggle this effect on/off at runtime, and for fx_create() to work in-game without you having to create a matching layer in your room first

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs. You should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix; however, there is also a new compatibily mode in Game Options for if your existing projects need to maintain the old way

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 433

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer and to toggle this effect on/off at runtime, and for fx_create() to work in-game without you having to create a matching layer in your room first

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs. You should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix; however, there is also a new compatibily mode in Game Options for if your existing projects need to maintain the old way

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

  • Added a new Game Option (so you need to enable this in the IDE to get the fix) which tells the runner to treat bounding boxes as inclusive and round() them to .000 so they act as if integers
  • By enabling this option, existing projects which showed problems with the new collision calculations going forward can maintain the old way and not require refactoring
  • Note that we would recommend going forward that you use the newer float bounding box calculations system and generate your sprites and code accordingly, rather than always ticking this option in new projects

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer, and for fx_create() to work in-game without you having to create a matching layer in your room first

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs, but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 433

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

Beta Runtime 417

Changed In-Game Sprites To Use QOI Image Format

  • Games now use the QOI image format with BZ2 compression, which is smaller than PNG (we saw in our testing that game packages are now around 80% of the size they would be in 2.3.7) and quicker to decompress
  • You should also see your project build times are quite a bit shorter in this release (again, we saw potentially around 50% quicker, but quite how much depends on the size of your project and the number of sprites, obviously)
  • If for some reason your game now fails to build or takes noticeably longer than 2.3.7 requires, please let us know via a bug report ticket and remember to attach a download of your project so we can check why it has an issue

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer, and for fx_create() to work in-game without you having to create a matching layer in your room first

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs, but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Beta Runtime 433

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer, and for fx_create() to work in-game without you having to create a matching layer in your room first

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs, but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since Beta Runtime 432

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

The new runtimes remove more stale code and trim down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7. This release also adds the ability to apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer.

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs, but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.

Changes Since IDE 2.3.7.403
Tweaked the Renderer's Memory-management
<ul>
• Should resolve a number of poor performance issues and graphics card memory crashes seen in the last couple of releases
• If you do still have issues, please file a bug report, but remember to attach your ui.log and a DXDiag/System Information report
Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
<ul>
• Marketplace/Local Package Integration: Packages downloaded to a Dropbox folder and imported whilst Dropbox is running will give "Failed to verify the package" error
• Note: this one is actually because Dropbox is quietly adding a .device file into your downloads - you may wish to review any files you have downloaded already
• Startup: [Mac IDE] GMS2 no longer crashes immediately when using Mojave

• Note: A few tickets suggest newer OS versions would show the same issue if you're actually using old Mac hardware which Apple do not themselves support in that OS, but you have turned off SIP and installed anyway
Other Bugs Fixed
<ul>

• Asset Browser: Creating an asset via keyboard hotkey immediately after deleting a folder in the Asset Browser now adds the new asset correctly/safely, rather than causing an error next time you open that project
• Building Projects: [YYC] A much more helpful error is now shown when builds fail because your Visual Studio install directory as set in Preferences cannot be found
• Building Projects: Fixed a likely reason for "Unable to obtain permission to execute" shown to some users who have valid licences [also added more logging for if this issue does happen again]
• General: [Ubuntu and Mac IDEs] Fixed an exception in Graphics.VertexBuffer.Destroy() when closing GMS2
• Image Editor: Undoing a resize by "Resize All Frames" now undoes both of the changes to height and width properly
• Image Editor: "Rotate brush 90 degrees" shortcut key now works again
• Inspector: "Disable IDE transition animations" Preference is now obeyed by Inspector windows also
• Preferences: [Mac IDE] Generating an Android keystore File now works on Macs with M1 CPUs

• Preferences: "Auto Logout" might fail for some Edu customers when the network connection is not correct, so have we added more logging for this - if you are affected by this issue also, then please file a bug report and attach your ui.log
• Project Save: Dragging a file onto GMS2 to add as an Included File no longer has the potential to stop all further save attempts for that project in that GMS2 session
• Room Editor: Cut/Copy/Paste Instance keyboard shortcuts are now working again
• Sprite Editor: GMS2 can now import .jpg files made by Photoshop 2021 [could have affected other editors in their new versions also, as it's due to a change in the .jpg header]
• UI/UX: Likely fixes for GMS crash in Exception in YoYoStudio.GUI.Gadgets.StackPanel,Void StackPanel_UpdateLayout() (according to logs, when copy/pasting or saving via Ctrl+S)
• Workspace Overview: You are again able to flow backwards (Shift+Tab whilst still holding Ctrl)
• Workspace Overview: Ctrl+Tab now correctly selects the last active window in the list whenever you try to select that one
Introduced Logging-in Via Opera Single Sign-on
<ul>

• You now have the choice of logging-in with your existing YoYo details or (particularly useful if you're working with the OperaGX target a lot) linking your Opera account to your YoYo Account and then using that to sign-in with

• If you do not already have an Opera account, then you can create one from the licensing dialog. Once your account is created, the Opera site will send you to your YoYo Accounts page so that you can log in there one time and link the two accounts. After that, you will be able to sign-in to GMS2 using the Opera account each time.
Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls
<ul>
• Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
• I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)
Added Two New "Nullish" Operators
<ul>

• Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable

• Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing
Added the Room Instance Inspector
<ul>
• Basic functionality of the Room Instance inspector has been added, and so you can now open this inspector from the Window menubar
• At the moment this new inspector only applies to instances in your room and does not contain full functionality (for example, you cannot edit creation code yet)
Added Several New Room Editor Filter Layer Types
<ul>
• We have now added Heat Haze, Twirl Distort, and Underwater as filter options you can choose in the Room Editor
• Note: The contents of the layer type dropdown does depend on which runtime is currently active, so you will only see these if using 2.3.7 runtimes
• There are also some visual improvements to the Desaturate and Large Blur layers (this one also gains a room editor performance fix)
Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds

2.3.7.474

Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0

  • Added support for importing and using Spine 4.0 images in your games
  • However, be aware that due to the way the Spine runtime only supports one version at a time, you will need to use Spine 4.0 to re-export all of your assets for your projects before they will work now
  • If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game

Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls

  • Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
  • I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)

Added Two New "Nullish" Operators

  • Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable
  • Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing

Implemented Android 12/API 31+ intent-filter changes

  • This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
  • Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
  • (We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions)

Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds

  • This runtime adds support for the new "Always Convert" functionality for sounds in the 2.3.7 IDE (see the IDE notes for more info)

Added Several New Filter Layer Types

  • This runtime adds support for three new Room Editor filter layer types in the 2.3.7 IDE - Heat Haze, Twirt Distort, and Underwater (see the IDE notes for more info)

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Stopped Ogg playback using existing channels that are still active, but no longer playing their previous sound and so are currently closing
  • Note: This fixes issues with sound playback using the wrong settings (e.g., the new sound looping when it's not meant to or being unable to fade it out) or with audio_get_name() failing to be able to tell what the currently-playing sound is, but you should check any audio-intensive projects carefully
  • Doing a "Create Exe" for Opera GX will now always use PNGCrush to compress all your images and reduce the submission package size

  • Made a significant optimisation for runner loading times if your project has lots of objects in it (typically >1000 before you will see real improvements) - this improvement is greater still if physics is enabled or if lots of the objects have collision events

Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0

  • If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game

Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls

  • Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
  • I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)

  • Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable
  • Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing

  • In-Game: Stopped Ogg playback using existing channels that are still active, but no longer playing their previous sound and so are currently closing
  • Note: This fixes issues with sound playback using the wrong settings (e.g., the new sound looping when it's not meant to or being unable to fade it out) or with audio_get_name() failing to be able to tell what the currently-playing sound is, but you should check any audio-intensive projects carefully
  • Doing a "Create Exe" for Opera GX will now always use PNGCrush to compress all your images and reduce the submission package size
  • Note: This will ensure your project's build cache is recreated for all images first (and does so every Create Exe), so be aware that build times will be a little longer now
  • True and False are now actual booleans (so therefore typeof(true) will return "boolean" and is_bool(true) will return 1, etc.)

• Basic functionality of the Room Instance inspector has been added, and so you can now open this inspector from the Window menubar
• At the moment this new inspector only applies to instances in your room and does not contain full functionality (for example, you cannot edit creation code yet)
Added Several New Room Editor Filter Layer Types
<ul>
• We have now added Heat Haze, Twirl Distort, and Underwater as filter options you can choose in the Room Editor
• Note: The contents of the layer type dropdown does depend on which runtime is currently active, so you will only see these if using 2.3.7 runtimes
• There are also some visual improvements to the Desaturate and Large Blur layers (this one also gains a room editor performance fix)
Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds
<ul>

• A while ago, we introduced a change where GMS2 assumes that a sound asset using an .ogg file type is already in the format you want and won't recompile the .ogg file if the Sound Editor's settings match a quick scan of contents of the .ogg

• However, it is possible that you might want an individual sound to always ensure that it is compiled by GMS2 before it is added to your project cache folder, so we have now added an option for this into the Sound Editor
• Be aware that this will force that sound to recompile each build, so you may wish to only tick this option when required
Added ability to switch off the use of kerning for a font
<ul>
• There is a new setting in the Font Editor for saying whether you wish to ignore the kerning information within the font

• Note: a reminder that different fonts may legitimately need different interpreter versions to be used in the font editor's options for that font asset, so you might want to check these options first if you have issues with a font
Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0
<ul>
• Added support for importing and using Spine 4.0 images in your games

• However, be aware that due to the way the Spine runtime only supports one version at a time, you will need to use Spine 4.0 to re-export all of your assets for your projects before they will work now
• If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game
Implemented Android 12/API 31+ intent-filter changes
<ul>

• This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
• Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
• (We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions.)

2.3.7 runtimes update a number of the SDKs GMS2 requires during builds (so please see our setup guides if you have issues building projects!) and raises Spine support to v4.0. Please be aware this Spine change will require you to re-export your Spine images using v4.0 before they will work again in GMS2.

This release also changes "true" and "false" into actual Booleans, adds support for a new "nullish" operator and several new filter layers in your rooms, as well as the ability to omit arguments from your function calls to have the game intelliegently use "undefined" for those items.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0

  • Added support for importing and using Spine 4.0 images in your games
  • However, be aware that due to the way the Spine runtime only supports one version at a time, you will need to use Spine 4.0 to re-export all of your assets for your projects before they will work now
  • If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game

Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls

  • Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
  • I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)

Added Two New "Nullish" Operators

  • Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable
  • Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing

Implemented Android 12/API 31+ intent-filter changes

  • This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
  • Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
  • (We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions)

Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds

  • This runtime adds support for the new "Always Convert" functionality for sounds in the 2.3.7 IDE (see the IDE notes for more info)

Added Several New Filter Layer Types

  • This runtime adds support for three new Room Editor filter layer types in the 2.3.7 IDE - Heat Haze, Twirt Distort, and Underwater (see the IDE notes for more info)

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Stopped Ogg playback using existing channels that are still active, but no longer playing their previous sound and so are currently closing
  • Note: This fixes issues with sound playback using the wrong settings (e.g., the new sound looping when it's not meant to or being unable to fade it out) or with audio_get_name() failing to be able to tell what the currently-playing sound is, but you should check any audio-intensive projects carefully
  • Doing a "Create Exe" for Opera GX will now always use PNGCrush to compress all your images and reduce the submission package size
  • Note: This will ensure your project's build cache is recreated for all images first (and does so every Create Exe), so be aware that build times will be a little longer now
  • True and False are now actual booleans (so therefore typeof(true) will return "boolean" and is_bool(true) will return 1, etc.)
  • Made a significant optimisation for runner loading times if your project has lots of objects in it (typically >1000 before you will see real improvements) - this improvement is greater still if physics is enabled or if lots of the objects have collision events

Changed the renderer used for the Windows IDE
<ul>
• The Windows IDE now uses Direct3D rather than the OpenGL it used in all previous releases

• You should see that this release fixes many of the rendering issues that have been reported for various editors in the last couple of GMS2 releases, plus likely an improvement to performance (especially if you had very poor performance in the last few releases)
Redesigned the Start Page
<ul>
• This version includes our new-look Start Page, complete with a quick UI tutorial aimed at new-users (for experienced users, you can skip and disable seeing it again)
• Our demo projects are now "Templates" on the new project screen, ready to be used as the basis of your own projects

• You are also now able to turn your own projects into Templates so you can reuse them as the base of new projects later on - see the new File > Export > As a Template and the matching settings in Game Options for doing this
• Note that the Home button on the menubar now closes your current project and returns you to the Start Page, ready to start working on a different project, so do be aware of this workflow change
Added support for Filters and Effects in the Room Editor
<ul>
• Indie and Enterprise users now have early access to the new "Filters and Effects" feature, which allows easily adding one of a range of graphical effect layers into your rooms
• Simply create a new Filter layer, use the dropdown to set which filter to use, and the layer then applies your chosen filter to all other layers at a lower depth
• These filters are even previewable in the Room Editor and so will automatically show you your end result (there is a new menubar option to disable Room Editor previews if you don't want this)
Added a Key Conflicts window to the Redefinable Keys menu
<ul>
• A new conflict window is now presented in the event of you trying to use the same keys for commands which would disrupt each other
• This window provides suggested alternatives and lets you easily see other uses of those keys

• If you still refer to these old-style names in your code, please change to calling the correct name now

2.3.6 brings a lot of stability fixes (particularly to the new OperaGX target introduced in 2.3.5) and fixes a number of issues with precise collisions - especially with scaled-up small sprites. It also introduces support for the Filters layer in the Room Editor. Plus, there is also a bit of clean-up of old code and variable/event names, so please do read the release notes carefully in case any of this applies to you.

See below for runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Fixed the OperaGX target so it will not attempt to load unsupported .dll extensions
  • Note: if you have a pre-2.3.5 project which uses extensions and you now want to run it on OperaGX, please check that the extension is suitable for use on the platform and that OperaGX is actually enabled in the extensions's options
  • Removed the ev_async_message_event constant used with event_perform_async(), as this event didn't fire Broadcast Message events like some users were attempting to use it for, and so caused confusion
  • Note: if you have this code in your project now, please change it to a suitable alternative event
  • Removed a lot of old, stale code relating to GM:S 1.x variables not used in GMS2 nowadays - you should not notice any changes, but please let us know if you do

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Garbage Collection: Structs are now garbage-collected properly when calling "delete" on them
  • In-Game: Fixed that scaled-up sprites using "Slow" masks give poor instance_place()/instance_place_list()/place_meeting() results and a large FPS drop since 2.3.3
  • In-Game: Fixed a crash when rapidly creating and destroying 20+ anim curves via code
  • In-Game: Fixed that playing a sound from a sequence could loop and also keep playing even after the sequence has ended
  • In-Game: Fixed an infinite loop when trying to grow a zero-sized buffer
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed some blurring of the game window when played in the browser

  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Mouse wheel now works as expected

  • In-Game: [OperaGX] url_open() now works as expected

  • In-Game: [HTML5] image_xscale = -1 now maintains the Sprite's origin, no longer becomes offset incorrectly
  • In-Game: [Android] Sprites are no longer drawn at different coordinates after minimising and reopening the game
  • In-Game: [iOS] Fixed the parsing of http response's header map when there is a 401 http_status code

Sprites Inspector
<ul>
• The Inspector has now been enabled for Sprites also, giving you the option of trying this new workflow in another editor - please do let us know how you find using it
• A reminder that the Inspector currently still has to be enabled manually from the Windows option on the menubar
Redefinable Keys Support
<ul>
• We have now added the ability for you to change GMS2's hotkey combinations for various commands throughout the IDE
• See the new Preferences > Redefine Keys section for controlling this
UX Tweak For The Create Exe Process
<ul>
• Added a new Preference to always silently stop any existing run when clicking to create an executable, and then carry on with the new build as normal
• Note this defaults to "off" (so you won't see any change) and you can enable it via Preferences > General Settings > Compiling > "Automatically stop running before packaging"
Startup Tweak For Web Server Port Check
<ul>

• Instead of checking your webserver port every startup, GMS2 will now only check this at the time you actually try to start the webserver (e.g., running a HTML5 game or opening the manual if the Preference to use the local manual is actually enabled)

• Note you would still see the dialog at these times if your port remains blocked, so you should continue to see our Permissions FAQ for more info on how to fix this, as GMS2 will not create firewall rules for you
Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
<ul>

• Asset Browser: [2.3.5] Removed the restriction on included files with names beginning with a number, as this is no longer required on current Apple OS versions [be careful claiming backwards support, though]

• Game Options: Android's product information fields no longer allow you to type in hyphens, as we have had tickets from a few users who had typed this and caused Gradle to error when building the project
• Note: If your project already has hyphens in any of these three text fields, please remove them now, as otherwise your build will fail
• Project Load: Added more logging for "completely empty ID reference" errors and also a fix to more reliably tell you the name of the asset(s) affected, so that you can fix your projects more easily
• Note: If you have a project which has this issue, please back it up first, but then do try it in this version and to attempt to fix your issue - if you are unable, send us the backup in a ticket

• Project Save: Fixed a versioning issue which meant importing a 2.3.4-format extension into 2.3.3 and then deleting the extension in the Asset Browser deletes the entire project [2.3.5 will now export files safe to use in those old IDEs]

• Code Editor: Accidentally adding double brackets when calling a function no longer gives a large parser error tooltip in the gutter
• Code Editor: Fixed user-defined shortcuts for code snippets being broken in 2.3.4
• Code Editor: [Mac IDE] Undo will no longer modify multiple lines if a mouse click was used to move the caret to a different line, rather than Enter
• Debugger: Stepping code functionality no longer navigates in some circumstances to a line that is not actually getting called
• Debugger: Fixed the Reset Layout menubar command so it actually removes your layout file and therefore resets your layout
• Image Editor: [Mac IDE] Cutting a frame no longer causes two frames to be cut
• Image Editor: [Mac IDE] Copy-pasting a frame no longer pastes it twice

• Image Editor: Fixed issues when drawing with the Polygon tool which could cause various bits of the screen to draw incorrectly
• Image Editor: Fixed that red/blue were swapped when pasting-in from external applications and that alpha was also wrong when copy/paste inside GMS2 itself
• Image Editor: Colour Replace tool now uses the correct red/blue values, like the fix above
• Image Editor: Fixed GMS2 going unstable when using the Colour Picker tool

• Install: Cleaned the Windows installer of any no-longer-used "components" packages for old versions of .NET and Visual C Runtime

• Project Load: Made GMS2 more reliably able to load some corrupted projects and therefore recover as much as possible

• Project Save: Resources created in the root of a project and then immediately moved into a group now save correctly again
• Project Save: GMS2 now automatically removes trailing whitespace in asset names rather than showing a filename error about the unwanted space character
• Sprite Editor: You can no longer resize the first frame into a negative value - fixes a minor UI issue with the editor not handling this properly and updating the time bar
• Startup: Added more logging to track down a rare startup crash "You must write ContentLength bytes to the request stream before calling [Begin]GetResponse" in the ui.log
• Startup: Added a fix for the Mac IDE getting an error about not being able to download and install Mono (it says a runtime could not be installed, but this was the Mono installer itself)
• Startup: Now only checks if the manual port is open if Preference to use the local manual is actually enabled [see the info in the section for this above]

2.3.4 runtimes bring updated Visual Studio support on a number of platforms, allowing you to install fewer external tools and us to simplify our setup guides. It also fixes an important Debugger crash issue and an important Vsync issue which was introduced in 2.3.3, plus a range of other bug fixes throughout. If you're a console developer, then this version also introduces Microsoft Xbox Series X/S and Sony PlayStation 5!

See below for runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Updated Visual Studio support on most platforms to require Microsoft Visual Studio 2019

  • Be aware that many YYC platforms/UWP/consoles have now stopped support for Visual Studio 2015 or 2017 and you will need to use (in most cases) 2019 instead
  • This means you need to install the new tools and have updated any existing GMS2 Preferences to point to your new VS install before attempting to build for these platforms, otherwise builds will likely fail
  • Please see the Required SDKs FAQ for specifics and the updated setup guides

Added support for new consoles

  • If your licence has been approved for Microsoft or Sony consoles already, then this version includes support for Microsoft Xbox Series X/S and Sony PlayStation 5
  • More information for these can be found alongside our other console docs (again, if you are approved)
  • Please see the very bottom of the Required SDKs FAQ for specifics and the new setup guides
