2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes since runtime 2.3.3.434

  • In-Game: Fixed most ways of calling a function which is in a global array so it no longer returns an "object undefined" error [we are aware of a route to still getting this]
  • In-Game: [VM] Fixed a code error "Object1.argument0(...) not set before reading it." when setting "self" or "global" struct values and accessing this value inside a function
  • Reverted the change for "In-Game: Sequences now create their object instances at their correct x/y values rather than creating them all at 0x0 and then quickly moving"
  • That one change above should fix various reports of issues with Sequences and objects inside the sequence not performing their Create events as expected
  • Building Projects: [Steam Windows IDE] Projects with spaces in the name no longer cause build failures due to alternative Steam launcher method issues

Runtime 2.3.3.434

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: [Android YYC] The NDK 22 installation check now finds your install correctly when starting builds
  • Building Projects: [HTML5] Added additional iframe focus-detection code in response to Itch.io/Newgrounds changes (see above)

  • In-Game: Incrementing decimal image_index values no longer returns the corrected value immediately, instead returns the "raw" result and allows a 1-frame delay before clamping properly (see above)
  • In-Game: Accessing an out-of-bounds index of an array inside a struct in VM will now error like YYC/HTML already do, rather than return 0
  • Please note that this release also changes the required SDKs for PS4 and Switch to newer versions - please see their setup guides for full details of what you need now

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes since runtime 2.3.3.434

  • In-Game: Fixed calling a function which is in a global array so it no longer returns an "object undefined" error
  • In-Game: [VM] Fixed a code error "Object1.argument0(...) not set before reading it." when setting "self" or "global" struct values and accessing this value inside a function
  • Reverted the change for "In-Game: Sequences now create their object instances at their correct x/y values rather than creating them all at 0x0 and then quickly moving"
  • That one change above should fix various reports of issues with Sequences and objects inside the sequence not performing their Create events as expected
  • Building Projects: [Steam Windows IDE] Projects with spaces in the name no longer cause build failures due to alternative Steam launcher method issues

Runtime 2.3.3.434

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Removed Git Tools From The Installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

• Note 1: This does mean that if you were using source control inside GMS2 previously you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!

• Note 2: The Mac IDE cannot push to an online repository if your keychain has not already been pre-configured with your password, etc., so when GMS2 detects this error we have added a dialog saying this and (briefly) how to fix
New Undo System
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous releases if you create a Sprite, resize it in the Sprite Editor, open it in the Image Editor and add some content, then click the Sprite Editor and press Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone rather than the Image Editor change. Now, focus is set back to the Image Editor and the last change there is undone (and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect)
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - as above, the editor would be reopened and the change performed
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes For High CPU Usage
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this and include a project which shows the issue on your machine

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes since runtime 2.3.3.434

  • In-Game: Fixed calling a function which is in a global array so it no longer returns an "object undefined" error
  • In-Game: [VM] Fixed a code error "Object1.argument0(...) not set before reading it." when setting "self" or "global" struct values and accessing this value inside a function
  • Reverted the change for "In-Game: Sequences now create their object instances at their correct x/y values rather than creating them all at 0x0 and then quickly moving"
  • That one change above should fix various reports of issues with Sequences and objects inside the sequence not performing their Create events as expected
  • Building Projects: [Steam Windows IDE] Projects with spaces in the name no longer cause build failures due to alternative Steam launcher method issues

Runtime 2.3.3.434

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Added Windows/macOS Runtimes Into The Installer
<ul>
• Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer
• This means as soon as GMS2 is installed you can create/open projects and test them on Windows or macOS (so if you're a free licence user, then there are no further downloads required)
• (If your licence allows other modules, these will still be downloaded on startup as per normal)
Removed Git Tools From The Installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

• Note 1: This does mean that if you were using source control inside GMS2 previously you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!

• Note 2: The Mac IDE cannot push to an online repository if your keychain has not already been pre-configured with your password, etc., so when GMS2 detects this error we have added a dialog saying this and (briefly) how to fix
New Undo System
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous releases if you create a Sprite, resize it in the Sprite Editor, open it in the Image Editor and add some content, then click the Sprite Editor and press Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone rather than the Image Editor change. Now, focus is set back to the Image Editor and the last change there is undone (and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect)
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - as above, the editor would be reopened and the change performed
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes For High CPU Usage
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this and include a project which shows the issue on your machine

• Should make importing and previewing sounds more reliable
• There was also a specific bug fix for Add Existing importing a single sound from another project could in some cases cause GMS2 to crash

• These are: Objects (and individual object instances inside the Sequence Editor), Notes, Scripts, Sequences (and instances of), Shaders, and Tilesets
• Now, if any of these are selected the Inspector will populate with many of the settings relevant to that asset/instance

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Added Windows/macOS Runtimes Into The Installer
<ul>
• Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer
• This means as soon as GMS2 is installed you can create/open projects and test them on Windows or macOS (so if you're a free licence user, then there are no further downloads required)
• (If your licence allows other modules, these will still be downloaded on startup as per normal)
Removed Git Tools From The Installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

• Note 1: This does mean that if you were using source control inside GMS2 previously you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!

• Note 2: The Mac IDE cannot push to an online repository if your keychain has not already been pre-configured with your password, etc., so when GMS2 detects this error we have added a dialog saying this and (briefly) how to fix
New Undo System
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous releases if you create a Sprite, resize it in the Sprite Editor, open it in the Image Editor and add some content, then click the Sprite Editor and press Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone rather than the Image Editor change. Now, focus is set back to the Image Editor and the last change there is undone (and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect)
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - as above, the editor would be reopened and the change performed
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes For High CPU Usage
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this and include a project which shows the issue on your machine
Updated FFmpeg Tools Version
<ul>
• Should make importing and previewing sounds more reliable
• There was also a specific bug fix for Add Existing importing a single sound from another project could in some cases cause GMS2 to crash
Additional Inspector Editors
<ul>
• These are: Objects (and individual object instances inside the Sequence Editor), Notes, Scripts, Sequences (and instances of), Shaders, and Tilesets
• Now, if any of these are selected the Inspector will populate with many of the settings relevant to that asset/instance
• If you multi-select items, then be aware only the relevant shared fields will be inspectable
• Another reminder that the Inspector can be accessed via Window > Inspector

Added Windows/macOS Runtimes Into The Tnstaller
<ul>
• Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer
• This means as soon as GMS2 is installed you can create/open projects and test them on Windows or macOS (so if you're a free licence user, then there are no further downloads required)
• (If your licence allows other modules, these will still be downloaded on startup as per normal)
Removed Git Tools From The Installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

• Note 1: This does mean that if you were using source control inside GMS2 previously you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!

• Note 2: The Mac IDE cannot push to an online repository if your keychain has not already been pre-configured with your password, etc., so when GMS2 detects this error we have added a dialog saying this and (briefly) how to fix
New Undo System
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous releases if you create a Sprite, resize it in the Sprite Editor, open it in the Image Editor and add some content, then click the Sprite Editor and press Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone rather than the Image Editor change. Now, focus is set back to the Image Editor and the last change there is undone (and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect)
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - as above, the editor would be reopened and the change performed
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes For High CPU Usage
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this and include a project which shows the issue on your machine

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

  • Building Projects: [Android YYC] The NDK 22 installation check now finds your install correctly when starting builds

  • In-Game: Accessing an out-of-bounds index of an array inside a struct in VM will now error like YYC/HTML already do, rather than return 0
  • Please note that this release also changes the required SDKs for PS4 and Switch to newer versions - please see their setup guides for full details of what you need now

Unbundled Git tools from the installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.
• Note: This does mean that you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!
Implemented a new Undo system
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous versions of GMS2 if you created a Sprite, resized it in the Sprite Editor, then opened it in the Image Editor and added some content, then switched focus back to the Sprite Editor and pressed Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone and not any of the later changes in the Image Editor. Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes for high CPU utilisation in the IDE
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this
• However, please be aware we have found some of our machines saw very little benefit - we're still looking into this, so please don't report tickets if CPU usage has stayed about the same for you

• Similarly, if your CPU values are lower now, you may realise that whilst the bottom dock / the Output Window is expanded, then CPU usage remains quite a bit higher than if the dock is collapsed - again, we are aware, so please don't report tickets for this

Runtime 290

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)

  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Runtime 290

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Detection for side mouse buttons on Desktop and Web targets

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Additional window-focusing code for running games on Itch.io/Newgrounds

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted to 2.2.5 behaviour when setting image_index values yourself

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Bundled Windows/macOS runtimes with the installer

• Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer

Unbundled Git tools from the installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.
• Note: This does mean that you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!
Implemented a new Undo system
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous versions of GMS2 if you created a Sprite, resized it in the Sprite Editor, then opened it in the Image Editor and added some content, then switched focus back to the Sprite Editor and pressed Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone and not any of the later changes in the Image Editor. Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes for high CPU utilisation in the IDE
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this
• However, please be aware we have found some of our machines saw very little benefit - we're still looking into this, so please don't report tickets if CPU usage has stayed about the same for you

• Similarly, if your CPU values are lower now, you may realise that whilst the bottom dock / the Output Window is expanded, then CPU usage remains quite a bit higher than if the dock is collapsed - again, we are aware, so please don't report tickets for this

Runtime 290

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Detection for side mouse buttons on Desktop and Web targets

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Additional window-focusing code for running games on Itch.io/Newgrounds

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted to 2.2.5 behaviour when setting image_index values yourself

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

Implemented a new Undo system
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous versions of GMS2 if you created a Sprite, resized it in the Sprite Editor, then opened it in the Image Editor and added some content, then switched focus back to the Sprite Editor and pressed Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone and not any of the later changes in the Image Editor. Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes for high CPU utilisation in the IDE
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this
• However, please be aware we have found some of our machines saw very little benefit - we're still looking into this, so please don't report tickets if CPU usage has stayed about the same for you

• Similarly, if your CPU values are lower now, you may realise that whilst the bottom dock / the Output Window is expanded, then CPU usage remains quite a bit higher than if the dock is collapsed - again, we are aware, so please don't report tickets for this

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Unbundled Git tools from the installer
<ul>

Implemented a new Undo system
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous versions of GMS2 if you created a Sprite, resized it in the Sprite Editor, then opened it in the Image Editor and added some content, then switched focus back to the Sprite Editor and pressed Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone and not any of the later changes in the Image Editor. Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket

<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this
• However, please be aware we have found some of our machines saw very little benefit - we're still looking into this, so please don't report tickets if CPU usage has stayed about the same for you

• Similarly, if your CPU values are lower now, you may realise that whilst the bottom dock / the Output Window is expanded, then CPU usage remains quite a bit higher than if the dock is collapsed - again, we are aware, so please don't report tickets for this

Bundled Windows/macOS runtimes with the installer
<ul>
• Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer
• This means as soon as GMS2 is installed you can create/open projects and test them on Windows or macOS (so if you're a Trial user, then there are no further downloads required)
Unbundled Git tools from the installer
<ul>
• GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

• This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.
• Note: This does mean that you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!
Implemented a new Undo system
<ul>
• All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

• It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous versions of GMS2 if you created a Sprite, resized it in the Sprite Editor, then opened it in the Image Editor and added some content, then switched focus back to the Sprite Editor and pressed Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone and not any of the later changes in the Image Editor. Now, GMS2 would set focus back to the Image Editor and undo your last change there, and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect.
• It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - in previous versions of GMS2, as soon as you closed an editor your changes were final
• If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket
Fixes for high CPU utilisation in the IDE
<ul>
• The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

• In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this
• However, please be aware we have found some of our machines saw very little benefit - we're still looking into this, so please don't report tickets if CPU usage has stayed about the same for you

• Similarly, if your CPU values are lower now, you may realise that whilst the bottom dock / the Output Window is expanded, then CPU usage remains quite a bit higher than if the dock is collapsed - again, we are aware, so please don't report tickets for this
Changed our FFmpeg integration
<ul>

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Optional arguments with default values for your functions

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Detection for side mouse buttons on Desktop and Web targets

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Additional window-focusing code for running games on Itch.io/Newgrounds

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted to 2.2.5 behaviour when setting image_index values yourself

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

2.3.2 introduces Nine Slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Fixes since runtime 423

  • Fixed runtime 423 issue with garbage collection/CPU stalls on game_end() or gc_collect() and gradual increases in memory seen in some games

Fixes since runtime 420

  • Fixed that if you tried to build iOS using the Windows IDE it could error with "The variable Xcode is not defined" (when the Mac IDE worked fine with that same Xcode install)
  • Fixed a CPU usage issue with the garbage collector, so now usage values should be much lower again on all platforms and also gives a slight performance boost compared to 2.3.1
  • Fixed an issue stopping ARM builds of Ubuntu YYC
  • Fixed an issue where projects which contain a large number of audio files could fail to build
  • Added a compiler optimisation to speed up texture page generation during builds
  • Added a small optimisation to speed up loading projects
  • Re-fixed that the Animation End event does not trigger reliably when the sprite frames and game speed result in very small values

Runtime 420

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache rather than re-writing files more often than required
  • Ternary expressions are now calculated at compile time to see if we can optimise these
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself to reduce the amount of redundant work it was going
  • The sounds change mentioned below...

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any .ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the .ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any .wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the file will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother and more accurate FPS values - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically
  • Note that whilst they're not listed individually below, multiple ticket samples were fixed at once by this change

Changes to image_index behaviour regarding Sprite Broadcast Messages

  • Following recent GMC feedback, modifying image_index manually to set new values will not modulo the resulting image_index value until the following frame (as 2.2.5-and-older used to do it)
  • Now, you will NOT get any sprite broadcast message(s) if you set image_index directly
  • Animation End events will still be fired as before if you set image_index to the final frame or beyond, there's no change here

Changes to when static variables are actually created by the compiler

  • Multiple fixes have been made on VM (YYC was usually correct) for multi-layer inheritance of constructor methods, especially if the method was redefined/uses static
  • As part of this change, each individual static variable in a given script/function are now handled first when compiling that script/event, so that their value can be used by the rest of your code
  • Note that you may still get a silent crash beyond our ability to prevent if you redefine a static method and you forget to declare each definition as a static also
  • Also fixed an issue where Static variables would get re-initialised when a function is called recursively

Misc changes to function behaviours to be aware of

  • array_length() now returns "undefined" when evaluating anything which is not an array. You may need to refactor your code to account for this change, as we have found several ticket sample projects checked array_length(0) when controlling game logic
  • buffer_load() now supports loading Included Files directly into buffers on HTML5 (same as you could already on Windows, etc.)
  • camera_set_begin_script() and camera_set_end_script() now have support for manipulating your surfaces
  • debug_get_callstack() now has an optional "maxDepth" argument, allowing you to control the size of error log you receive
  • exception_unhandled_handler(undefined) can now be used to remove any currently-set custom exception handler and return to the default GMS2 handler
  • json_parse() no longer ignores keys where the value is "null", "undefined", "nan", "infinity", or "-infinity" (note it will read the last three in as strings you will need to handle yourself later, as the JSON standard doesn't actually have rules for handling these)
  • json_stringify() now supports map keys which are set to "nan", "infinity", and "-infinity" (see the line above)
  • show_debug_message() formatting when displaying a struct on HTML5 is now consistent with how it has always behaved on Windows, etc.
  • Added a "stack overflow" error on YYC when turning an array pushed to itself into a string (VM already showed an error)
  • Multiplication of a float by an int64 (in this specific order) no longer results in the float being cast to an int first
  • HTML5 will also now not truncate int64 numbers when using postfix/prefix increment/decrement operators (as Windows, etc., already do)
  • Fixed that results of maths operations which involved enums set to float values were rounded to integer
  • Fixed that you previously got inconsistent results for "self" and "[self]" when using "with" on a struct, both will now warn that this is recursive

2.3.2 introduces Nine Slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Fixes since runtime 420

  • Fixed that if you tried to build iOS using the Windows IDE it could error with "The variable Xcode is not defined" (when the Mac IDE worked fine with that same Xcode install)
  • Fixed a CPU usage issue with the garbage collector, so now usage values should be much lower again on all platforms and also gives a slight performance boost compared to 2.3.1
  • Fixed an issue stopping ARM builds of Ubuntu YYC
  • Fixed an issue where projects which contain a large number of audio files could fail to build
  • Added a compiler optimisation to speed up texture page generation during builds
  • Added a small optimisation to speed up loading projects
  • Re-fixed that the Animation End event does not trigger reliably when the sprite frames and game speed result in very small values

Runtime 420

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache rather than re-writing files more often than required
  • Ternary expressions are now calculated at compile time to see if we can optimise these
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself to reduce the amount of redundant work it was going
  • The sounds change mentioned below...

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any .ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the .ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any .wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the file will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother and more accurate FPS values - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically
  • Note that whilst they're not listed individually below, multiple ticket samples were fixed at once by this change

Changes to image_index behaviour regarding Sprite Broadcast Messages

  • Following recent GMC feedback, modifying image_index manually to set new values will not modulo the resulting image_index value until the following frame (as 2.2.5-and-older used to do it)
  • Now, you will NOT get any sprite broadcast message(s) if you set image_index directly
  • Animation End events will still be fired as before if you set image_index to the final frame or beyond, there's no change here

Changes to when static variables are actually created by the compiler

  • Multiple fixes have been made on VM (YYC was usually correct) for multi-layer inheritance of constructor methods, especially if the method was redefined/uses static
  • As part of this change, each individual static variable in a given script/function are now handled first when compiling that script/event, so that their value can be used by the rest of your code
  • Note that you may still get a silent crash beyond our ability to prevent if you redefine a static method and you forget to declare each definition as a static also
  • Also fixed an issue where Static variables would get re-initialised when a function is called recursively

Misc changes to function behaviours to be aware of

  • array_length() now returns "undefined" when evaluating anything which is not an array. You may need to refactor your code to account for this change, as we have found several ticket sample projects checked array_length(0) when controlling game logic
  • buffer_load() now supports loading Included Files directly into buffers on HTML5 (same as you could already on Windows, etc.)
  • camera_set_begin_script() and camera_set_end_script() now have support for manipulating your surfaces
  • debug_get_callstack() now has an optional "maxDepth" argument, allowing you to control the size of error log you receive
  • exception_unhandled_handler(undefined) can now be used to remove any currently-set custom exception handler and return to the default GMS2 handler
  • json_parse() no longer ignores keys where the value is "null", "undefined", "nan", "infinity", or "-infinity" (note it will read the last three in as strings you will need to handle yourself later, as the JSON standard doesn't actually have rules for handling these)
  • json_stringify() now supports map keys which are set to "nan", "infinity", and "-infinity" (see the line above)
  • show_debug_message() formatting when displaying a struct on HTML5 is now consistent with how it has always behaved on Windows, etc.
  • Added a "stack overflow" error on YYC when turning an array pushed to itself into a string (VM already showed an error)
  • Multiplication of a float by an int64 (in this specific order) no longer results in the float being cast to an int first
  • HTML5 will also now not truncate int64 numbers when using postfix/prefix increment/decrement operators (as Windows, etc., already do)
  • Fixed that results of maths operations which involved enums set to float values were rounded to integer
  • Fixed that you previously got inconsistent results for "self" and "[self]" when using "with" on a struct, both will now warn that this is recursive

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post
Nine Slice Support
<ul>
• Nine Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between

• The Sprite Editor has a new Nine Slice panel where you can now enable this, and of course this new capability carries through into your game, where you can later manipulate the sprite at runtime should you wish
• Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
• Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ runtime also when building your project
AnimCurve Library
<ul>
• We have added a new library of preset curve types you can apply to your Bezier curves to automatically add points or change ease in/out values and easily add effects like "bounce" or "elastic"

• Also added a ? button for opening the relevant manual page onto each of the AnimCurve Editor, the AnimCurve Library window, and the Sequence Editor
New IDE and Manual localisations
<ul>
• We have now added Brazilian-Portuguese, Chinese, and Russian translations into the IDE, the installer, and also the online/downloadable versions of our manual
