2.3.2 introduces Nine Slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache rather than re-writing files more often than required
  • Ternary expressions are now calculated at compile time to see if we can optimise these
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself to reduce the amount of redundant work it was going
  • The sounds change mentioned below...

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any .ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the .ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any .wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the file will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother and more accurate FPS values - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically
  • Note that whilst they're not listed individually below, multiple ticket samples were fixed at once by this change

Changes to image_index behaviour regarding Sprite Broadcast Messages

  • Following recent GMC feedback, modifying image_index manually to set new values will not modulo the resulting image_index value until the following frame (as 2.2.5-and-older used to do it)
  • Now, you will NOT get any sprite broadcast message(s) if you set image_index directly
  • Animation End events will still be fired as before if you set image_index to the final frame or beyond, there's no change here

Changes to when static variables are actually created by the compiler

  • Multiple fixes have been made on VM (YYC was usually correct) for multi-layer inheritance of constructor methods, especially if the method was redefined/uses static
  • As part of this change, each individual static variable in a given script/function are now handled first when compiling that script/event, so that their value can be used by the rest of your code
  • Note that you may still get a silent crash beyond our ability to prevent if you redefine a static method and you forget to declare each definition as a static also
  • Also fixed an issue where Static variables would get re-initialised when a function is called recursively

Misc changes to function behaviours to be aware of

  • array_length() now returns "undefined" when evaluating anything which is not an array. You may need to refactor your code to account for this change, as we have found several ticket sample projects checked array_length(0) when controlling game logic
  • buffer_load() now supports loading Included Files directly into buffers on HTML5 (same as you could already on Windows, etc.)
  • camera_set_begin_script() and camera_set_end_script() now have support for manipulating your surfaces
  • debug_get_callstack() now has an optional "maxDepth" argument, allowing you to control the size of error log you receive
  • exception_unhandled_handler(undefined) can now be used to remove any currently-set custom exception handler and return to the default GMS2 handler
  • json_parse() no longer ignores keys where the value is "null", "undefined", "nan", "infinity", or "-infinity" (note it will read the last three in as strings you will need to handle yourself later, as the JSON standard doesn't actually have rules for handling these)
  • json_stringify() now supports map keys which are set to "nan", "infinity", and "-infinity" (see the line above)
  • show_debug_message() formatting when displaying a struct on HTML5 is now consistent with how it has always behaved on Windows, etc.
  • Added a "stack overflow" error on YYC when turning an array pushed to itself into a string (VM already showed an error)

  • Fixed that results of maths operations which involved enums set to float values were rounded to integer
  • Fixed that you previously got inconsistent results for "self" and "[self]" when using "with" on a struct, both will now warn that this is recursive

Nine Slice Support
<ul>
• Nine Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between

• The Sprite Editor has a new Nine Slice panel where you can now enable this, and of course this new capability carries through into your game, where you can later manipulate the sprite at runtime should you wish
• Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
AnimCurve Library
<ul>
• We have added a new library of preset curve types you can apply to your Bezier curves to automatically add points or change ease in/out values and easily add effects like "bounce" or "elastic"
• Presets can be applied to a whole curve or between selected points only
Mac DMG Export Package
<ul>
• If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
• A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times
<ul>
• We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
• A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
• Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
• A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
• Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
• The sounds change mentioned below
Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds
<ul>
• Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:

• If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files

• Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before

• Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound
Use Your Default Browser For Tutorials
<ul>

• Continuing our drive to use external browsers for all website functionality and thereby improve usability as well as reduce the GMS2 installer size, tutorial panels will now open in your default browser outside GMS2

• Please be aware that we have plans to make our tutorials be actual pages on our website so we can live-update fixes and add more tutorials more easily, and so the existing tutorials will all be updated in the not-too-distant future. This means formatting issues with the current tutorials are a known issue and will be fixed asap - kindly do not submit bug reports for these

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
  • The sounds change mentioned below

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother FPS - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses

And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

Beta runtime 254...

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
  • The sounds change mentioned below

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother FPS - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses

2.3.2 introduces nine slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Beta runtime 254...

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
  • The sounds change mentioned below

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother FPS - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses

2.3.2 introduces nine slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Beta runtime 254...

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
  • The sounds change mentioned below

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother FPS - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses

2.3.2 introduces nine slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache
  • The sounds change mentioned below

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the wav will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother FPS - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses

Project Conversion Fixes
<ul>

• Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
• 1) The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
• 2) Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
• 3) DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
• 4) Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

• If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 (and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy), please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the project .yyz/.zip
Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor - Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached
Room Manager Tools
<ul>

• The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
• Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom
Multiple New Package Formats
<ul>
• Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
• ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device you are targeting for that build)
• UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
• Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

• If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Removed The English Manual From The Installer
<ul>

• As more of you are using GMS2's localisation capabilities and choosing to work in your native languages, we have now removed the English manual from the GMS2 install to save a reasonable amount of download size and install space requirement
• The first time you access the manual inside GMS2 you will be asked if you want to download a local copy and work offline or if you're happy continuing with the online manual
• If you want to download the manual later on, or want to change your manual language, then you can do this via Preferences > General Settings > Help
• Be aware also that as well as manual.yoyogames.com (English), there is now also manual-de (Deutsch), manual-fr (Française) and manual-es (Español)
Misc Other Changes
<ul>
• Changed the default sorting method used when importing a project to be Custom, so the Asset Browser order matches how the project looked before

• Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on { for those who only want to fold via regions

• Added a new Preference for whether you want changing the filtering of the asset browser to immediately re-expanded the groups or not (that the asset browser always expanded all groups each time you created an asset while the filter is active has been fixed)

• Have had to slightly change the Mac IDE keys for managing Bookmarks, as the old ones clashed with macOS hotkeys and so caused issues - setting a bookmark is now CMD+CTRL+[0-9] and jumping back to it later is CMD+[0-9]
• Within the Sequence Editor, you can now create Moment functions using the name you set in the text box, rather than having to create and then rename
• Added a Preference to edit the boiler plate comment shown at the top of a new Script Resource (or to turn it off if you want)
• Added a timeout to debugger connections - so now GMS2 will abort the build and show a "Are you perhaps firewalled?" if the debugger takes too long, rather than waiting indefinitely
• File > My Account will now use your default browser, rather than opening a browser workspace tab inside GMS2
• Lots of missing translations for 2.3.0 features have now been added, along with the translations for the new stuff in 2.3.1

• Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)
• Removed some redundant arguments from buffer_get_surface(), so you will need to refactor any code using this function

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Runtime 2.3.1.406

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
  • Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
  • Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

Multiple New Package Formats

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.
  • game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now
  • ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.
  • There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

Misc Other Changes

  • Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
  • Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual
  • Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

Project Conversion Fixes
<ul>

• Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
• 1) The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
• 2) Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
• 3) DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
• 4) Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

• If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 (and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy), please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the project .yyz/.zip
Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor - Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached
Room Manager Tools
<ul>

• The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
• Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom
Multiple New Package Formats
<ul>
• Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
• ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device you are targeting for that build)
• UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
• Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

• If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Removed The English Manual From The Installer
<ul>

• As more of you are using GMS2's localisation capabilities and choosing to work in your native languages, we have now removed the English manual from the GMS2 install to save a reasonable amount of download size and install space requirement
• The first time you access the manual inside GMS2 you will be asked if you want to download a local copy and work offline or if you're happy continuing with the online manual
• If you want to download the manual later on, or want to change your manual language, then you can do this via Preferences > General Settings > Help
• Be aware also that as well as manual.yoyogames.com (English), there is now also manual-de (Deutsch), manual-fr (Française) and manual-es (Español)
Misc Other Changes
<ul>
• Changed the default sorting method used when importing a project to be Custom, so the Asset Browser order matches how the project looked before

• Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on { for those who only want to fold via regions

• Added a new Preference for whether you want changing the filtering of the asset browser to immediately re-expanded the groups or not (that the asset browser always expanded all groups each time you created an asset while the filter is active has been fixed)

• Have had to slightly change the Mac IDE keys for managing Bookmarks, as the old ones clashed with macOS hotkeys and so caused issues - setting a bookmark is now CMD+CTRL+[0-9] and jumping back to it later is CMD+[0-9]
• Within the Sequence Editor, you can now create Moment functions using the name you set in the text box, rather than having to create and then rename
• Added a Preference to edit the boiler plate comment shown at the top of a new Script Resource (or to turn it off if you want)
• Added a timeout to debugger connections - so now GMS2 will abort the build and show a "Are you perhaps firewalled?" if the debugger takes too long, rather than waiting indefinitely
• File > My Account will now use your default browser, rather than opening a browser workspace tab inside GMS2
• Lots of missing translations for 2.3.0 features have now been added, along with the translations for the new stuff in 2.3.1

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Runtime 2.3.1.406

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
  • Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
  • Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

Multiple New Package Formats

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.
  • game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now
  • ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.
  • There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

Misc Other Changes

  • Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
  • Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual
  • Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

Project Conversion Fixes
<ul>

• Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
• 1) The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
• 2) Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
• 3) DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
• 4) Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

• If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 (and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy), please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the project .yyz/.zip
Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor - Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached
Room Manager Tools
<ul>

• The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
• Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom
Multiple New Package Formats
<ul>
• Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
• ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device you are targeting for that build)
• UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
• Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

• If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Removed The English Manual From The Installer
<ul>

• As more of you are using GMS2's localisation capabilities and choosing to work in your native languages, we have now removed the English manual from the GMS2 install to save a reasonable amount of download size and install space requirement
• The first time you access the manual inside GMS2 you will be asked if you want to download a local copy and work offline or if you're happy continuing with the online manual
• If you want to download the manual later on, or want to change your manual language, then you can do this via Preferences > General Settings > Help
• Be aware also that as well as manual.yoyogames.com (English), there is now also manual-de (Deutsch), manual-fr (Française) and manual-es (Español)

<ul>
• Changed the default sorting method used when importing a project to be Custom, so the Asset Browser order matches how the project looked before

• Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on { for those who only want to fold via regions

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
  • Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
  • Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

Multiple New Package Formats

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.
  • game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now
  • ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.
  • There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

Misc Other Changes

  • Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
  • Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual
  • Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

Project Conversion Fixes
<ul>

• Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
• The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
• Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
• DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
• Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

• If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy, please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the original .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor = Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window!
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline, and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached
Room Manager Tools
<ul>

• The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
• Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom
Multiple new package formats have been added
<ul>
• Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
• ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
• UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
• Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

• If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Misc Other Changes
<ul>

• Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on { for those who only want to fold via regions

• Added a new Preference for whether you want changing the filtering of the asset browser to immediately re-expanded the groups or not (that the asset browser always expanded all groups each time you created an asset while the filter is active has been fixed)

• Have had to slightly change the Mac IDE keys for managing Bookmarks, as the old ones clashed with macOS hotkeys and so caused issues - setting a bookmark is now CMD+CTRL+[0-9] and jumping back to it later is CMD+[0-9]
• Within the Sequence Editor, you can now create Moment functions using the name you set in the text box, rather than having to create and then rename
• Added a Preference to edit the boiler plate comment shown at the top of a new Script Resource (or to turn it off if you want)
• Added a timeout to debugger connections - so now GMS2 will abort the build and show a "Are you perhaps firewalled?" if the debugger takes too long, rather than waiting indefinitely
• File > My Account whill now use your default browser, rather than opening a browser workspace tab inside GMS2
• Lots of missing translations for 2.3.0 features have now been added - note that at this time the 2.3.1 additions are not translated

• Added a new accessor for structs - $ (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for in-game changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Beta 187...

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used in show_debug_overlay() to be blue for garbage collection, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions

Multiple new package formats have been added

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Major changes to be aware of

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and change it accordingly.

game_save() and game_load() have had a fix to make them save all the internal variables they should have been saving in 2.3.0 - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work.

Misc Other Changes

  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for in-game changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Beta 187...

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used in show_debug_overlay() to be blue for garbage collection, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions

Multiple new package formats have been added

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Major changes to be aware of

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and change it accordingly.

game_save() and game_load() have had a fix to make them save all the internal variables they should have been saving in 2.3.0 - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work.

Misc Other Changes

  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for in-game changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Beta 187...

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used in show_debug_overlay() to be blue for garbage collection, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions

Multiple new package formats have been added

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Major changes to be aware of

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and change it accordingly.

game_save() and game_load() have had a fix to make them save all the internal variables they should have been saving in 2.3.0 - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work.

Misc Other Changes

  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

<ul>
