Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor = Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window!
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline, and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARM, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for in-game changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Changes since Beta 187

  • Debugger: [Mac IDE] Does not show values of any Watches
  • In-Game: A sequence audio track will play the beginning of the sound again when it completes [note that this is now controlled in the Inspector within the IDE]
  • In-Game: Closing the runner when a sequence moment has been used will cause the runner to crash
  • In-Game: Some projects show error "Layer system integrity compromised" in output window when changing room, causes some to hang
  • In-Game: [macOS] array_sort() silent crashes when custom sort and array greater than 7 elements
  • In-Game: [Windows YYC] Project attached errors when matching gems
  • In-Game: url_open() gives broken URL in very recent Chrome/Chromium-based browsers
  • In-Game: script_execute_ext() will silent crash if the argument array is empty
  • In-Game: Different result when using Bitwise shifts between HTML5 and windows
  • In-Game: [HTML5] current_time() return format is not consistent with other platforms
  • In-Game: ds_list_read returns "undefined" when legacy mode is set to "false" or omitted
  • Some console SDK requirements have changed since the last beta, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.

Note: The fix mentioned above for ds_list_read() is actually that 2.3.0 should have written out a different string formatting version number along with the changes to formatting when writing out any data structure as a string (lists/maps/queues, etc.). Therefore, whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - you will unfortunately need to use 2.3.0 to read your data now and then re-save the string using 2.3.1/this beta.

Beta 187...

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used in show_debug_overlay() to be blue for garbage collection, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions

Multiple new package formats have been added

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Major changes to be aware of

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and change it accordingly.

game_save() and game_load() have had a fix to make them save all the internal variables they should have been saving in 2.3.0 - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work.

Misc Other Changes

  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

Project Conversion Fixes
<ul>

• Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
• The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
• Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
• DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
• Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

• If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy, please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the original .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Bezier Curves
<ul>
• Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor = Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

• Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself
Dopesheet Curve Editor
<ul>

• Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
• Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet
Snappable Dopesheet
<ul>

• And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window!
• Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
• Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another
Sprite Broadcast Messages
<ul>
• 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
• You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline, and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached
Room Manager Tools
<ul>

• The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
• Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom
Multiple new package formats have been added
<ul>
• Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
• ARM packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
• UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
• Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

• If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)
Misc Other Changes
<ul>

• Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on ( for those who only want to fold via regions

• Added a new Preference for whether you want changing the filtering of the asset browser to immediately re-expanded the groups or not (that the asset browser always expanded all groups each time you created an asset while the filter is active has been fixed)

• Have had to slightly change the Mac IDE keys for managing Bookmarks, as the old ones clashed with macOS hotkeys and so caused issues - setting a bookmark is now CMD+CTRL+[0-9] and jumping back to it later is CMD+[0-9]
• Within the Sequence Editor, you can now create Moment functions using the name you set in the text box, rather than having to create and then rename
• Added a Preference to edit the boiler plate comment shown at the top of a new Script Resource (or to turn it off if you want)
• Added a timeout to debugger connections - so now GMS2 will abort the build and show a "Are you perhaps firewalled?" if the debugger takes too long, rather than waiting indefinitely
• File > My Account whill now use your default browser, rather than opening a browser workspace tab inside GMS2
• Lots of missing translations for 2.3.0 features have now been added - note that at this time the 2.3.1 additions are not translated

• Added a new accessor for structs - $ (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARM, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used in show_debug_overlay() to be blue for garbage collection, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions

Multiple new package formats have been added

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARM packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (now part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and change it accordingly.

game_save() and game_load() have had a fix to make them save all the internal variables they should have been saving in 2.3.0 - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work.

Misc Other Changes

  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

2.3.0 is a huge new release and there is a lot changed, as this version now contains everything we announced in the "Upcoming Changes to GML" blogs that we published last year as well as a very sizeable list of bug fixes and new additions to match changes to asset types now in the 2.3.0 IDE, so please read these notes carefully and check out the guide linked-to below. (For the IDE release notes, see this page.)

Because this version is so big and contains so much new stuff these notes will be brief, but for more information on everything below please see this detailed introduction to all the new features and some important notes about moving your projects from 2.2.5 to 2.3.0. Please also be aware that opening an existing project in 2.3.0 the first time will ask you to convert the project and save it out again with a new name. This is because the project format has now been changed quite extensively. You will not be able to open newer-style projects in 2.2.5 or older, and similarly 2.3.0 does not allow you to set 2.2.5 or older runtimes as active.

You should check out the all-new manual for specifics on the new/changed functions and if your project requires any modifying post-conversion, as it is likely at least some small changes will need to be made.

Scripts now contain functions

  • A script asset is no longer limited to being just one custom function - instead, you will find a new function declaration is added whenever you create a script, and you can add your own below this and call these functions as required elsewhere in your game
  • Scripts are also now processed on startup, which means if you create a script which contains lines which are not wrapped in a function declaration, those lines will always run on game start, allowing you to very easily create initialisation scripts and control functionality
  • NOTE: You should review your scripts after importing any 2.2.5 projects in case you need to remove/tweak these function declarations so that your game initialises correctly.

Methods

  • You can also now bind functions to your instances and call them in a natural way

All arrays are now 1D

  • However, they can actually now be chained, so you can create arrays three (or more) deep if you require by chaining the declaration - e.g. array[0][0][0]
  • The 2D array functions have now been deprecated, but if you have these in your 2.2.5 projects they will still work due to the compatibility layer

Sequences and Animation Curves

  • There are new functions to allow you to create entirely new assets at runtime or to return and modify existing ones created in the IDE

Structs

  • You can now declare structs, which are (in very simple terms) one variable holding a collection of other variables, and create instances of these on-demand, allowing you to manage your data more clearly

Garbage Collector

  • The runner now has a multi-stage garbage collector to clean up in-game memory and maintain performance
  • This is all automatically done for you, but there are functions to allow you to call it on-demand also and even to turn it off if you wish

Handling exceptions via Try/Catch

  • You can now Try() a bit of code and Catch() if it gave any errors, allowing you to hopefully recover from a bad situation
  • If things aren't recoverable, you can also Finally() a last bit of code before your game shows an error and ends
  • You can also Throw() an exception at any time, allowing you to create your own custom errors
  • And you can handle runner exceptions also by declaring your own unhandled exception handler

And much, much more!

Original Release 359/358
Updated Licensing to Remove GPU Checks
<ul>
• Some customers had issues where dual-GPUs in their machines meant moving the IDE between displays or toggling power-saving modes could cause their licence to be invalidated
• This GPU check has been removed, but now everyone needs to refresh their licence the first time they run 2.2.4 - please remember you will need an internet connection to achieve this
• Note, if you're using 2.2.4 on the same machine as 2.2.3 or older (e.g., you have a Steam install and a standalone), then be aware you will be asked to log-in again each time you start the IDE
macOS Catalina Support
<ul>

• This version of GMS2 is compliant with Apple's new "notarization" system - if you're using Catalina then it's important you update to this new version, or you will have issues making/running projects
• Note: that this change by Apple means when building your games, before the package will work on any other machine the packages need to be submitted in Xcode to Apple and notarized
• Fixed an issue with project files being left open during builds longer than required, which should stop "Too many files open" build errors (all versions of macOS)
• Changed the "clean" button to confirm if you need elevated permissions in order to clean files in your build folder (e.g., Apple Sign-In information) and then prompt you on the Mac if required
Changed behaviour around saving empty code files
<ul>
• Code files are now only created on disk if there is actually something to save when the editor is closed the first time after creating the resource
• Now, if you create a new Script/Event/Shader/Instance Creation Code/Room Creation Code/Timeline moment/Note and then close the Code Editor without typing anything, no empty file will be created
• Stops redundant file watcher notifications that your project has changed on disk
Extra Name Verification For Included Files
<ul>
• Building for Apple platforms and Android/Amazon, you will now get an error if you try to export an Included File which has a name starting with a number
• These device OSes do not allow filenames starting with a number, so this stops you wondering why the file can't be found in-game later on
• Until you fix the incorrect filename or disable the Included File from being exported into your package, you will see this error each time
Removed redundant in-game analytics checkbox in Game Options
<ul>
• The runner no longer requests analytics information when players run games, following the previous de-activation of the server, so this redundant checkbox has now been removed
Extended HTML5 Browser Launch Settings
<ul>
• Changed the micro webserver into a console application, so you now won't see the UI pop up when you run your games - instead, all the server's logging will be in your Output Window
• Added Preferences for you to specify the default webserver URLs and port
• Added Device Manager support to pass command line arguments to the browser (e.g., start with the dev tools open)
• Because these new Preferences have been added, this means you can still configure every field which was previously shown on the webserver UI
Misc
<ul>
• General: Changed GPU memory allocation for editor windows, which should result in better performance when moving between workspaces and/or running GMS2 for a while
• General: Fixed Help > Release Notes / Runtime Release notes link to be https versions, not http, to avoid issues where some users could not see the contents of the notes
• General: Fixed those above two links to send you to the correct versions of the notes if you're currently using a beta release without actually having opted-in
• Build Windows: Fixed Windows VM Steam builds to use the correct Steamworks dll version from your Steamworks install folder (YYC was fine)
• Code Editor: Fixed that custom snippets were only appended to the defaults, they couldn't replace a default - snippets will now override if a duplicate keybinding is found
• Compiling: Fixed on some platforms the build timer didn't stop at the end of the build, instead it kept going until the game was also closed
• Compiling: Fixed an issue where changing the creation order of instances in the Room Editor could make double-clicking compiler errors open the wrong instance's code

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Runtime Update 367+

  • 0031442: HTML5: Attached project hangs when comparing two arrays which also reference themselves
  • 0031441: Mac: Xbox One wireless gamepads do not get correct input from D-Pads
  • 0031431: General: Objects with depth < -15998 are not drawn
  • 0031443: HTML5: inconsistent results between HTML5 and windows when using bitwise operators
  • 0031418: Web Server: [Mac IDE] [Catalina] Attempting to run HTML5 target will not create the web server
  • The webserver is now run as a console application on all operating systems, so you won't see the server window any more - instead, you will get server startup/shutdown text in your Output Window log
  • All of the Preferences for controlling the web server still work, so any configuring you used to do in the server UI you can still do via Preferences
  • 0031420: Functions: string_upper/lower() on md5_file() result of a file that does not exist causes crash
  • 0031425: HTML5: Timelines throw an error in browser console about missing event_perform_timeline(), don't start
  • 0031426: HTML5: for() loops that omit sections of the statement/expression will cause a page crash
  • 0031428: Windows YYC: Post-increment optimisation in 2.2.4 causes issues when parsing script arguments array, tries to read off the end
  • Fixed a UWP issue where if you hadn't set your package name, building with the empty default caused issues, so the default is now "Made with GameMaker Studio 2"
  • Fixed a HTML5 obfuscation issue where nested /* comments not being closed properly/individually could cause building the project to get stuck

Runtime Update 366

  • 0031417: HTML5: for() loops cause a page crash

Original Release 364

Updated IAP Support For Google Play, Amazon, and all Apple platforms

  • Updated the Google IAPs extension and created new Amazon IAPs and Apple IAPs extensions - you now need to use these for all IAP functionality (these won't work with older runtimes)
  • Added support for subscriptions on all of these platforms
  • Added support for communication with external payment verification servers (note that Amazon requires you to use your own web server for verifying all IAPs)
  • Added support for local verification of receipts on some stores (not Amazon and not for any subscriptions - all stores require a custom web server for subscriptions)
  • Note that whilst verification (local or remote) is technically optional we would recommend you always use this!
  • Removed all functionality from the old iap_...() functions built-in to the runner - these now only debug message to the console that you shouldn't use that function

Apple Sign-In Support

  • Added Game Options to toggle Apple Sign-In support on macOS, iOS, and tvOS
  • You can download the new extension from the Marketplace

Websocket Support

  • Added support for websockets to allow HTML5 to HTML5 connections and HTML5 to VM/YYC connections
  • Now, you can create your server as a GMS2 desktop app or a NodeJS application and have multiple browsers and other native apps connect to this
  • See the manual for network_create_server() / network_create_server_raw() and network_create_socket() / network_create_socket_ext()

Other Notable HTML5 Changes

  • Fixed a number of functions not working and/or causing debug builds to fail to start because the code was missing a semicolon
  • Fixed turning an individual view off when the room had views enabled prevented instances within that viewport triggering their events
  • Fixed file_find_first() returning -1 instead of "" and file_find_next() returning nothing at all
  • Fixed several issues where event_perform_object() did not work the same as it does on Windows, etc.
  • Fixed several inconsistencies with keyboard_* and mouse_* variables between Windows and HTML5 when changing rooms or resetting the game (0030702)
  • Fixed event_number so it is not always 0
  • Fixed skeleton_animation_get_frame() so it does not always return 0
  • Fixed round() so it doesn't fail when trying to use very large numbers
  • Fixed ds_grid_value_* to return the correct match as soon as it is found, rather than carrying on and then always returning the bottom-right corner
  • Fixed date_valid_datetime() so dates older than Jan 1 1970 are no longer valid (matches Windows, etc.)
  • Fixed randomise/randomize() to return the seed value (matches Windows, etc.)
  • Fixed is_infinity() and is_nan() behaviours to match Windows, etc.
  • And plenty more... (See the Change Log link below.)

Updated Android build toolchain

  • Added support for building projects using Android API 29
  • Added support for building projects using AndroidX (Android Support Library is no longer supported, so you need to update any extensions in your projects which rely on this!)
  • Added support for building a Google Play App Bundle package (toggle the file format drop-down in the Explorer/Finder dialog when clicking Create Exe)
  • Added support for injecting text into the Android "application tag" during builds (be aware some extensions need you to set android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" for allowing http traffic in Android API 28+)
  • Added support for specifying an Amazon TV banner image and have this packaged correctly in-game
  • Changed to a current version of Gradle (5.1.1), so now you can use current versions of JDK and more easily implement some of your own extensions
  • Removed the change of title to "[Game Name] (as Yoyo runner)" when doing a run (Create exe never did this)
  • Please note that our Google Play Services and Google Play Expansion extensions have been updated to match these changes and so won't build with older runtimes!

Noteable macOS Changes

  • Notarisation support has been added during builds - you will need to submit your archive in Xcode to Apple to complete the process
  • Mac: Fixed gamepad_test_mapping() did not override the mapping properly when the pad was one which already had a default mapping in the database

Noteable iOS Changes

  • Fixed legacy splash screen info and startup code in packages were stopping the updated splashes from 2.2.2 from working properly in current Xcode builds
  • Note: This does remove the old functionality where the runner would try to download the game over wifi - you have to use USB between the iDevice and your Mac (as we have actually documented for a while)
  • Fixed an iOS 13 issue where landscape games incorrectly launched in a portrait view, so only a portion of the game view was visible and was also rotated
  • Fixed achievement_load_leaderboard() on Game Center, plus added the updated "team_player_id" and "game_player_id" variables in iOS 12.4 and above (all of this on tvOS also)
  • Fixed the building of frameworks in your project which have a "+" sign in its name
  • Fixed the "Defer Home Indicator Input" option so on iOS 13 this option isn't effectively ignored by the OS
  • Note: If enabled, the home bar will always be shown at low alpha, the first swipe wakes the bar and the second takes you home; If disabled, the bar is not shown in-game, but the first edge swipe will take you home
  • Added PS4/Xbox One gamepad support and the updated "menu" and "options" buttons support Apple added for iOS 13 / tvOS 13 (and macOS Catalina)
  • Added the plist flags required for TestFlight submissions, following recent-ish requirement changes
  • Note that there is currently no mention of ipadOS in our docs/the IDE and no new target has been added - this is because iOS packages still work absolutely fine on ipadOS also

Notable UWP Changes

  • UWP: Fixed window_set_size(), window_set_fullscreen() and the "start in fullscreen" option so you can now control the game window size as you'd expect
  • UWP: Added implementations of window_set_caption(), window_mouse_set(), window_get_x() and window_get_y()
  • UWP: Added debug output of failed DPDeploy return values - now exposes more information when there is a device connection error
  • Note that following changes to Device Portal in Windows 10 v1903, please make sure you do not require authentication in Device Portal, otherwise DPDeploy will fail (0031273)

Misc

  • Gamepads: Gamepad functionality is now only bundled-into your app package if you actually use gamepad functions - be aware only having Async events for the pad found/lost events isn't enough to cause pad support to be added
  • Buffers: Fixed a memory leak in buffer_compress() with handling the source buffer
  • Buffers: Fixed various issues where the "usedsize" value of the buffer was not being updated properly or was mistakenly being initialised to the full size of the buffer
  • Buffers: Changed buffer_base64_decode() to return -1 if it can't decode a string, rather than throwing an error
  • Collisions: Fixed a couple of issues where disabling "solid" for an instance caused collisions to think the instance was in a previous position when you re-enabled "solid" later
  • Collisions: Fixed a crash checking collisions against an instance which has an empty sprite set as its sprite_index (and it won't detect a hit)
  • Functions: Fixed the OpenGL implementation of gpu_set_texrepeat(true) (0031303)
  • Functions: Fixed json_decode() so a json "null" becomes a GML "undefined" and json_encode() so it turns a GML "undefined" into a json "null"
  • Functions: Fixed json_encode() so encoding a map containing an array key will now throw a code error rather than silently crashing
  • Functions: Fixed room_assign() so Create events in the new room are fired as expected
  • Functions: Fixed room_duplicate() so it uses the "object following" value set in the source room
  • Functions: Added support for buffer_f16
  • Functions: Added variable_instance_names_count()
  • General: Removed the Output Window debug text for alleged max/min/avg FPS values, as this always showed odd and incorrect results when using game_end()
  • General: Fixed that a constant of 0.5 evaluates to true when part of a boolean expression
  • Networking: Fixed http_request() on macOS, iOS/tvOS, UWP and some consoles so when using a buffer body so it doesn't always do a POST and instead does what you asked for
  • Physics: Games now throw a code error if physics_fixture_add_point() is called when you haven't already set the polygon/chain shape
  • Ubuntu: Fixed the game window position on multiple-monitor setups so it's launched/leaves fullscreen in the middle of the primary monitor, not across the bezels of both monitors

2.2.4 is a big update of the Android toolchain to match the requirements of API 29 (Android 10), and the same on macOS/iOS/tvOS to match Apple's announcements in their new releases - please update to this version if you're using macOS Catalina.

IAP support has been greatly updated - including subscriptions support and receipt verification functionality!

There has been another big push on making HTML5 games work more closely to how they do on other platforms, and we also added Websockets support so now you have much more scope for networked games.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Updated IAP Support For Google Play, Amazon, and all Apple platforms

  • Updated the Google IAPs extension and created new Amazon IAPs and Apple IAPs extensions - you now need to use these for all IAP functionality (these won't work with older runtimes)
  • Added support for subscriptions on all of these platforms
  • Added support for communication with external payment verification servers (note that Amazon requires you to use your own web server for verifying all IAPs)
  • Added support for local verification of receipts on some stores (not Amazon and not for any subscriptions - all stores require a custom web server for subscriptions)
  • Note that whilst verification (local or remote) is technically optional we would recommend you always use this!
  • Removed all functionality from the old iap_...() functions built-in to the runner - these now only debug message to the console that you shouldn't use that function

Apple Sign-In Support

  • Added Game Options to toggle Apple Sign-In support on macOS, iOS, and tvOS
  • You can download the new extension from the Marketplace

Websocket Support

  • Added support for websockets to allow HTML5 to HTML5 connections and HTML5 to VM/YYC connections
  • Now, you can create your server as a GMS2 desktop app or a NodeJS application and have multiple browsers and other native apps connect to this
  • See the manual for network_create_server() / network_create_server_raw() and network_create_socket() / network_create_socket_ext()

Other Notable HTML5 Changes

  • Fixed a number of functions not working and/or causing debug builds to fail to start because the code was missing a semicolon
  • Fixed turning an individual view off when the room had views enabled prevented instances within that viewport triggering their events
  • Fixed file_find_first() returning -1 instead of "" and file_find_next() returning nothing at all
  • Fixed several issues where event_perform_object() did not work the same as it does on Windows, etc.
  • Fixed several inconsistencies with keyboard_* and mouse_* variables between Windows and HTML5 when changing rooms or resetting the game (0030702)
  • Fixed event_number so it is not always 0
  • Fixed skeleton_animation_get_frame() so it does not always return 0
  • Fixed round() so it doesn't fail when trying to use very large numbers
  • Fixed ds_grid_value_* to return the correct match as soon as it is found, rather than carrying on and then always returning the bottom-right corner
  • Fixed date_valid_datetime() so dates older than Jan 1 1970 are no longer valid (matches Windows, etc.)
  • Fixed randomise/randomize() to return the seed value (matches Windows, etc.)
  • Fixed is_infinity() and is_nan() behaviours to match Windows, etc.
  • And plenty more... (See the Change Log link below.)

Updated Android build toolchain

  • Added support for building projects using Android API 29
  • Added support for building projects using AndroidX (Android Support Library is no longer supported, so you need to update any extensions in your projects which rely on this!)
  • Added support for building a Google Play App Bundle package (toggle the file format drop-down in the Explorer/Finder dialog when clicking Create Exe)
  • Added support for injecting text into the Android "application tag" during builds (be aware some extensions need you to set android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" for allowing http traffic in Android API 28+)
  • Added support for specifying an Amazon TV banner image and have this packaged correctly in-game
  • Changed to a current version of Gradle (5.1.1), so now you can use current versions of JDK and more easily implement some of your own extensions
  • Removed the change of title to "[Game Name] (as Yoyo runner)" when doing a run (Create exe never did this)
  • Please note that our Google Play Services and Google Play Expansion extensions have been updated to match these changes and so won't build with older runtimes!

Noteable macOS Changes

  • Notarisation support has been added during builds - you will need to submit your archive in Xcode to Apple to complete the process
  • Mac: Fixed gamepad_test_mapping() did not override the mapping properly when the pad was one which already had a default mapping in the database

Noteable iOS Changes

  • Fixed legacy splash screen info and startup code in packages were stopping the updated splashes from 2.2.2 from working properly in current Xcode builds
  • Note: This does remove the old functionality where the runner would try to download the game over wifi - you have to use USB between the iDevice and your Mac (as we have actually documented for a while)
  • Fixed an iOS 13 issue where landscape games incorrectly launched in a portrait view, so only a portion of the game view was visible and was also rotated
  • Fixed achievement_load_leaderboard() on Game Center, plus added the updated "team_player_id" and "game_player_id" variables in iOS 12.4 and above (all of this on tvOS also)
  • Fixed the building of frameworks in your project which have a "+" sign in its name
  • Fixed the "Defer Home Indicator Input" option so on iOS 13 this option isn't effectively ignored by the OS
  • Note: If enabled, the home bar will always be shown at low alpha, the first swipe wakes the bar and the second takes you home; If disabled, the bar is not shown in-game, but the first edge swipe will take you home
  • Added PS4/Xbox One gamepad support and the updated "menu" and "options" buttons support Apple added for iOS 13 / tvOS 13 (and macOS Catalina)
  • Added the plist flags required for TestFlight submissions, following recent-ish requirement changes
  • Note that there is currently no mention of ipadOS in our docs/the IDE and no new target has been added - this is because iOS packages still work absolutely fine on ipadOS also

Notable UWP Changes

  • UWP: Fixed window_set_size(), window_set_fullscreen() and the "start in fullscreen" option so you can now control the game window size as you'd expect
  • UWP: Added implementations of window_set_caption(), window_mouse_set(), window_get_x() and window_get_y()
  • UWP: Added debug output of failed DPDeploy return values - now exposes more information when there is a device connection error
  • Note that following changes to Device Portal in Windows 10 v1903, please make sure you do not require authentication in Device Portal, otherwise DPDeploy will fail (0031273)

Misc

  • Gamepads: Gamepad functionality is now only bundled-into your app package if you actually use gamepad functions - be aware only having Async events for the pad found/lost events isn't enough to cause pad support to be added
  • Buffers: Fixed a memory leak in buffer_compress() with handling the source buffer
  • Buffers: Fixed various issues where the "usedsize" value of the buffer was not being updated properly or was mistakenly being initialised to the full size of the buffer
  • Buffers: Changed buffer_base64_decode() to return -1 if it can't decode a string, rather than throwing an error
  • Collisions: Fixed a couple of issues where disabling "solid" for an instance caused collisions to think the instance was in a previous position when you re-enabled "solid" later
  • Collisions: Fixed a crash checking collisions against an instance which has an empty sprite set as its sprite_index (and it won't detect a hit)
  • Functions: Fixed the OpenGL implementation of gpu_set_texrepeat(true) (0031303)
  • Functions: Fixed json_decode() so a json "null" becomes a GML "undefined" and json_encode() so it turns a GML "undefined" into a json "null"
  • Functions: Fixed json_encode() so encoding a map containing an array key will now throw a code error rather than silently crashing
  • Functions: Fixed room_assign() so Create events in the new room are fired as expected
  • Functions: Fixed room_duplicate() so it uses the "object following" value set in the source room
  • Functions: Added support for buffer_f16
  • Functions: Added variable_instance_names_count()
  • General: Removed the Output Window debug text for alleged max/min/avg FPS values, as this always showed odd and incorrect results when using game_end()
  • General: Fixed that a constant of 0.5 evaluates to true when part of a boolean expression
  • Networking: Fixed http_request() on macOS, iOS/tvOS, UWP and some consoles so when using a buffer body so it doesn't always do a POST and instead does what you asked for
  • Physics: Games now throw a code error if physics_fixture_add_point() is called when you haven't already set the polygon/chain shape
  • Ubuntu: Fixed the game window position on multiple-monitor setups so it's launched/leaves fullscreen in the middle of the primary monitor, not across the bezels of both monitors

2.2.3 sees the release of tvOS as a new platform, Android using OpenGL ES 2 by default, and being able to turn off the sandbox and using subst'ed drives on desktop platforms. It also comes with a whole bunch of important bug fixes and the extending of a number of functions which were only implemented for very specific platforms to now work properly on all applicable platforms.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Runtime 344 Hotfix Change

  • 0031135 Compiling: Asset Compiler gets stuck in an infinite loop "Reading config delta" trying to process overriden instance variables

New tvOS export target

  • Added tvOS as a new supported target platform
  • Also adds support for the Siri gamepad/remote
  • See the manual and our setup guide on the Helpdesk for more info
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Mac Build Tools Updated

  • Worked around the version of Mono installed by Visual Studio 2019 For Mac having a broken certificate-checker and causing errors when trying to compile projects in GMS2
  • Fixed an OpenSSH issue which stopped some Mojave users from being able to build projects on their Ubuntu machines even though Target Manager said the connection was successful
  • Fixed that iOS builds always failed to run project from the IDE due to i386 architecture error during the Tests phase, causing you to have to run the project in Xcode
  • Fixed the Mac build settings which were causing the "icon" vs "Icon" filename issue when building Mac VM packages and submitting these to the App Store

Changes to layer system for persistent instances and particle systems

  • Fixed/changed persistent instances/particle systems to now preserve their layer information as they move between rooms, creating a new layer of that name and depth in the new room if required
  • If a layer of the correct name already exists in the new room, then the instance/particle system will be placed on that layer (even if the depth value differs)
  • Fixes issues with the instance's layer information changing to just be "-1" after moving between rooms

Changes to Android support/behaviours

  • Changed the runner to always use OpenGL ES 2 if the device supports it. Fixes "inconsistency" bugs reported for older Android devices.
  • Changed to now only pause the runner on explicit "onPause" messages from the OS and not pause on "focus lost" messages also - fixes issues where dragging down the tray would pause your game
  • Fixed an issue with Lint analysis failing builds during the gamepad checking stage if your Minimum API value was set to 18 or lower

Ability to launch Steam-enabled games via alternative launcher on Windows

  • Added new Game Option > Windows > "Use alternative launcher for Steam application"
  • Only valid if using the Windows Steam IDE, as this fixes the issue where Steam now detects GMS2's own app ID instead of the real ID of your game if you simply ran the project inside the IDE
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Ability to turn off the file-system sandbox on desktop OSes

  • Added Game Options into Windows/macOS/Ubuntu for disabling the file-system sandbox restrictions, so you can save/load files from anywhere not protected by the OS or other security software
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Ability to turn off using subst'ed drives when building for some platforms

  • Preferences > General Settings > Compiling now has a new setting "Use subst for drive paths" - disabling this will stop GMS2 mounting temp build folders as extra drives
  • Note: Has no effect on building for Android or tvOS, as Google's/Apple's build tools frequently exceed Window's maximum filepath length, so without this on you likely couldn't build these platforms
  • Note: Has no effect on runtime downloads/installs either, so if your machine simply doesn't allow subst to run, this option won't stop you needing to resolve that before GMS2 can work properly
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Better support/logging of custom errors on Windows builds

  • Added support for both VM and YYC builds to pass debug_event() messages to show_debug_message()
  • Added support for debug_event() to make YYC games actually finish crashing before showing the error dialog which caused the crash - useful when debugging your YYC game in Visual Studio
  • See debug_event()'s manual page for full info on both changes and how to use this new functionality

Misc

  • Fixed the FPS cap/sync on Ubuntu if using an Nvidia GPU, so now your games won't run at turbo speed
  • Fixed that the iPhone X "home indicator" bar was remaining slightly visible at all times - it now fades away from sight
  • Fixed a couple of issues with touches and VKeys not working at the very edges of iOS device screens - however, remember Apple's guidelines are to not have UI here anyway!
  • Fixed a memory leak when returning to a persistent room
  • Fixed layer_destroy_instances() on HTML5 so it now works as expected
  • Fixed http_request() so it always returns headers on Windows 7
  • Fixed a number of collision issues with re-activated instances
  • Fixed a HTML5-only issue with sometimes only using one Spine sprite for all objects
  • Fixed that an unwanted READ_PHONE_STATE permission was being added by the compiler into projects which used Google Play Licensing
  • Fixed texture_global_scale() on Windows to confirm the texture page has not disabled scaling before doing any scaling operation - stops Windows/macOS inconsistencies with this function
  • Fixed a number of inconsistencies with date_... functions on HTML5 so they now work the same way as Windows
  • Fixed an issue with textures/fonts occasionally being lost in-game if you used mipmapping support on macOS
  • Fixed an issue with Spine animations not moving smoothly if you were drawing the skeleton yourself
  • Fixed an issue with gamepad support not working in Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers (Opera, Vivaldi, etc.)
  • Changed YYC's default epsilon value to be the same as VM's (0.00001), stops issues with floating point precision differing between VM and YYC
  • Changed (whenever the compiler determines it's safe to do so) i++ to always be ++i as this is much faster to perform, especially when using YYC
  • Extended surface_depth_disable() so it now works on all platforms
  • Extended the runner's mip-mapping functionality to support HTML5 also
  • Added four-byte wide Unicode character support, so now emojis, etc., can be drawn in-game if they are added to your fonts
  • Added new functions/constants for NaN and infinity, so you can handle these better and avoid errors

This release has the long-awaited Spine update, which brings support for the recent 3.7 version of Spine. We have also revamped our font-handling and updated the FreeType library. Our HTML5 audio-handling has been improved in line with browser changes and we have addressed issues with streaming audio on Android and iOS browsers.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Spine Support Updated to v3.7

We have used a public fork of the spine runtimes (see our Github). We plan to use this repository going forward, so if you are interested in seeing which changes we have had to make, or which changes/fixes we have taken from the original Esoteric repository, you can.

As well as fixing a few Spine collision issues, we have added support for several Spine features, and you can find the detail for these in the manual (and the guide linked-to in the heading above):

  • Clipping attachments - These are attachments assigned to Spine slots which clip away parts of the sprite
  • Per-attachment colours - We now support tinting attachments based on their assigned colours
  • Per-slot blend modes - We now support per-slot blend modes as specified in the Spine IDE
  • Partial tint-black support - Note that this requires the use of a custom shader (see our manual)
  • Multiple texture page support - We now support Spine sprites which use atlases referencing multiple image files (see this guide)
  • Floating point frame indexes - so you get super-smooth animations, especially noticeable for slow-mo or speed-up effects

FreeType library update

  • All platforms now use v2.9.1 of FreeType (was 2.8.0). Fixes incompatibilities with some fonts and should improve rendering quality of others - requires 2.2.2+ IDE also, otherwise your font might not look as expected!

GML Consistency

  • Changed many string-handling and constant/variable conversion behaviours to match how VM works
  • Made YYC ignore empty scripts the same as VM does, which stops in-game code errors
  • Fixed that ternary operators did not work in YYC
  • See this blog post for further info

Facebook Support Change

  • Created a new Facebook extension for implementing up-to-date FB functionality, replaces our legacy version released a long time ago
  • Removed all the old "facebook_..." functions and constants from the runner, so now if you don't add the FB extension your game has no FB code in it
  • Any project using the old integration now needs to be updated to use the new extension and new function names, etc.
  • See the Marketplace for the new extension and this Helpdesk guide on implementing the extension in your projects

In-Game GIF File Creation

  • Added a new family of functions to allow you to create .gif files from surfaces: gif_open(), gif_add_surface(), gif_save(), and gif_save_buffer()

Extra Tileset Management Functions

  • tileset_get_texture(tileset_id) - get the texture for the given tileset
  • tileset_get_uvs(tileset_id) - get the array of UVs for the tileset (in the same format as sprite_get_uvs() returns its info)
  • tileset_get_name(tileset_id) - get the name of the tileset

Performance Optimisations

  • A number of areas of the asset compiler and runner have now been optimised so your games will run faster and use less memory
    • Runner
      • Camera performance and handling has been improved - this has significant changes when surfaces are set and reset
      • Sped up room change operations
      • Sped up Graphics::SetMatrix, which affects many sprite, views and surface operations
      • When creating Surfaces the runner now doesn’t recalculate matrices if not required
      • Draw event optimisations on sparse layers
      • Memory optimisations on several internal structures for instances and events
      • Optimised the search for and handling of events, particularly for objects with parents
      • Sped up hashing functions used for all maps and internal dictionaries
      • Sped up Instance variable look-ups
      • Smaller collision tree - only instances that have collision events or are marked as solid are added by default. Others are added if a collision query is made that would/could return them
      • Note: If any collision call is made with "object_all" everything gets added to the tree, so it is best to avoid doing this
      • Now only add timeline and path structures for each instance if they are actually used by that instance
    • Asset Compiler
      • Sped up constructing texture pages from texture groups
      • Handling of cropped textures has been improved
  • We have also added new texture page management functions so you can better control your game's memory allocation:
    • texture_prefetch(), texture_is_ready() and texture_flush()
    • texturegroup_get_...() for returning arrays of assets ids on a given page - added variants for textures, sprites, fonts, and tilesets
    • texture_debug_messages() toggles whether the runner writes texture fetch\flush debug output
    • Spine sprites listed as part of a texture page are also included when the above functions are called (SWFs are already on the texture page, so work anyway)
    • See the manual for specifics
  • Please test your games thoroughly, and let us know if you have issues

This release sees important fixes for Mac submission packages, fixes for iOS audio crash issues, and a number of memory protection fixes on all platforms. New in this release:

For IDE release notes, see this page


Collision List Functions

  • Added ..._list() versions of the collision functions (e.g., collision_line_list(), instance_position_list()) to return a list of all colliders, not just the first one found
  • Can also choose to order the list by instance position or leave at the default of instance-creation order, as per the non-list functions()
  • Tends to be much faster than the single-return functions if you need multiple colliders, as there is much less overhead and duplicated checking of instances required
  • See the manual for more information

New collision type for sprites: Non-axis-aligned bounding box

  • Is more accurate than Rectangle collisions because it rotates the bounding box with the sprite rather than making the bounding box bigger
  • Gives better performance than having to use precise collisions (if this new type is applicable for your needs, of course)
  • See the manual for more information

Virtual Keyboard Functions

  • Functions have now been added to show, configure the type of keyboard, get data back, and hide the virtual keyboard

In these August 2023.800 Beta releases there are: New functions for rotating and colouring particles and others which allow you to burst the particles previously created in the editor; IPv6 support on many more platforms (some consoles do not support IPv6); functions for controlling the mouse on some platforms; and many other fixes and improvements

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2023.6.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for some very important changes you need to be aware of.

Changes Since Beta Runtime 395

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: [Ubuntu] Build-and-Launch stops after the .appimage has been created and does not launch the game
  • In-Game: [Switch] Global arrays are lost when the room changes
  • In-Game: Texture state functions (such as wrapping and mipmapping) don't work correctly for stages 3-6
  • In-Game: draw_set_font(-1) will cause a fatal error
  • In-Game: sprite_exists(-1) will cause a fatal error
  • In-Game: sprite_exists() throws an error when querying a sprite which has already been destroyed

Beta Runtime 395

IPv6 Support On More Platforms

  • More platforms can now send/receive unicast traffic using IPv6 - everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • IPv6 hostnames will now be detected and existing networking functions should all work

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • nameof(name) Returns the argument as a string, resolved at compile time

Design/Debug GUI Functions

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay
  • dbg_section(name) Declare a new debug section and add it to the current debug view that is active - NOTE: if no view has already been declared using dbg_view() then a "Default" view will be created automatically and the section will be added to that
  • dbg_slider(dbgref,[minimum],[maximum],[label]) Creates a slider for a real value within the current debug section, minimum and maximum values can be specified
  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)
  • dbg_watch(dbgref,[label]) Creates a watch for any value within the current debug section - each value is converted to a string and displayed
  • dbg_text(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text entry (from a variable) within the current debug section, this text can be multiline and is not split into 2 columns but shown in a single column
  • dbg_sprite(dbgrefSprite,dbgrefSpriteIndex,[label]) Creates a sprite view within the current debug section of the specified sprite with the specified index
  • dbg_text_input(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text input entry within the current debug section
  • dbg_checkbox(dbgref,[label]) Creates a checkbox entry within the current debug section - variable will be a boolean value
  • dbg_colour(dbgref,[label]) dbg_color(dbgref,[label]) Creates a colour entry within the current debug section - variable will be a colour RGB value with no alpha
  • dbg_button(label,dbgref,[width],[height]) Creates a button within the current debug section and the given method will be called when the button is pressed - it is not split into two columns but shown in a single column
  • NOTE: For all of the above functions, if no section has already been declared using dbg_section() then a "Default" section will be created automatically and the gadget will be added to that
  • dbg_same_line() Causes the next debug control to be placed on the same line as the current debug control (if they are both single-column controls)
  • dbg_ref(dbgrefOrStruct,dbgrefOrName,[index]) Create a debug reference to a live variable

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

[Switch] Added support for expanding save data area size dynamically, so players can create more save files when required

  • switch_save_data_get_max_size() - Gets the maximum allowable save data area and save data journal area size from the NMETA file.
  • switch_save_data_get_size(account_id) - Gets the save data area and save data journal area size for the user.
  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) - This function extends the save data area for a user. The user's save data must not be mounted. This function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly.

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

Beta Runtime 395

IPv6 Support On More Platforms

  • More platforms can now send/receive unicast traffic using IPv6 - everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • nameof(name) Returns the argument as a string, resolved at compile time

Fix For macOS VM Building (sudden new "Malware" notifications the OS might be showing you)

Runtime 2023.6.0.137

Changes To Verifying Preferences Path/Command Line Paths During Builds

  • Previously, if a required path for command line builds was not supplied when triggering the build this could result in a silent crash of the build tools, rather than a useable error message saying that you needed to supply the required path (and which specific path was at fault)
  • Now, all of the paths are checked before the build is started and if issues are found the build will be correctly stopped and you will get an error message asking you to supply the missing info
  • Note that this change does also affect builds done inside the IDE - so if you try to build for a target which you have not correctly configured inside Preferences, you will now more reliably get an error message telling you which setting needs to be fixed (and again the build will be failed properly)

Debug overlays have been updated!

  • We have incorporated Dear ImGui into the runner and initially we are using it to have a better and richer debug experience
  • The old FPS overlay is now replaced with an improved graph showing changes over time and it will also show a stacked snapshot of the current frame as well
    • FPS window - shows the current FPS graph
    • Audio window - shows the current audio that is in flight and a graph of the mixers that are active
    • Log window - shows the log output (currently only on Windows and macOS, but other platforms will follow in future releases)
  • Mouse and keyboard input are supported within ImGui, so you can interact with the windows and move them around as you wish
  • We will be expanding the ImGui usage over the next few versions in order to add in more functionality and capabilities

New Audio Effects

  • Three new audio filters have been added:
    • High-shelf filter (AudioEffectType.HiShelf) - this passes all frequencies, but increases or reduces frequencies above the shelf frequency by a specified gain
    • Low-shelf filter (AudioEffectType.LoShelf) - this passes all frequencies, but increases or reduces frequencies below the shelf frequency by a specified gain
    • Peak EQ filter (AudioEffectType.PeakEQ) - A peak EQ filter creates a peak or a dip in the spectrum by a specified gain around a specified centre frequency
  • Each of these filters have the same parameter set:
    • freq - the midpoint frequency (in Hz) of the shelf's slope (HiShelf / LoShelf) or the centre frequency (PeakEQ)
    • q - the quality factor
    • gain - the amount (as linear gain) to boost frequencies by (use db_to_lin() to give values in dB)
  • As mentioned above, the AudioEffectType enum has 3 new options: PeakEQ (which equals 7), HiShelf (8), and LoShelf (9)
  • And similarly, the AudioEffect struct has a new key for “freq”

Create Your Own "Game Launcher" App

  • game_change() can now be used to change from the current game and instead load the data file from another game, allowing you to pass arguments to the new game, and returning to the launcher again when the new game is closed
  • The other project(s) must have been compiled already and then its data.win file also needs to have been added into the launcher project as an Included File
  • This function requires VM builds (not YYC) and is supported on Windows, macOS, PS4, PS5 and Switch only - and note that only Windows supports running the launcher project from the IDE, all the others require the launcher to be built as a standalone application before game_change() can work

New Asynchronous Zip Functions

  • zip_create() creates a new Zip archive structure (note that the object returned from this function is garbage-collected when no longer referenced, so it doesn't need to be manually cleaned up)
  • zip_add_file(zip, path, file_path) adds a copy of the given file to a to a Zip structure - for nesting, include slashes in the path (e.g. "myFolder/test.txt")
  • zip_save(zip, path) finalises the Zip structure (meaning that no new files can be written to it) and saves the archive to the given path
  • Note that zip_save() is performed asynchronous and will trigger an event on success or failure

Ability To Retrieve Skeleton Attachment Data At Runtime

  • sprite_get_info() now includes a full list of all the available attachments for each slot on the skeleton if the sprite you have requested is a Spine sprite
  • Each element under "slots" now has an "attachments" array, which is a list of attachment names for that slot
