Xbox GDK Video PlayBack Changes

  • Video playback on Xbox has always worked slightly differently to the other consoles. On Xbox videos were always drawn to fill the currently-set surface, whereas on the other consoles a new surface is created, which the video is decoded to, and it's then the game's responsibility to draw that surface to wherever it's required to be displayed
  • This release changes how Xbox works, so that it matches the other platforms - accordingly, any code you have for video playback on Xbox will need to be reviewed now

Xbox GDK Now Able To Load UWP Game Saves

  • xboxone_set_savedata_uwp_compatibility() enables compatibility with existing UWP save game files - this function must be called before the game performs any savedata-related file operations
  • Note: this function is only to be used in projects which are updating an already-released UWP title to use GDK instead

Changes To Cocoapods Initialisation

  • Changed the initialisation flow to make the process simpler
  • Will also detect and workaround/fix more setup issues present on the Mac
  • Also adds architecture support for both Intel and Silicon Macs

Choose Your Preferred Spine Collision Values

  • Prior to April, GameMaker would inconsistently apply one of either of the bounding box and/or collision mask from a Spine collision mesh or the precomputed mask from the Sprite Editor, depending on different code paths executed in the game
  • In April Betas this was temporarily changed to always use the Spine collision mesh everywhere, but then we received feedback that a number of games were relying on collision values defined in the Sprite Editor (even though those values did not apply well to all Spine sprites) and so that change got removed again before the April monthly release
  • This updated change for June now adds a "Spine Collision Mesh" option into the Sprite Editor, which allows you to explicitly choose to consistently use Spine collision meshes OR GM collision masks in all code paths, on a per-sprite basis

Control SDF Settings For A Font In The IDE

  • Added support for outputting SDF font-rendering information during compilation, so now fonts which were created in the IDE are supported in-game
  • You can find new settings in the Font Editor and the Inspector to enable/disable SDF and configure the required values
  • Also, when in-game you will now find font_get_info() now includes SDF status and information

Added support for struct "shorthand"

  • Inside the code editor you can now use "shorthand" to declare a struct and say that you want it to contain a member with the same name as an existing variable, saving you needing to add the ": repeat the variable name" bit each time
  • So, for example, if we have these three lines in our code: var apples = 10; var oranges = 15; var all_fruits = {apples: apples, oranges: oranges, lemons: 7} we could now shorten that third line and write it as var all_fruits = {apples, oranges, lemons: 7} instead
  • The compiler will expand your code back into the old format for you and so everything will work as before in-game

Misc New Functions

  • ds_grid_to_mp_grid(src,dest,[func]) - converts a DS grid into an MP grid. You can also provide an optional predicate function argument to map the DS grid value to the corresponding MP grid value. If you don't provide a predicate function, the function will treat zero values as empty and non-zero values as occupied.
  • surface_get_format(surface_id) - returns the format of the given surface. All formats are listed in our manual.
  • display_get_frequency() - returns the frequency (or refresh rate) of the display that the game is being played on. It will return a real value as frames-per-second, so for example if your monitor is 60hz you will get 60, if it's running at 144hz then you will get 144, and so on.

In this June 2023.6 release there are: new debug overlays which use a new GUI system; 3 new audio effects; support for the new NPLN multiplayer system on Switch; changes to Xbox GDK to make video rendering require the same setup as the other platforms and being able to read old UWP saves in your GDK games; changes to Cocoapods to make them easier to setup and more reliably handle existing setup issues on the Mac; a new “game launcher” system; support for a struct “shorthand” style in the Code Editor and for the new Spine collisions and SDF font controls already mentioned above; lots of other new functions and a number of important bug fixes.

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for all runtime changes/fixes since 2023.4.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for all the IDE ones.

Changes To Verifying Preferences Path/Command Line Paths During Builds

  • Previously, if a required path for command line builds was not supplied when triggering the build this could result in a silent crash of the build tools, rather than a useable error message saying that you needed to supply the required path (and which specific path was at fault)
  • Now, all of the paths are checked before the build is started and if issues are found the build will be correctly stopped and you will get an error message asking you to supply the missing info
  • Note that this change does also affect builds done inside the IDE - so if you try to build for a target which you have not correctly configured inside Preferences, you will now more reliably get an error message telling you which setting needs to be fixed (and again the build will be failed properly)

Debug overlays have been updated!

  • We have incorporated Dear ImGui into the runner and initially we are using it to have a better and richer debug experience
  • The old FPS overlay is now replaced with an improved graph showing changes over time and it will also show a stacked snapshot of the current frame as well
    • FPS window - shows the current FPS graph
    • Audio window - shows the current audio that is in flight and a graph of the mixers that are active
    • Log window - shows the log output (currently only on Windows and macOS, but other platforms will follow in future releases)
  • Mouse and keyboard input are supported within ImGui, so you can interact with the windows and move them around as you wish
  • We will be expanding the ImGui usage over the next few versions in order to add in more functionality and capabilities

New Audio Effects

  • Three new audio filters have been added:
    • High-shelf filter (AudioEffectType.HiShelf) - this passes all frequencies, but increases or reduces frequencies above the shelf frequency by a specified gain
    • Low-shelf filter (AudioEffectType.LoShelf) - this passes all frequencies, but increases or reduces frequencies below the shelf frequency by a specified gain
    • Peak EQ filter (AudioEffectType.PeakEQ) - A peak EQ filter creates a peak or a dip in the spectrum by a specified gain around a specified centre frequency
  • Each of these filters have the same parameter set:
    • freq - the midpoint frequency (in Hz) of the shelf's slope (HiShelf / LoShelf) or the centre frequency (PeakEQ)
    • q - the quality factor
    • gain - the amount (as linear gain) to boost frequencies by (use db_to_lin() to give values in dB)
  • As mentioned above, the AudioEffectType enum has 3 new options: PeakEQ (which equals 7), HiShelf (8), and LoShelf (9)
  • And similarly, the AudioEffect struct has a new key for “freq”

Create Your Own "Game Launcher" App

  • game_change() can now be used to change from the current game and instead load the data file from another game, allowing you to pass arguments to the new game, and returning to the launcher again when the new game is closed
  • The other project(s) must have been compiled already and then its data.win file also needs to have been added into the launcher project as an Included File
  • This function requires VM builds (not YYC) and is supported on Windows, macOS, PS4, PS5 and Switch only - and note that only Windows supports running the launcher project from the IDE, all the others require the launcher to be built as a standalone application before game_change() can work

New Asynchronous Zip Functions

  • zip_create() creates a new Zip archive structure (note that the object returned from this function is garbage-collected when no longer referenced, so it doesn't need to be manually cleaned up)
  • zip_add_file(zip, path, file_path) adds a copy of the given file to a to a Zip structure - for nesting, include slashes in the path (e.g. "myFolder/test.txt")
  • zip_save(zip, path) finalises the Zip structure (meaning that no new files can be written to it) and saves the archive to the given path
  • Note that zip_save() is performed asynchronous and will trigger an event on success or failure

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

  • dbg_section(name) Declare a new debug section and add it to the current debug view that is active - NOTE: if no view has already been declared using dbg_view() then a "Default" view will be created automatically and the section will be added to that
  • dbg_slider(dbgref,[minimum],[maximum],[label]) Creates a slider for a real value within the current debug section, minimum and maximum values can be specified
  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)
  • dbg_watch(dbgref,[label]) Creates a watch for any value within the current debug section - each value is converted to a string and displayed
  • dbg_text(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text entry (from a variable) within the current debug section, this text can be multiline and is not split into 2 columns but shown in a single column
  • dbg_sprite(dbgrefSprite,dbgrefSpriteIndex,[label]) Creates a sprite view within the current debug section of the specified sprite with the specified index
  • dbg_text_input(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text input entry within the current debug section
  • dbg_checkbox(dbgref,[label]) Creates a checkbox entry within the current debug section - variable will be a boolean value
  • dbg_colour(dbgref,[label]) dbg_color(dbgref,[label]) Creates a colour entry within the current debug section - variable will be a colour RGB value with no alpha
  • dbg_button(label,dbgref,[width],[height]) Creates a button within the current debug section and the given method will be called when the button is pressed - it is not split into two columns but shown in a single column

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

Switch - Support For Larger Save Areas

  • Functions have now been added for expanding a player's save data area size dynamically, so your game can create more save space when required
  • switch_save_data_get_max_size() gets the maximum allowable save data area and save data journal area size from the NMETA file
  • switch_save_data_get_size(account_id) gets the save data area and save data journal area size for the user
  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) extends the save data area for a user - the save data must not be mounted at the time and this function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth

  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large

If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large

In these August 2023.800 Beta releases there are: New functions for rotating and colouring particles and others which allow you to burst the particles previously created in the editor; IPv6 support on many more platforms (some consoles do not support IPv6); functions for controlling the mouse on some platforms; and many other fixes and improvements

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2023.6.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for some very important changes you need to be aware of.

Changes Since Beta Runtime 396

Functions To Create Your Own Debug/Design ImGUI Overlays

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay
  • dbg_section(name) Declare a new debug section and add it to the current debug view that is active - NOTE: if no view has already been declared using dbg_view() then a "Default" view will be created automatically and the section will be added to that
  • dbg_slider(dbgref,[minimum],[maximum],[label]) Creates a slider for a real value within the current debug section, minimum and maximum values can be specified
  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)
  • dbg_watch(dbgref,[label]) Creates a watch for any value within the current debug section - each value is converted to a string and displayed
  • dbg_text(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text entry (from a variable) within the current debug section, this text can be multiline and is not split into 2 columns but shown in a single column
  • dbg_sprite(dbgrefSprite,dbgrefSpriteIndex,[label]) Creates a sprite view within the current debug section of the specified sprite with the specified index
  • dbg_text_input(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text input entry within the current debug section
  • dbg_checkbox(dbgref,[label]) Creates a checkbox entry within the current debug section - variable will be a boolean value
  • dbg_colour(dbgref,[label]) dbg_color(dbgref,[label]) Creates a colour entry within the current debug section - variable will be a colour RGB value with no alpha
  • dbg_button(label,dbgref,[width],[height]) Creates a button within the current debug section and the given method will be called when the button is pressed - it is not split into two columns but shown in a single column
  • NOTE: For all of the above functions, if no section has already been declared using dbg_section() then a "Default" section will be created automatically and the gadget will be added to that
  • dbg_same_line() Causes the next debug control to be placed on the same line as the current debug control (if they are both single-column controls)
  • dbg_ref(dbgrefOrStruct,dbgrefOrName,[index]) Create a debug reference to a live variable
  • Additionally, show_debug_overlay() has now been extended to allow setting whether it's minimised or not, its scale and its alpha - show_debug_overlay(enable,[minimised],[scale],[alpha])

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

Switch - Support For Larger Save Areas

  • Functions have now been added for expanding a player's save data area size dynamically, so your game can create more save space when required
  • switch_save_data_get_max_size() gets the maximum allowable save data area and save data journal area size from the NMETA file
  • switch_save_data_get_size(account_id) gets the save data area and save data journal area size for the user
  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) extends the save data area for a user - the save data must not be mounted at the time and this function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly

Beta Runtime 396

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

In these August 2023.800 Beta releases there are: New functions for rotating and colouring particles and others which allow you to burst the particles previously created in the editor; IPv6 support on many more platforms (some consoles do not support IPv6); functions for controlling the mouse on some platforms; and many other fixes and improvements

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2023.6.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for some very important changes you need to be aware of.

Changes Since Beta Runtime 396

Functions To Create Your Own Debug/Design ImGUI Overlays

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay
  • dbg_section(name) Declare a new debug section and add it to the current debug view that is active - NOTE: if no view has already been declared using dbg_view() then a "Default" view will be created automatically and the section will be added to that
  • dbg_slider(dbgref,[minimum],[maximum],[label]) Creates a slider for a real value within the current debug section, minimum and maximum values can be specified
  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)
  • dbg_watch(dbgref,[label]) Creates a watch for any value within the current debug section - each value is converted to a string and displayed
  • dbg_text(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text entry (from a variable) within the current debug section, this text can be multiline and is not split into 2 columns but shown in a single column
  • dbg_sprite(dbgrefSprite,dbgrefSpriteIndex,[label]) Creates a sprite view within the current debug section of the specified sprite with the specified index
  • dbg_text_input(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text input entry within the current debug section
  • dbg_checkbox(dbgref,[label]) Creates a checkbox entry within the current debug section - variable will be a boolean value
  • dbg_colour(dbgref,[label]) dbg_color(dbgref,[label]) Creates a colour entry within the current debug section - variable will be a colour RGB value with no alpha
  • dbg_button(label,dbgref,[width],[height]) Creates a button within the current debug section and the given method will be called when the button is pressed - it is not split into two columns but shown in a single column
  • NOTE: For all of the above functions, if no section has already been declared using dbg_section() then a "Default" section will be created automatically and the gadget will be added to that
  • dbg_same_line() Causes the next debug control to be placed on the same line as the current debug control (if they are both single-column controls)
  • dbg_ref(dbgrefOrStruct,dbgrefOrName,[index]) Create a debug reference to a live variable
  • Additionally, show_debug_overlay() has now been extended to allow setting whether it's minimised or not, its scale and its alpha - show_debug_overlay(enable,[minimised],[scale],[alpha])

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

Switch - Support For Larger Save Areas

  • Functions have now been added for expanding a player's save data area size dynamically, so your game can create more save space when required
  • switch_save_data_get_max_size() gets the maximum allowable save data area and save data journal area size from the NMETA file
  • switch_save_data_get_size(account_id) gets the save data area and save data journal area size for the user
  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) extends the save data area for a user - the save data must not be mounted at the time and this function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly

Beta Runtime 396

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

Beta Runtime 395

IPv6 Support On More Platforms

  • More platforms can now send/receive unicast traffic using IPv6 - everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • IPv6 hostnames will now be detected and existing networking functions should all work

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • nameof(name) Returns the argument as a string, resolved at compile time

  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New SDF Font Rendering Effects

  • Added support for three new rendering effects now available in-game: "Crisp Glow", "Outline", "Drop Shadow" (each of which can be configured in the Font Editor also)
  • font_enable_effects(font, enable, optional_params) has been added for controlling all of this at runtime - all effects require this to be enabled on a font for the effect to be visible (it will also show an error if it is passed a font which is an IDE-generated font which did not have SDF enabled)
  • "optional_params" must be a struct and can contain any (or all) of the following fields:
    • "thickness": the thickness modifier for the font - this can be a value from -32 to 32 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • "coreColour": the core colour of the font
    • "coreAlpha: the alpha of the core part of the font
    • ""glowEnable": enable\disable the glow effect on the font
    • ""glowStart": the distance where the glow effect starts fading out - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowEnd": the distance where the glow effect finishes fading to fully transparent - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowColour": the glow colour of the font
    • ""glowAlpha": the glow alpha of the font
    • ""outlineEnable": enables\disables the outline effect on the font
    • ""outlineDistance": the distance that the outline extends from the edge of each glyph - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""outlineColour": the outline colour of the font
    • ""outlineAlpha": the outline alpha of the font
    • ""dropShadowEnable": enable\disable the drop shadow effect on the font
    • ""dropShadowSoftness": the width of the penumbra region of the shadow - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""dropShadowOffsetX": the X offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowOffsetY": the Y offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowColour": the drop shadow colour of the font
    • ""dropShadowAlpha": the drop shadow alpha of the font
    • Be aware that when drawing text using the standard text drawing functions the colour values specified for the core, outline and glow colours will be multiplied by either the current draw colour in the case of "draw_text()" or whichever manually-specified colours were passed to those other text functions
    • Also note that the drop shadow offset is affected by both the scale and rotation of the text that is drawn (i.e. an offset value of 10 pixels will become 100 pixels if the text is drawn at 10-times scale, and rotating the text by 45 degrees will cause the shadow offset to also be rotated 45 degrees)

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) extends the save data area for a user - the save data must not be mounted at the time and this function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly

  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • nameof(name) Returns the argument as a string, resolved at compile time

In these August 2023.800 Beta releases there are: New functions for rotating and colouring particles and others which allow you to burst the particles previously created in the editor; IPv6 support on many more platforms (some consoles do not support IPv6); functions for controlling the mouse on some platforms; and many other fixes and improvements

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2023.6.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for some very important changes you need to be aware of.

Changes Since Beta Runtime 406

New SDF Font Rendering Effects

  • Added support for three new rendering effects now available in-game: "Crisp Glow", "Outline", "Drop Shadow" (each of which can be configured in the Font Editor also)
  • font_enable_effects(font, enable, optional_params) has been added for controlling all of this at runtime - all effects require this to be enabled on a font for the effect to be visible (it will also show an error if it is passed a font which is an IDE-generated font which did not have SDF enabled)
  • "optional_params" must be a struct and can contain any (or all) of the following fields:
    • "thickness": the thickness modifier for the font - this can be a value from -32 to 32 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • "coreColour": the core colour of the font
    • "coreAlpha: the alpha of the core part of the font
    • ""glowEnable": enable\disable the glow effect on the font
    • ""glowStart": the distance where the glow effect starts fading out - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowEnd": the distance where the glow effect finishes fading to fully transparent - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowColour": the glow colour of the font
    • ""glowAlpha": the glow alpha of the font
    • ""outlineEnable": enables\disables the outline effect on the font
    • ""outlineDistance": the distance that the outline extends from the edge of each glyph - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""outlineColour": the outline colour of the font
    • ""outlineAlpha": the outline alpha of the font
    • ""dropShadowEnable": enable\disable the drop shadow effect on the font
    • ""dropShadowSoftness": the width of the penumbra region of the shadow - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""dropShadowOffsetX": the X offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowOffsetY": the Y offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowColour": the drop shadow colour of the font
    • ""dropShadowAlpha": the drop shadow alpha of the font
  • Be aware that when drawing text using the standard text drawing functions the colour values specified for the core, outline and glow colours will be multiplied by either the current draw colour in the case of "draw_text()" or whichever manually-specified colours were passed to those other text functions
  • Also note that the drop shadow offset is affected by both the scale and rotation of the text that is drawn (i.e. an offset value of 10 pixels will become 100 pixels if the text is drawn at 10-times scale, and rotating the text by 45 degrees will cause the shadow offset to also be rotated 45 degrees)

Particle Functions Now Use Typed References

  • Particle system Assets, Instances, Emitters, and Types are all now typed references, and so all part_...() functions will now confirm that the argument you have passed them is actually the correct thing they were expecting and will show an appropriate error when the argument being passed in is wrong
  • particle_get_info() also now supports particle systems created in-game via part_system_create() (in previous releases it only considered particles created in the IDE and so you could see incorrect results for in-game instances)

    • "effectParams": contains a struct with the same fields as is detailed in the documentation for "font_enable_effects()" above - note that this will always contain a valid struct regardless of whether "effectsEnabled" is true or not, so always check the field above also!

Functions To Create Your Own Debug/Design ImGUI Overlays

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay
  • dbg_section(name) Declare a new debug section and add it to the current debug view that is active - NOTE: if no view has already been declared using dbg_view() then a "Default" view will be created automatically and the section will be added to that
  • dbg_slider(dbgref,[minimum],[maximum],[label]) Creates a slider for a real value within the current debug section, minimum and maximum values can be specified
  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)
  • dbg_watch(dbgref,[label]) Creates a watch for any value within the current debug section - each value is converted to a string and displayed
  • dbg_text(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text entry (from a variable) within the current debug section, this text can be multiline and is not split into 2 columns but shown in a single column
  • dbg_sprite(dbgrefSprite,dbgrefSpriteIndex,[label]) Creates a sprite view within the current debug section of the specified sprite with the specified index
  • dbg_text_input(dbgref,[label]) Creates a text input entry within the current debug section
  • dbg_checkbox(dbgref,[label]) Creates a checkbox entry within the current debug section - variable will be a boolean value
  • dbg_colour(dbgref,[label]) dbg_color(dbgref,[label]) Creates a colour entry within the current debug section - variable will be a colour RGB value with no alpha
  • dbg_button(label,dbgref,[width],[height]) Creates a button within the current debug section and the given method will be called when the button is pressed - it is not split into two columns but shown in a single column
  • NOTE: For all of the above functions, if no section has already been declared using dbg_section() then a "Default" section will be created automatically and the gadget will be added to that
  • dbg_same_line() Causes the next debug control to be placed on the same line as the current debug control (if they are both single-column controls)
  • dbg_ref(dbgrefOrStruct,dbgrefOrName,[index]) Create a debug reference to a live variable
  • Additionally, show_debug_overlay() has now been extended to allow setting whether it's minimised or not, its scale and its alpha - show_debug_overlay(enable,[minimised],[scale],[alpha])

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

Switch - Support For Larger Save Areas

  • Functions have now been added for expanding a player's save data area size dynamically, so your game can create more save space when required
  • switch_save_data_get_max_size() gets the maximum allowable save data area and save data journal area size from the NMETA file
  • switch_save_data_get_size(account_id) gets the save data area and save data journal area size for the user
  • switch_save_data_set_size(account_id,save_data_size,save_data_journal_size) extends the save data area for a user - the save data must not be mounted at the time and this function can only be called a limited number of times (32), so use sparingly

Beta Runtime 396

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

Beta Runtime 395

IPv6 Support On More Platforms

  • More platforms can now send/receive unicast traffic using IPv6 - everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • IPv6 hostnames will now be detected and existing networking functions should all work

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • nameof(name) Returns the argument as a string, resolved at compile time

"Send A Bug Report" Tool
<ul>

New SDF Font Rendering Effects
<ul>

• Added support for three new rendering effects now available in-game: "Crisp Glow", "Outline", "Drop Shadow" - each of which can be enabled/disabled and configured in a new panel within the Font Editor

• Be aware that when drawing text using the standard text drawing functions the colour values specified for the core, outline and glow colours will be multiplied by either the current draw colour in the case of "draw_text()" or whichever manually-specified colours were passed to those other text functions

• Also note that the drop shadow offset is affected by both the scale and rotation of the text that is drawn (i.e. an offset value of 10 pixels will become 100 pixels if the text is drawn at 10-times scale, and rotating the text by 45 degrees will cause the shadow offset to also be rotated 45 degrees)
• You can also use the new font_enable_effects(), which has been added for controlling all of this at runtime - see the runtime notes for more on how to do this
Feather: Ability To Ignore/Modify Rules Checks For Specific Items
<ul>

• Extended the "// feather" directives by adding an "in" suffix, which takes a case-insensitive filepath string (matching the asset browser's folder structure for your project), plus the rule(s) you wish to be ignored
• For example, you could create a blank new script and put it at the root of your Asset Browser tree and then type in commands like the following:
• // feather ignore GM2017 in *: ignore all Naming Rule violations in the whole project
• // feather ignore GM1064 in ./*: ignore GM1064 in the current folder and all subfolders
• // feather use type-errors in /Objects/System/*: set the profile to type-errors in specifically the Objects/System group
• // feather use all in /Objects/System/obj_controller: set the profile to all for the obj_controller Object

• Note that if you have two rules which affect the same path/object, then there is no guaranteeing which will be applied - and if you have lots of custom rules in your script then this may cause a performance overhead
• Also, be aware that you cannot use .. to go up the filepath

In these August 2023.800 Beta releases there are: New functions for rotating and colouring particles and others which allow you to burst the particles previously created in the editor; IPv6 support on many more platforms (some consoles do not support IPv6); functions for controlling the mouse on some platforms; and many other fixes and improvements

As always, please do check your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions before doing any builds - you can see our Required SDKs FAQ and the various platform setup guides that page links to in order to get all of this information at any time.

See below for runtime changes/fixes since 2023.6.0 and then check the IDE Release Notes for some very important changes you need to be aware of.

Changes Since Beta Runtime 406

New SDF Font Rendering Effects

  • Added support for three new rendering effects now available in-game: "Crisp Glow", "Outline", "Drop Shadow" (each of which can be configured in the Font Editor also)
  • font_enable_effects(font, enable, optional_params) has been added for controlling all of this at runtime - all effects require this to be enabled on a font for the effect to be visible (it will also show an error if it is passed a font which is an IDE-generated font which did not have SDF enabled)
  • "optional_params" must be a struct and can contain any (or all) of the following fields:
    • "thickness": the thickness modifier for the font - this can be a value from -32 to 32 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • "coreColour": the core colour of the font
    • "coreAlpha: the alpha of the core part of the font
    • ""glowEnable": enable\disable the glow effect on the font
    • ""glowStart": the distance where the glow effect starts fading out - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowEnd": the distance where the glow effect finishes fading to fully transparent - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowColour": the glow colour of the font
    • ""glowAlpha": the glow alpha of the font
    • ""outlineEnable": enables\disables the outline effect on the font
    • ""outlineDistance": the distance that the outline extends from the edge of each glyph - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""outlineColour": the outline colour of the font
    • ""outlineAlpha": the outline alpha of the font
    • ""dropShadowEnable": enable\disable the drop shadow effect on the font
    • ""dropShadowSoftness": the width of the penumbra region of the shadow - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""dropShadowOffsetX": the X offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowOffsetY": the Y offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowColour": the drop shadow colour of the font
    • ""dropShadowAlpha": the drop shadow alpha of the font
  • Be aware that when drawing text using the standard text drawing functions the colour values specified for the core, outline and glow colours will be multiplied by either the current draw colour in the case of "draw_text()" or whichever manually-specified colours were passed to those other text functions
  • Also note that the drop shadow offset is affected by both the scale and rotation of the text that is drawn (i.e. an offset value of 10 pixels will become 100 pixels if the text is drawn at 10-times scale, and rotating the text by 45 degrees will cause the shadow offset to also be rotated 45 degrees)

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay

  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)

New Particle Functions

  • part_system_colour(ps,colour,alpha) This function can be used to change colour and alpha with which the particle system is blended
  • part_system_angle(ps,angle) This function can be used to change the rotation of the particle system
  • part_system_global_space(ps, enable) using which you can enable global space particles. When enabled, particles keep their position and direction when the particle system is moved or rotated.
  • part_emitter_delay(ps,ind,delay_min,delay_max,delay_unit) using which you can configure delay before an emitter burst first particles
  • part_emitter_interval(ps,ind,interval_min,interval_max,interval_unit) using which you can configure the interval between following bursts
  • part_emitter_enable(ps,ind,enable) Emitters that are disabled are not updated nor rendered and they don't spawn new particles until they're enabled again
  • part_emitter_relative(ps,em,enable) which is used to enable/disable relative mode for an emitter, which means the number of particles it bursts or streams becomes relative to its area
  • part_type_size_x(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle) This function is used to configure particle size similarly to part_type_size(), except only for the x axis. You can use function part_type_size_y() to configure the size on the y axis separately as well
  • part_type_size_y(ind,size_min,size_max,size_incr,size_wiggle)
  • part_type_subimage(ind,subimg) This function can be used to set a particle type to use a custom sub-image (frame) of a sprite. If the particle's sprite is animated, then this sub-image will be used as the starting frame of the animation
  • particle_get_info(partsys) will now also give you information regarding the above-added functionality

New Mouse Functions

  • window_mouse_set_locked(enable) With this function you can enable or disable mouse lock. When enabled, the mouse cursor is hidden and locked at the center of the window. When disabled, the mouse cursor is shown and unlocked. While the cursor is locked, you can still use functions window_mouse_get_delta_x() and window_mouse_get_delta_y() to retrieve how much has it moved since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_locked() Returns whether the mouse cursor was locked using function window_mouse_set_locked
  • window_mouse_get_delta_x() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the x axis since the last frame
  • window_mouse_get_delta_y() Returns how many pixels has the mouse cursor moved on the y axis since the last frame

Misc New Functions

  • gpu_get_depth() This function returns the current depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, it will be equal to the current layer's depth, but can be changed using gpu_set_depth
  • gpu_set_depth(depth) This function can be used to change the depth (z coordinate) for 2d drawing functions. By default, layer's depth will be used. Note that GameMaker will only change the depth when it starts drawing a new layer, so you may want to restore the original value (from gpu_get_depth) after you're done drawing
  • effect_create_layer(layer_id,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect on a specified layer. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large
  • effect_create_depth(depth,kind,x,y,size,colour) With this function you can create a simple effect at a specified depth. If the effect is anything other ef_rain or ef_snow then you can define an x/y position to create the effect, and the size can be a value of 0, 1, or 2, where 0 is small, 1 is medium and 2 is large

New SDF Font Rendering Effects

  • Added support for three new rendering effects now available in-game: "Crisp Glow", "Outline", "Drop Shadow" (each of which can be configured in the Font Editor also)
  • font_enable_effects(font, enable, optional_params) has been added for controlling all of this at runtime - all effects require this to be enabled on a font for the effect to be visible (it will also show an error if it is passed a font which is an IDE-generated font which did not have SDF enabled)
  • "optional_params" must be a struct and can contain any (or all) of the following fields:
    • "thickness": the thickness modifier for the font - this can be a value from -32 to 32 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • "coreColour": the core colour of the font
    • "coreAlpha: the alpha of the core part of the font
    • ""glowEnable": enable\disable the glow effect on the font
    • ""glowStart": the distance where the glow effect starts fading out - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowEnd": the distance where the glow effect finishes fading to fully transparent - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""glowColour": the glow colour of the font
    • ""glowAlpha": the glow alpha of the font
    • ""outlineEnable": enables\disables the outline effect on the font
    • ""outlineDistance": the distance that the outline extends from the edge of each glyph - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""outlineColour": the outline colour of the font
    • ""outlineAlpha": the outline alpha of the font
    • ""dropShadowEnable": enable\disable the drop shadow effect on the font
    • ""dropShadowSoftness": the width of the penumbra region of the shadow - this can be a value from 0 to 64 (values outside this range will be clamped)
    • ""dropShadowOffsetX": the X offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowOffsetY": the Y offset of the drop shadow in pixels
    • ""dropShadowColour": the drop shadow colour of the font

  • Also note that the drop shadow offset is affected by both the scale and rotation of the text that is drawn (i.e. an offset value of 10 pixels will become 100 pixels if the text is drawn at 10-times scale, and rotating the text by 45 degrees will cause the shadow offset to also be rotated 45 degrees)

  • dbg_view(name,visible) Declare a new debug view that can be accessed from the debug overlay

  • dbg_drop_down(dbgref,specifier,[label]) Creates a dropdown for an integer value within the current debug section - values and names for the dropdown are declared as a comma-delimited string where integer values can also be specified after a colon symbol (so "Zero,One:10,Two:20" will create a 3-entry dropdown that will set the variable to the value 0, 10 or 20 depending on which one is selected)

"Compressor" Audio Effect

  • A compressor applies variable gain-reduction to an input signal - the reduction applied corresponds to the amount that the signal exceeds the 'threshold' of the effect, as well as the compression 'ratio' chosen
  • When the signal exceeds the threshold the excess of the threshold will be reduced by the ratio (this is a "downward" compressor type)
  • Gain reduction is not applied or released instantaneously, but instead ramps up and down according to 'attack' and 'release' parameters (lower values specify more responsive compression, while higher values specify less responsive compression)
  • Accordingly, there are new entries in the AudioEffect struct to allow for this effect:
    • "attack": The response time to apply the effect
    • "ingain": The input gain scalar
    • "outgain": The output gain scalar
    • "ratio": The compression ratio
    • "release": The response time to stop applying the effect
    • "threshold": The gain threshold over which the effect is applied
  • And for the AudioEffectType enum: "Compressor" (which equals 11)

More IPv6 Support

  • Multicast traffic is also now supported using IPv6 - again, everything except Switch, PS4, and PS5 (which do not support IPv6 at this time)
  • Adds a pair of network_set_config() constants ("network_config_enable_multicast" and "network_config_disable_multicast") to enable/disable the new multicast functionality on a per-socket basis:
  • When multicast is enabled on a UDP socket, it will be joined to the all-hosts (FF02::1) multicast group on each network interface in the system and calls to network_send_broadcast() will transmit multicast packets on those groups in addition to IPv4 broadcasts
  • In general, games doing LAN discovery using network_send_broadcast() will want to turn this on; however, your game must be written in such a way to handle receiving the same packet multiple times from multiple IPs (i.e. the host's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses) and disambiguate these from other hosts (e.g. by embedding a unique value in the packet for each sender)
