First, this version sees a major milestone for GameMaker Studio: a fully dedicated Mac version. This has long been a desire of both YoYo Games and the community, and we are excited to welcome this version into the GameMaker family. The great news for both Windows and Mac users is that it is all part of the same license - buy any module and it will work on Windows and Mac with that one purchase. So if you're a Mac user who has been "stuck on Windows" or using a VM there's no better time to swap to the Mac native IDE!
Hotfix 2 Changes
<ul>
• Fixed crashes seen when using the debugger in the Mac IDE on lower-spec Macs - please report if you see this, including your Mac's specs
• Fixed an issue with importing large sprites
• Fixed an issue with incorrect newer mono files/folders being used by the Mac IDE
• Added a few missing manual fixes, including more debugger info
Hotfix 1 Changes
<ul>
• Fixed the memory leak when using nested #regions in the code editor in 2.1.0.204
• Fixed an issue seen internally where building for Android can now get the runtime stuck, preventing further runs
• Fixed an issue seen internally where stopping a build just as the game was about to start could cause IDE "unstable" error
General IDE Changes
<ul>
• Added a fix for Marketplace demo/tutorial downloads not working in 2.0.7 if you browsed the Marketplace rather than using the Demos/Tutorials part of the start page
• Redesigned the login dialogue to enable those who need to specify authentication details for their web proxy connection

• Redesigned the target manager dialogue to flip the column order for worker and platform, so this should make it clearer when a worker is required and which platforms you have access to as part of your licence
• Updated the Micro Web server to allow for simpler bandwidth throttling, and show loading of assets using a progress bar
• Added into Game Options > Main a checkbox for if you want to change scripts/events to be DnD TM or not from that point, so now you can very easily toggle existing projects
Integrated Debugger
<ul>
• We've now not only fully integrated the debugger, but also added several improvements to it, giving a simpler, more user-friendly layout
• We added a very handy FPS graph and message timeline window - use debug_event() and show_debug_message() to send messages to this window
• You can also now hover over variables in scripts within the debugger workspace to preview their values
• You'll find a new tutorial all about the new debugger on the Tutorials page of the Start Page now
• Please note there is a known issue listed below for some users of the Mac IDE
Resource Tree Enhancements
<ul>
• The resource tree has had a make-over, with guidelines and resource type icons now on by default
• Preferences have been added to allow you to turn these off again, as well as giving a huge range of customisation options
• So now you can make the resource tree look how you want - even if that happens to be rainbow Comic Sans!
"Recent Windows" Window
<ul>
• Found by default under the resource tree, this window helps you quickly navigate throughout the sections of your project you are working on at that time
• Preferences have been added to configure the behaviour of the list, so try these and see what works best for you
• Please note it will only appear automatically in newer project layouts, but you can open it via the Windows menu in older ones
Code-Folding Support
<ul>
• Lastly, we've also added code-folding to the code editor using the new #region and #endregion tags
• Helps enormously when dealing with larger scripts, but can also be used to "recreate" the 1.4 look of multiple code actions in one event
Known Issues
<ul>
• Welcome Page is disabled during start-up - it can still be accessed via the Help menu, so new users can still get to these videos and links
• Some lower-specced Macs have issues with the game starting/closing during debugger sessions, which causes the IDE to crash
• "Save As" and "Export" are not handling all supplementary options files (typically console-specific files and icons)
• Some online connectivity issues - IDE occasionally thinking it's offline
• Runtime download/activation has been seen to crash the IDE occasionally during subsequent startup
• Closing and reopening the Marketplace tab can cause issues downloading some assets thereafter, need to restart GMS2 to fix
• Dead instances of Window's RuntimeBroker application can block attempts to use the manual in the IDE - just get a white page
• Still looking into reports of offline not working for the full 30 days - usually a lot sooner than this if you get this issue
• UWP building errors over missing makepri.exe if you only have Windows SDK v10.0.15063.0 and not the older versions also
• Added better exception handling and logging, so if you get a crash please send us your %programdata%\GameMakerStudio2\ui.log file

• IDE startup sequence should be more robust and getting stuck on a white screen at startup is fixed.
• Removed the Steam online check added into 2.0.6, following feedback from users that this caused more issues than it solved.
• Added a fix for getting the runtime the IDE expects each time you start the IDE.
• The Start Page has been rewritten and is much faster and smoother.
• New image editor Blur effect added.
• New image editor Reverse Frames command added.
• New build timer system has been added to the notification panel during builds.
• Newly-imported 1.4 projects will now have their NSIS script file replaced. NSIS build fixes make the old ones incompatible.
• Support has been added for those who need to specify authentication details for their web proxy connection.
Remote Worker System
• Our new Remote Worker tool has been added for Mac IDE users to be able to use a PC to build the Windows-based targets.
• Because of this, a new first column has been added into Target Manager for controlling the device a build takes place on.
Runner Changes
<ul>
• Lots of HTML5 bug fixes.
• buffer_load_async() now works in HTML5, and will now load pure binary data.
• buffer_md5() on HTML5 now returns exactly the same as the native versions, not an HTML5-specific value.
Known Issues

• There are currently intermittent issues opening Explorer file dialogs, which will cause the IDE to hang. This appears to stem from a Windows security update, as other applications report the same issue.
• If you are experiencing this, then please make sure to update Windows to the latest set of patches - while this currently hasn't fixed the issue, it has lessened the likelihood of seeing this.
• If you experience the above failure, you will need to kill the IDE using the task manager, as the broken file dialog will have stolen all input and so the IDE cannot be closed using normal methods.
• There are still some intermittent online connectivity issues - IDE occasionally thinking it's offline.
• Runtime download/activation has been seen to crash the IDE occasionally during subsequent startup.

<ul>

<ul>

• Several Android keystore-generation issues

• Many, many HTML5 in-game fixes

• Mac IDE: Preference to delete old runtimes when installing a new one stops the IDE responding for a long time before it finishes

• DnD™: Lots of DnD™ improvements, including icons on the Actions window, and a simple "collapse all" on the menu
• Image Editor: Ellipse and rectangle tools can now be sized from the middle by pressing ALT
• Image Editor: Ellipse and rectangle tools can now be transparent without error and have been optimised
• Image Editor: New "colour replace" tool added
• Image Editor: New "non-contiguous" mode added to magic wand
• Image Editor: The rotate tool now does "any" angle. 90-degree rotate is still on the key shortcut (z)
• Image Editor: Brush scale is now unfiltered (press and hold SHIFT+Z)
• Room Editor: Rectangle, line and fill tile tools added (these do not yet do auto-tiling)
• Room Editor: Tilemap rendering and memory optimisations for very large rooms
• Code Editor: Syntax errors can now be seen by mousing over the ! in the code editor gutter
• Preferences: New preference to carry on having Syntax Errors window pop up on each error
• Preferences: New "DPI Override" preference which allows you to shrink or grow UI layouts without changing Windows zoom level
• Sprite Editor: There is now a new "automatic" mode for collision masks, auto-resizes when the image does
• Debugger: Variable views for Instance, Local and Global window types have been fixed
Known Issues
• Source control is still not yet available. This will hopefully be resolved soon
• Mac YYC is not signing app store builds correctly
• Debugger still has issues variables showing as "undefined" in the Watch window
• Editing paths within the Room Editor is buggy
• More work still needs to be done to improve readability of the GML code produced by DnD™
• See more on the "report a bug" page
• Added a quick check that our installer deployed the Visual C++ redistributables successfully - will say to reinstall, rather than allowing a crash on startup
• New way of downloading runtimes so it's faster and more reliable - also resumes downloads rather than always restarting
• A runtime installation issue has been fixed that would have caused crashes or the inability to test projects
• Inside a code window, F7/F8 will now allow you to quickly adjust preference for the size of the font for all code windows
• There is now a Preference to let you swap zooming from CTRL+WHEEL to just WHEEL (scrolling will then be on CTRL+WHEEL)
• There is now a Game Option for paid users to disable sending game statistics for that project
• Included files have now been fixed and have been added back in
• Disappearing Event contents when you rename the object in the resource tree has been fixed
• A font-generation issue which caused fuzzy and mis-aligned text in-game has been fixed
• Shift+Backspace now does a backspace
• Fixed variables with square brackets to be added properly by autocomplete
• Fixed crashes when Ctrl+C to copy a frame in the image editor when the image has multple frames
• Changed the "View" properties in the room editor to say "Camera" to clear up confusion
• Fixed sprites defaulting to "precise (slow)" - they're now rectangle
Known Issues
• Creating, renaming or adding an existing extension is currently disabled (will still import as part of a 1.4 project)
• Built-in Source control is currently disabled
• Building a Steam-enabled Mac doesn't copy the Steamworks file - you can copy this yourself as a workaround
• Known issues are also now shown on the "report a bug" page

• New sound mixer for volume adjusting of all sounds and music
• Fully skinnable UI
• Multilingual capable UI

2023.11 brings lots of behind-the-scenes performance improvements to both the IDE and Runtime; various new functions have been added to expand what you can do with buffers and rooms; following on from the SDF Effects added last release, you can now apply these effects to text tracks within your Sequences; you can now create your own Game Strip projects (and there is a new template project in the IDE you can use to learn about Game Strips); and there is a very large number of bug fixes and also some of the popular community requests since our public request system was revealed a few months ago.

For all the public general changes and bug fixes added for 2023.11 click here to open the Bugs Milestone page and for all of the public new features click here to open the Feature Requests Milestone page

Before You Update

  • Always ensure your SDKs and other external tools are the correct versions for this release before doing any builds - Required SDKs FAQ
  • Also, if you use antivirus/antimalware or any restricted user permissions on your machine, always check your external settings allow for this new release to work properly - User Permissions and Internet Access Required by GameMaker

Changes To The Release Notes

  • It also shows you what else is intended for the Monthly release and is yet to be fixed or implemented (the "Open" list on each page)
  • You can expand the "Show More" near the top of the page to read the overview/summarised information about what is in the release
  • Both lists will stay up-to-date during Beta periods as features are added and bugs are found, and so this is the new way of seeing all of the "Headline Known Issues" during Betas also
  • To see what is already planned for upcoming releases or (in future!) went into old releases, you can do this on the Milestones list pages also: Bugs - Feature Requests

2024.200 Betas bring: a lot of bug fixes and performance improvements already (especially in-game, but also a number of stability and project-loading fixes in the IDE). In terms of new features and notable changes, you will also find: the code editor and compiler will now better catch functions which have not had all required arguments provided; #macro definitions now support inheritance (as was always implied by the IDE using a tree for the configs editor); Tilemaps are now compressed in your rooms; Static functions now have non-anonymous names to help with debugging issues and there have been various fixes to the Debugger itself; there is a new gml_pragma() option "optimise" for HTML5 games to turn on/off further JS optimisations; a new Gaussian Blur filter has been added for you to use in your games; fixed that borderless games would still resize themselves when using async dialogs, despite not being exclusive fullscreen; fixed issues with building Extensions on case-sensitive operating systems; and there have been some tweaks and improvements to the in-IDE bug reporting tool.

This month’s runtime update introduces Opera GX YYC support for everyone; enables video playback functionality on almost all platforms (UWP is not being implemented); two new audio falloff models have been added: audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled; and all Ubuntu builds have changed to use Steam’s new Linux runtime tools and so you can now create a more consistent cross-distro “AppImage” package if you wish

Accordingly, OperaGX has a brand new setup guide so you can configure YYC builds and the Ubuntu guide has been updated to state the extra packages you need. Please see their guides and the Required SDKs FAQ before attempting to build for these platforms.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Support For Opera GX Builds Using YYC

  • We have added the ability for everyone to run games on Opera GX using YYC, improving the in-game performance compared to the VM output type
  • Your build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the new setup guide before attempting any builds
  • Be aware that using YYC to build your game will automatically disable subst during that build (it simply ignores whatever your Preference is currently set to), as this would otherwise cause an error with the Emscripten SDK

Added Support For Video Playback

  • You can now play video on all platforms apart from UWP and Xbox One using XDK (using GDK is fine) - you can also pause, resume, seek to a specific moment, get the duration/current position, and modify the volume, amongst other things
  • Note that before including any videos in your games you must ensure that you have valid licensing rights to distribute videos in that file/codec format!
  • Please see the manual for the full information, as there are a number of new functions and constants which have been added, plus you will now get async events for when videos start/stop playing
  • Also be aware that not all platforms render the colours of videos in the same way, so you need to check which format is correct for the current platform in-game and draw the video accordingly, otherwise your picture will probably be coloured red - again, see the manual page for video_get_format() for the full info

Changed Ubuntu Builds To Use The Steam Runtime

  • Building any non-ARM projects for the Ubuntu target now uses the Steam Runtime as part of this process
  • This removes a lot of the library/dependency issues that come from different Linux distributions and updates
  • You will be required to install the Steam SDK on your Ubuntu build machine, so please see the Required SDKs FAQ and the Ubuntu setup guide that page links to before trying to do any builds

Added Support For Ubuntu AppImage Packages

  • Further to the above Ubuntu change, we have added a new option to build AppImage packages when building for Ubuntu (you can still build a .zip also)
  • An AppImage is a distribution-agnostic means of distributing software on Linux and your Appimage will automatically contain all the libraries and binaries to run your game on the system, so players just need to run the one file you give them (akin to a macOS .app bundle package)
  • The AppImage type has become the default choice when clicking Run/Create Exe; however, ARM is not currently supported and so the runtime will fall back to old build system and a .zip
  • Your Ubuntu build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the setup guide before attempting any builds

More Audio Falloff Options

  • Two new audio falloff models have been added for use with the function audio_falloff_set_model):
  • audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled
  • These behave similarly to audio_falloff_inverse_distance_clamped and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_clamped, but have been scaled in such a way that sounds are guaranteed to fall off entirely by the maximum distance

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: [tvOS] GameCenter extension now works on tvOS [Note that you need the new version of the extension also to get the full fix]
  • Building Projects: [Ubuntu] Steamworks extension no longer causes projects to fail to build if the project name contains spaces [Note that you need the new version of the extension also to get the full fix]
  • In-Game: Windows app store games containing the GDK extension now close properly when requested [Note that you need the new version of the extension also to get the full fix]
  • Using the "Steam alternative launcher" Game Option will now automatically disable subst during that build (it simply ignores whatever your Preference is currently set to), as we have determined that this is the root cause of a number of in-game errors with files not being found
  • OperaGX games now write their save data in a game-specific subfolder - you should not notice any change, as it will look at the old directory if a save is not found and then save it to the new location later, but this is a fix for preventing accidental overwriting by other games
  • In-Game: Some game's rooms loaded more slowly and sprite_pretech() took longer when built in the last couple of releases due to QOI decompression time, as was most commonly seen on some Android devices when using YYC [Note: Use the new Texture Groups Editor dropdown and select the QOI option to get the full fix - see the IDE notes for more info]
  • In-Game: int64() now correctly floors values instead of rounding them in previous releases

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: Typing an incorrect number of digits for CSS colours no longer results in the error displaying twice

This month’s runtime update introduces Opera GX YYC support for everyone; enables video playback functionality on almost all platforms (UWP is not being implemented); two new audio falloff models have been added: audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled; and all Ubuntu builds have changed to use Steam’s new Linux runtime tools and so you can now create a more consistent cross-distro “AppImage” package if you wish

Accordingly, OperaGX has a brand new setup guide so you can configure YYC builds and the Ubuntu guide has been updated to state the extra packages you need. Please see their guides and the Required SDKs FAQ before attempting to build for these platforms.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Support For Opera GX Builds Using YYC

  • We have added the ability for everyone to run games on Opera GX using YYC, improving the in-game performance compared to the VM output type
  • Your build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the new setup guide before attempting any builds
  • Be aware that using YYC to build your game will automatically disable subst during that build (it simply ignores whatever your Preference is currently set to), as this would otherwise cause an error with the Emscripten SDK

Added Support For Video Playback

  • You can now play video on all platforms apart from UWP and Xbox One using XDK (using GDK is fine) - you can also pause, resume, seek to a specific moment, get the duration/current position, and modify the volume, amongst other things
  • Note that before including any videos in your games you must ensure that you have valid licensing rights to distribute videos in that file/codec format!
  • Please see the manual for the full information, as there are a number of new functions and constants which have been added, plus you will now get async events for when videos start/stop playing
  • Also be aware that not all platforms render the colours of videos in the same way, so you need to check which format is correct for the current platform in-game and draw the video accordingly, otherwise your picture will probably be coloured red - again, see the manual page for video_get_format() for the full info

Changed Ubuntu Builds To Use The Steam Runtime

  • Building any non-ARM projects for the Ubuntu target now uses the Steam Runtime as part of this process
  • This removes a lot of the library/dependency issues that come from different Linux distributions and updates
  • You will be required to install the Steam SDK on your Ubuntu build machine, so please see the Required SDKs FAQ and the Ubuntu setup guide that page links to before trying to do any builds

Added Support For Ubuntu AppImage Packages

  • Further to the above Ubuntu change, we have added a new option to build AppImage packages when building for Ubuntu (you can still build a .zip also)
  • An AppImage is a distribution-agnostic means of distributing software on Linux and your Appimage will automatically contain all the libraries and binaries to run your game on the system, so players just need to run the one file you give them (akin to a macOS .app bundle package)
  • The AppImage type has become the default choice when clicking Run/Create Exe; however, ARM is not currently supported and so the runtime will fall back to old build system and a .zip
  • Your Ubuntu build machine will require some extra tools to support this, so please see the setup guide before attempting any builds

More Audio Falloff Options

  • Two new audio falloff models have been added for use with the function audio_falloff_set_model):
  • audio_falloff_inverse_distance_scaled and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_scaled
  • These behave similarly to audio_falloff_inverse_distance_clamped and audio_falloff_exponent_distance_clamped, but have been scaled in such a way that sounds are guaranteed to fall off entirely by the maximum distance

2022.2 introduces a new ability to create text tracks/instances and animate these within your sequences, then draw the text later in-game. It also changes a long-time GameMaker behaviour that arrays will make and edit a copy when you pass an array into a function, and so we have added an option to maintain the old way if you want. As well as these two important additions, there is the ability to send text to a secure websocket, to define colours in the code editor using CSS web standard values and for this to appear correctly in your game, and also a range of important bug fixes.

Steamworks users: Please also be aware that you now need to use our Steamworks extension from the Marketplace and include this inside your projects if you wish to publish games to Steam - the runner has been cleaned of all its old in-built functions, and so there are no longer Game Options or most Preferences for Steam setup, as this is all now configured for your project within the extension once you have added it.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since 2022.2.0

  • In-Game: [Windows] Fixed that Windows 7 users would get a MFCreateDXGISurfaceBuffer error in Runner.exe when using 2022.2.0 runtimes to build their project
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed a couple of issues with Included Files which could cause your game to get stuck on an "All downloads complete" page

2022.2.0

Added Support For Text Tracks In Sequences

  • You can now add text tracks/instances into your sequences by clicking the "T" text tool in the canvas toolbox, edit the text via the new text layer inspector (which will open automatically when creating a new text item in your sequence) and animate it via the dope sheet, then draw it in-game later on
  • Note that at this time there is no ability to later override the contents of the text in-game, but this will come sometime in the future

Added A Toggle For If Arrays Should Copy-On-Write

  • There is a new game option for whether your games should continue to copy arrays when writing to them or not, which may give performance/memory improvements in your games
  • Note that when opening/importing existing projects this will default to being enabled (maintaining the old behaviour of doing the copy) and for new projects this will default to off (the new behaviour of not copying)

Added Support For "text" WebSocket messages

  • network_send_raw() now has an optional "options" parameter which can be set to "network_send_binary" or "network_send_text"
  • This will force that mode when sending messages on a WebSocket socket (Binary remains the default if the parameter is not specified)
  • Similarly, the matching async_load map has a new "message_type" field for all received WebSocket messages, which will also be set to network_send_binary or network_send_text

Added Support For Defining In-Game Colours Using CSS Values

  • You can now insert CSS colours into your GML code by using a '#' symbol followed by 6 digit hex code - e.g., var col = #F0F8FF; // AliceBlue
  • Be aware, though, that this actually sets col using the correct format for GMS2 (which is $AABBGGRR, while CSS colours are in the form #RRGGBB), so the debugger and elsewhere in GMS2 will show col as $00FFF8F0 (or 16775408 in decimal) rather than the #F0F8FF you might have expected
  • Note that this format is usable any place where a number can be used, as GML colours are just numbers, so these hex values can be used in more places than just defining a colour

New Functionality Within Xbox Builds

  • Game Options for the GDK target now has a new checkbox for enabling “Simplified User Model” functionality (defaults to off), which will then toggle the user model in your games
  • Game Options labels for the Xbox stat-system names have been reworded to match Microsoft’s current naming conventions, plus the settings have been expanded to allow mixing systems (again, to match what Microsoft allows nowadays)
  • xboxone_get_achievement(user, achievement) can now be called to query the progress of the chosen achievement - this one works on XDK and GDK
  • Added 120Hz support for Xbox Series X/S
  • Please see the Xbox docs for more information on all of these

Removed In-Built Steamworks Functions

  • Removed the old code inside the runner for all Steam functions (which relied on a very old Steamworks SDK), in favour of a new extension which can be updated more easily in future
  • This means the runner now does not always ship with this functionality, regardless of whether you were using Steam in your games or not
  • For this reason, many of the IDE settings for enabling and configuring Steamworks are now gone, in favour of you editing these values inside the extension once it is added to your project
  • The new Steamworks extension will be added to the Marketplace soon - again, to be clear: you will require this extension in your project and to configure some of its setup values if you want to enable Steam in your projects going forward

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: Splash screen images would only work in previous versions if it was a genuine .png file you supplied in Game Options (as opposed to some other format, but renamed “.png”); however, GMS2 will now detect a mismatch and convert incorrect file types
  • In-Game: Precise collisions on instances with bounds extending beyond their image size now return a hit when overlapping just the bbox [note that compatibility mode is deliberately unchanged and so "still has this bug"]
  • In-Game: HTML5's json_encode() will now write out bools values as bools rather than as the strings "true" and "false" (with the quotes) - this is so it can be read easily by Windows' json_decode(), but you may need to revise your own code here if you were expecting a string
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Instances created in-game now have the same draw order as Windows, etc.
  • In-Game: Added interpolation across audio_queue_sound() buffer boundaries, which avoids "ticks" when one sound stops and the next begins

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: Custom noise PNG made in Paint.net causes builds to fail
  • Building Projects: [YYC] Fixed that using a pre-inc/dec expression as a function argument would causes build to fail in 2022.1
  • Building Projects: Android now more reliably stops the build timer/process automatically when a compile error occurs, rather than always having to click the stop button yourself before you could build again
  • Building: [Ubuntu IDE] Android YYC builds no longer fail because of case-sensitivity issues with gradlew
  • Building Projects: [macOS] "Allow Incoming/Outgoing network connections" values are now correctly written to the Xcode project again
  • Building Projects: [HTML5] Fixed a caching issue if a different layer effect is selected in a room between runs
  • Building Projects: [Windows IDE] iOS extension app delegate class names are now correctly maintained during the build
  • Building Projects [TVOS]: Fixed silent crashes during startup when running on simulators, even with empty projects
  • Building Projects: [Ubuntu YYC] Builds no longer fail due to ssh error "The client is already connected"
  • Note: Also made a fix for Ubuntu YYC console logging not working in real-time
  • Building Projects: [XDK YYC] Fixed an issue where projects containing functions which have multiple unused arguments might have failed with the error “Fatal error LNK1248: image size (...) exceeds maximum allowable size (FFFFFFFF)”
  • Command Line Builds: Made Igor's /ssdk option optional
  • In-Game: Fixed a code error when using floor()/ceil()/round() on both indexes of a DS grid if that grid is also inside an array
  • In-Game: Single-Layer Effects are now drawn correctly when using custom cameras also
  • In-Game: Added support for PS4/PS5 stick deadzone values smaller than +/- 0.10 from 0, so now it will smoothly increase from 0, rather than waiting until -0.1/0.1 before anything happens
  • In-Game: async_load map now supports much longer strings that 16384 bytes for the message when using websockets
  • In-Game: [YYC] Fixed that Switch cases which compared against struct values did not work
  • In-Game: [YYC] Fixed that using the $ accessor for some variables with the same name as built-in variables would always return undefined in previous versions
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Creating a static variable after another static variable no longer causes an "unexpected token" error
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Creating a static array with [] after another array no longer causes an unwanted extra comma to appear in the source code [2022.1.0 had a partial fix, but this route still remained]
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed that a runtime exception could be encountered after a Draw GUI event when dealing with textures or calling vertex_submit()
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed mouse_x/y to no longer return NaN in some cases, as this would causes crashes if the NaN was passed to other functions
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Instances can no longer be destroyed twice in Destroy events (which caused a variety of issues if you had accidentally done this in previous versions)
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Websocket urls containing paths no longer incorrectly moves the port suffix to the end of the whole URL
  • In-Game: [macOS/iOS] Fixed that all layer... getter property functions would silently crash the game if passed a method as the element id
  • In-Game: [iOS] Passing a bool into an extension function now works correctly, rather than always resulting in 0 as it did previously
  • In-Game: [iOS] achievement_post_score() had multiple issues with the current extension [note that the fix also requires the use of an extension already updated since the bug was filed]
  • In-Game: add_sprite() no longer silently crashes the runner when trying to load a gif format image
  • In-Game: add_sprite() also no longer silently crashes the runner if passed a gif image where the final frame fails to be detected properly [different issue to the one above]
  • In-Game: [Windows] audio_create_sync_group() now respects its "loop" argument
  • In-Game: audio_is_playing() now returns the correct value for .mp3 files
  • In-Game: audio_sound_set_track_position() behaviour no longer differs between Windows/HTML5, depending on if called before or after audio_play_sound()
  • In-Game: file_attributes(..., fa_directory) result is no longer inverted
  • In-Game: is_method() now returns accurate and consistent results for built-in functions between Windows/HTML5
  • In-Game: layer_background_index() now caps the value to the number of frames in the sprite and so wraps back to the start of the sprite correctly
  • In-Game: [HTML5] layer_sequence_y/layer_sequence_x() now moves any clipping masks in the sequence as well
  • In-Game: [HTML5] layer_set_target_room() now affects all later layer_...() calls
  • In-Game: [Windows] network_connect_raw_async() now fires the expected async event when it should
  • In-Game: script_execute_ext() now calls in-built functions referenced in an array correctly again
  • In-Game: [YYC] sprite_nineslice_create() now works again on these targets
  • In-Game: [Switch] video_set_volume() is now supported

The 2022.1 runtime changes the format of all images in-game to lower build times and package sizes, adds the ability to connect to secure websockets on almost all platforms, fixes a performance issue building large projects on the Mac IDE and enables simulator use on an M1-equipped Mac, as well as raising the version of Gradle used during Android builds and introducing support for the newest SDK/NDK versions.

Note that there is also quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs. You should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix; however, there is also a new compatibility mode in Game Options for if your existing projects need to maintain the old way. More information on this change can be found on its page in the manual.

As well as all of the above, this version includes new functions to apply a filter/effect target to a single specified layer and to toggle this effect on/off at runtime, and enables fx_create() to dynamically add your chosen filters into your game builds without you having to create a matching layer in your room first. The new runtimes also remove more stale code for old extensions/features no longer supported and accordingly trims down some package sizes a little, whilst also fixing a number of the top issues reported in 2.3.7

Be aware that this release ends support for our Remote Worker tool and so this is not part of the IDE installer any more. Going forward, please just use the Windows and Mac IDEs directly on your machines.

2022.1.0

Changed Bounding Box Values To Be Floats And Added A Compatibility Collisions Mode

  • There is quite a substantial change to collisions, as bounding box values are now floats rather than ints - this increases accuracy and fixes a number of long-standing bugs (see below for some of the bugs fixed), but you should test your games carefully, as you may need to make changes to your code in response to this fix.
  • See the manual page for this change for more information
  • However, for existing projects where you do not wish to make the change or it’s not practical to refactor, there is a new Game Option (so you need to enable this in the IDE to get the fix) which tells the runner to treat bounding boxes as inclusive and round() them to .000 so they act as if integers, which is how collisions worked in previous GMS2 releases
  • Note that we would recommend going forward that you use the newer float bounding box calculations system and generate your sprites and code accordingly, rather than always ticking this option in new projects

Changed In-Game Sprites To Use QOI Image Format

  • Games now use the QOI image format with BZ2 compression, which is smaller than PNG (we saw in our testing that game packages are now around 80% of the size they would be in 2.3.7) and quicker to decompress
  • You should also see your project build times are quite a bit shorter in this release (again, we saw potentially around 50% quicker, but quite how much depends on the size of your project and the number of sprites, obviously)
  • If for some reason your game now fails to build or takes noticeably longer than 2.3.7 requires, please let us know via a bug report ticket and remember to attach a download of your project so we can check why it has an issue

Updated the version of Gradle that Android builds will use

  • Should offer better support for some extensions (particularly for those writing new extensions themselves), but we have also added support for a compatibility mode with older versions of Gradle/Java also
  • Please note that Gradle installs its own updates and this change may require a download during your first/next Android build - ensure you have internet access if your compiler log says Gradle needs this
  • Our current Marketplace assets do not require this change and so are not being updated at this time, but eventually some may require it in future

Added Functions For Toggling Filters In-Game

  • Added new functions to enable\disable the existing fx values on layers (without having to remove the filter from the layers) and also to toggle whether a filter on that layer applies to only the one layer or to all below it also - these functions are:
  • layer_enable_fx(layer_name_or_id, bool) enables\disables the filter on the specified layer
  • layer_fx_is_enabled(layer_name_or_id) returns whether any filter is enabled on the specified layer
  • fx_set_single_layer("filterName", true/false) controls whether that filter affect just this one layer (true) or all underneath it (false)
  • fx_get_single_layer("filterName") returns the value of the above function again later on

Automatic Detection Of Filter/Effects Being Used By fx_create()

  • fx_create() calls are now detected at compile time and your filters are added to the game automatically, so you no longer have to create a "placeholder" Room Editor layer which uses that effect just so it can be used in-game by this function

Added Secure Web Sockets Support

  • network_create_socket() now supports a new "network_socket_wss" type which you can then use with network_connect() to connect to a secure socket
  • Similarly, network_connect()'s second argument now supports providing a wss:// URL for use with _ws or _wss sockets
  • Secure sockets are now supported on almost all platforms (everything except for UWP, Xbox One builds which used the XDK, and OperaGX)
  • Note also that this change also added some basic parsing to support paths on the end of the socket "URL" (e.g. "foo.com/path")

Changed The Application Oven To Also Support M1 Architecture

  • You shouldn't see any difference when building projects, etc., but this means the app with now run natively on these Macs

Added support for targeting iOS and tvOS simulators on M1 CPU Macs

  • Updated the Xcode project to allow VM and YYC builds to run on simulators launched on an M1 architecture Mac
  • (Intel Macs worked fine already)

Removed the Remote Worker

  • Whilst there are a small number of worker users and so we appreciate this might affect your workflow, the usage levels are so low that continuing to ship the installer as part of the download to everyone and support the worker each release is not effective
  • Please use the regular Windows and Mac IDEs for all your platform builds now

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • A number of old packages have now been removed from various platform runners - old social features like ads/achievements/challenges and also some push notifications packages. You should not see any change, as these things were long ago replaced with our Marketplace asset extensions, but just be aware that if you do still reference these in old projects, then you will need to remove that code now.

2.3.7 runtimes update a number of the SDKs GMS2 requires during builds (so please see our setup guides if you have issues building projects!) and raises Spine support to v4.0. Please be aware this Spine change will require you to re-export your Spine images using v4.0 before they will work again in GMS2.

This release also changes "true" and "false" into actual Booleans, adds support for a new "nullish" operator and several new filter layers in your rooms, as well as the ability to omit arguments from your function calls to have the game intelliegently use "undefined" for those items.

See below for all the runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes Since Runtime 2.3.7.474

  • Building Projects: [YYC] A much more helpful error is now shown when builds fail because your Visual Studio install directory as set in Preferences cannot be found
  • Building Projects: Fixed a likely reason for "Unable to obtain permission to execute" shown to some users who have valid licences [also added more logging for if this issue does happen again]
  • Garbage Collection: Weak refs are now being detached properly when the item is cleared, stops game crashes if the item is accidentally accessed thereafter
  • In-Game: Nullish operator now works with struct/map/list accessors
  • In-Game: The new 2.3.7 filter layers are now re-applied correctly after calling game_restart()
  • In-Game: [YYC and HTML5] Boolean values in arrays and structs now compile as typeof(bool)
  • In Game: [YYC] Nullish operator now produces the same results as VM builds do when structs are used as part of the rexpression
  • In-Game: [macOS VM] string(NaN) no longer returns "nan" instead of "NaN" when game ran on M1 Macs
  • In-Game: [macOS VM] infinity == infinity no longer returns false when game ran on M1 Macs
  • In-Game: [macOS VM] is_nan(NaN) no longer returns false when game ran on M1 Macs
  • In-Game: [macOS VM] array_equals() with arrays containing NaN no longer returns true when game ran on M1 Macs
  • All 4 of the above macOS VM issues in the original 2.3.7 release also affected iOS and tvOS if built using a recent version of Xcode, so all 3 platforms are fixed now
  • In-Game: [HTML5] variable_global_exists() will now return true when a variable is set to undefined, rather than false as it did before
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Extensions with variable number of arguments no longer compile to invalid JS
  • In-Game: [OperaGX, iOS] get_string_async() no longer crashes your game when clicking the Cancel button if the entered string is either empty or very long
  • In-Game: json_encode() can parse big ds_maps again
  • In-Game: json_stringify(myStruct) again includes all nested structs inside "myStruct", rather than just adding the first one and any others became null
  • In-Game: skeleton_attachment_set() when no skin is set no longer causes games to crash silently
  • In-Game: url_open() will no longer stop your game if it is unable to be called due to no suitable OS browser setting [note that you also get some simple logging as to why that machine couldn't complete the operation if you launch the game .exe with the -debugoutput flag]

2.3.7.474

Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0

  • Added support for importing and using Spine 4.0 images in your games
  • However, be aware that due to the way the Spine runtime only supports one version at a time, you will need to use Spine 4.0 to re-export all of your assets for your projects before they will work now
  • If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game

Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls

  • Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
  • I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)

Added Two New "Nullish" Operators

  • Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable
  • Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing

Implemented Android 12/API 31+ intent-filter changes

  • This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
  • Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
  • (We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions)

Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds

  • This runtime adds support for the new "Always Convert" functionality for sounds in the 2.3.7 IDE (see the IDE notes for more info)

Added Several New Filter Layer Types

  • This runtime adds support for three new Room Editor filter layer types in the 2.3.7 IDE - Heat Haze, Twirt Distort, and Underwater (see the IDE notes for more info)

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • In-Game: Stopped Ogg playback using existing channels that are still active, but no longer playing their previous sound and so are currently closing
  • Note: This fixes issues with sound playback using the wrong settings (e.g., the new sound looping when it's not meant to or being unable to fade it out) or with audio_get_name() failing to be able to tell what the currently-playing sound is, but you should check any audio-intensive projects carefully
  • Doing a "Create Exe" for Opera GX will now always use PNGCrush to compress all your images and reduce the submission package size
  • Note: This will ensure your project's build cache is recreated for all images first (and does so every Create Exe), so be aware that build times will be a little longer now
  • True and False are now actual booleans (so therefore typeof(true) will return "boolean" and is_bool(true) will return 1, etc.)
  • Made a significant optimisation for runner loading times if your project has lots of objects in it (typically >1000 before you will see real improvements) - this improvement is greater still if physics is enabled or if lots of the objects have collision events

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: [Ubuntu ARM] Fixed a suffix name clash error when your project contains extensions for both armv7 and aarch64
  • Building Projects: [HTML5] Code "static a=[]; static b=1" no longer produces invalid JS
  • Building Projects: [iOS] Fixed building projects when using Xcode 13
  • Extensions: Adding an int64 to a dsmap from an extension no longer converts the value to a double first
  • Garbage Collection: Fixed a game crash when assigning a function literal to a global variable in GML extension's init function
  • In-Game: Moving a particle system to another layer no longer also moves the Object it was created by
  • In-Game: Shake filters no longer cause tiles on lower layers to briefly disappear when the filter starts playing
  • In-Game: Made a few appearance/quality fixes for the Twirl Distort filter
  • In-Game: "ref" variable inside weak_ref now returns undefined if the reference has been GC'ed
  • In-Game: [Windows] Windows' error sound effect no longer plays when using Alt+Enter to toggle fullscreen
  • In-Game: [Windows] Fixed a memory leak for window "handles" which caused their count to keep increasing
  • In-Game: [macOS] Precise collisions now work correctly for rotated sprites again [a collisions optimisation fix had been lost for 2.3.6, but has now been restored]
  • In-Game: [Ubuntu] Fixed a crash on game start if using any functions from .gml extensions in the project
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed a crash on game start if using any Included Files pointing to external WASM packages
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Implemented client-side game caching within the browser
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed game crashes when attempting to destroy an instance twice, if that instance has code for handling a ds list
  • In-Game: [HTML5] You are now able to convert a function to a boolean [which fixes an uncaught exception in earlier releases]
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed a crash when deleting a physics joint
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Instances in the process of being destroyed are no longer found or will return values when calling "ObjectName.variableName" code, so now works the same as other platforms
  • In Game: [HTML5] Spine animations now work properly again / In-Game: [HTML5] draw_skeleton_time() now works again
  • In-Game: [HTML5] Intersect View Boundary events now correctly stop firing after the object has left the view, so now works the same as other platforms
  • In-Game: [Android VM and YYC] Fixed an inconsistency with the contents of a struct when ran on these two targets
  • In-Game: [Android] Accessing a "global." array no longer gives unexpected "trying to index a variable not an array" error
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] audio_position_listener() no longer causes audio skipping if called frequently in a Step event [assuming you don't actually move the listener every frame, as now subsequent calls to set the same position are ignored]
  • In-Game: buffer_compress(oldBufffer,newBuffer) no longer blocks memory being freed by a subsequent call to buffer_delete(oldBuffer)
  • In-Game: display_get_frequency() fixed/reimplemented this old function so it now works with modern monitors and devices
  • In-Game: draw_sprite_stretched() and draw_sprite_stretched_ext() no longer obey origin offset values when drawing nine slice sprites, so behave the way the manual says they should have and the same as non-nine slice sprites did
  • In-Game: [HTML5] draw_tile() will now draw the expected tiles if called inside a "with(structName)" block
  • In-Game: [HTML5] environment_get_variable() now returns an empty string instead of "undefined", so now works the same as other platforms
  • In-Game: font_add() now detects and uses the correct kerning values for some specific fonts whoich used to have issues (e.g. "lady-copra" reported to us)
  • In-Game: [HTML5] game_project_name now returns the expected project name instead of the Game Options display name
  • In-Game: [Android] http_request() no longer causes the game to crash when attempting to send a large surface via HTTP POST
  • In-Game: json_decode() no longer fails for strings containing more than 32 layers of nested items [the new limit is 128]
  • In-Game: keyboard_check(vk_lshift) no longer reacts to keypresses when the game window is not in focus [same fix was made for vk_rshift, and the "combined" Shift was already fixed in an earlier release]
  • In-Game: keyboard_check_direct(vk_anykey) now detects keyboard keys as you'd expect (rather than only detecting LMB presses, as it did in previous recent releases)
  • In-Game: [HTML5] layer_script_begin/end now have the correct event_type and event_number values
  • In-Game: show_message(sequence_instance) no longer causes an immediate stack overflow
  • In-Game: [HTML5] sprite_merge() now displays all frames correctly, rather than just the first one
  • In-Game: variable_struct_remove() with a nested and empty struct no longer causes the game to crash
  • In-Game: weak_ref_create() no longer causes a memory leak

2.3.6 brings a lot of stability fixes (particularly to the new OperaGX target introduced in 2.3.5) and fixes a number of issues with precise collisions - especially with scaled-up small sprites. It also introduces support for the Filters layer in the Room Editor. Plus, there is also a bit of clean-up of old code and variable/event names, so please do read the release notes carefully in case any of this applies to you.

See below for runtime changes/fixes and check the IDE Release Notes

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Fixed the OperaGX target so it will not attempt to load unsupported .dll extensions
  • Note: if you have a pre-2.3.5 project which uses extensions and you now want to run it on OperaGX, please check that the extension is suitable for use on the platform and that OperaGX is actually enabled in the extensions's options
  • Removed the ev_async_message_event constant used with event_perform_async(), as this event didn't fire Broadcast Message events like some users were attempting to use it for, and so caused confusion
  • Note: if you have this code in your project now, please change it to a suitable alternative event
  • Removed a lot of old, stale code relating to GM:S 1.x variables not used in GMS2 nowadays - you should not notice any changes, but please let us know if you do

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Garbage Collection: Structs are now garbage-collected properly when calling "delete" on them
  • In-Game: Fixed that scaled-up sprites using "Slow" masks give poor instance_place()/instance_place_list()/place_meeting() results and a large FPS drop since 2.3.3
  • In-Game: Fixed a crash when rapidly creating and destroying 20+ anim curves via code
  • In-Game: Fixed that playing a sound from a sequence could loop and also keep playing even after the sequence has ended
  • In-Game: Fixed an infinite loop when trying to grow a zero-sized buffer
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed some blurring of the game window when played in the browser
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Shift keys now work as expected
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Mouse wheel now works as expected
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Gamepad detection on startup now works as expected
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed inconsistent behaviour on some suitable shaders between GX and Windows
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] keyboard_string no longer gets an unwanted "E" character added to the string when enter/return is pressed
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] keyboard_string now responds correctly to pressing backspaces and also to setting it to ""
  • In-Game: [OperaGX] url_open() now works as expected
  • In-Game: [HTML5] SWF sprites now play correctly when assigned to an object
  • In-Game: [HTML5] image_xscale = -1 now maintains the Sprite's origin, no longer becomes offset incorrectly
  • In-Game: [Android] Sprites are no longer drawn at different coordinates after minimising and reopening the game
  • In-Game: [iOS] Fixed the parsing of http response's header map when there is a 401 http_status code
  • In-Game: [HTML5] asset_get_index() now returns the correct index for all Tile Set assets
  • In-Game: [HTML5] audio_sound_set_position() no longer breaks the ability to later manually stop that sound before it has finished playing
  • In-Game: ds_grid_read() no longer causes a memory leak
  • In-Game: event_perform_async(ev_async_message_event, map) doesn't seem to trigger any objects' Broadcast Message event [see the note above, as this event has been removed now]
  • In-Game: [HTML5] game_project_name() now returns the expected game title name instead of the actual project name
  • In-Game: network_connect() with a string URL such as "abc" now triggers the expected async event
  • In-Game: network_connect_raw_async() no longer fires an incorrect positive connection event as soon as the function is called
  • In-Game: [macOS] network_create_server(network_socket_ws, ...) no longer fails each time with "Error: Can't open main server socket"

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Changes since runtime 2.3.3.434

  • In-Game: Fixed most ways of calling a function which is in a global array so it no longer returns an "object undefined" error [we are aware of a route to still getting this]
  • In-Game: [VM] Fixed a code error "Object1.argument0(...) not set before reading it." when setting "self" or "global" struct values and accessing this value inside a function
  • Reverted the change for "In-Game: Sequences now create their object instances at their correct x/y values rather than creating them all at 0x0 and then quickly moving"
  • That one change above should fix various reports of issues with Sequences and objects inside the sequence not performing their Create events as expected
  • Building Projects: [Steam Windows IDE] Projects with spaces in the name no longer cause build failures due to alternative Steam launcher method issues

Runtime 2.3.3.434

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Building Projects: [Android YYC] The NDK 22 installation check now finds your install correctly when starting builds
  • Building Projects: [HTML5] Added additional iframe focus-detection code in response to Itch.io/Newgrounds changes (see above)
  • Building projects: [iOS YYC] Mac IDE fix for the error 'tell app \\"Xcode\\" to quit' which appears for some users
  • In-Game: Incrementing decimal image_index values no longer returns the corrected value immediately, instead returns the "raw" result and allows a 1-frame delay before clamping properly (see above)
  • In-Game: Accessing an out-of-bounds index of an array inside a struct in VM will now error like YYC/HTML already do, rather than return 0
  • Please note that this release also changes the required SDKs for PS4 and Switch to newer versions - please see their setup guides for full details of what you need now

Other Bugs Fixed

  • Building Projects: Made a number of various improvements to reduce the amount of time some very large projects require to compile (VM and YYC)

  • Building Projects: [HTML5] Running a freshly-imported project for Windows and then HTML5 straight after no longer gives corrupted/missing visuals in that first HTML5 build
  • Debugger: Collision events and associated scripts when the "other" object is a parent are now shown correctly
  • Debugger: Using a "Step ..." command whilst on a line with an error no longer skips showing you that error
  • Debugger: Lines that call "delete" are now stepped-into properly
  • Debugger: Texture information is now correctly reported, flushing no longer continues to show old images
  • Garbage Collector: Memory is now cleared correctly when an array is resized smaller

  • In-Game: Clicking your LMB / tapping the screen no longer causes a drop in fps/fps_real values while the click is held
  • In-Game: Re-fixed Animation End events so they still trigger reliably when the sprite frames and game speed result in very small increment values
  • In-Game: Fixed that reusing a function parameter's name as a "self." variable inside the function and then += that "self." version, the external variable is affected instead
  • In-Game: Fixed being unable to set/remove your struct variables if they have the same name as GMS2's in-built variables

2.3.3 runtimes bring the ability to declare the value for optional arguments on a function, a few helper functions, and support for two thumb mouse buttons on Desktop and HTML5 platforms. Further fixes and optimisations to reduce compile times, plus an important FPS fix in-game.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are several very important ones, so please read carefully) and check the IDE Release Notes

Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments

  • Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later
  • A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults
  • Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”
  • You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

Added buffer_set_used_size()

  • In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
  • Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
  • As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added font_get_info()

  • Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
  • Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
  • “undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
  • See the new manual page for this function for more info

Added sprite_get_info()

  • Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
  • Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)

  • Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
  • mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes

  • Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually

  • 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
  • This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again
  • However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

2.3.2 introduces Nine Slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Fixes since runtime 423

  • Fixed runtime 423 issue with garbage collection/CPU stalls on game_end() or gc_collect() and gradual increases in memory seen in some games

Fixes since runtime 420

  • Fixed that if you tried to build iOS using the Windows IDE it could error with "The variable Xcode is not defined" (when the Mac IDE worked fine with that same Xcode install)
  • Fixed a CPU usage issue with the garbage collector, so now usage values should be much lower again on all platforms and also gives a slight performance boost compared to 2.3.1
  • Fixed an issue stopping ARM builds of Ubuntu YYC
  • Fixed an issue where projects which contain a large number of audio files could fail to build
  • Added a compiler optimisation to speed up texture page generation during builds
  • Added a small optimisation to speed up loading projects
  • Re-fixed that the Animation End event does not trigger reliably when the sprite frames and game speed result in very small values

Runtime 420

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache rather than re-writing files more often than required
  • Ternary expressions are now calculated at compile time to see if we can optimise these
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself to reduce the amount of redundant work it was going
  • The sounds change mentioned below...

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any .ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the .ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any .wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the file will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother and more accurate FPS values - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically
  • Note that whilst they're not listed individually below, multiple ticket samples were fixed at once by this change

Changes to image_index behaviour regarding Sprite Broadcast Messages

  • Following recent GMC feedback, modifying image_index manually to set new values will not modulo the resulting image_index value until the following frame (as 2.2.5-and-older used to do it)
  • Now, you will NOT get any sprite broadcast message(s) if you set image_index directly
  • Animation End events will still be fired as before if you set image_index to the final frame or beyond, there's no change here

Changes to when static variables are actually created by the compiler

  • Multiple fixes have been made on VM (YYC was usually correct) for multi-layer inheritance of constructor methods, especially if the method was redefined/uses static
  • As part of this change, each individual static variable in a given script/function are now handled first when compiling that script/event, so that their value can be used by the rest of your code
  • Note that you may still get a silent crash beyond our ability to prevent if you redefine a static method and you forget to declare each definition as a static also
  • Also fixed an issue where Static variables would get re-initialised when a function is called recursively

Misc changes to function behaviours to be aware of

  • array_length() now returns "undefined" when evaluating anything which is not an array. You may need to refactor your code to account for this change, as we have found several ticket sample projects checked array_length(0) when controlling game logic
  • buffer_load() now supports loading Included Files directly into buffers on HTML5 (same as you could already on Windows, etc.)
  • camera_set_begin_script() and camera_set_end_script() now have support for manipulating your surfaces
  • debug_get_callstack() now has an optional "maxDepth" argument, allowing you to control the size of error log you receive
  • exception_unhandled_handler(undefined) can now be used to remove any currently-set custom exception handler and return to the default GMS2 handler
  • json_parse() no longer ignores keys where the value is "null", "undefined", "nan", "infinity", or "-infinity" (note it will read the last three in as strings you will need to handle yourself later, as the JSON standard doesn't actually have rules for handling these)
  • json_stringify() now supports map keys which are set to "nan", "infinity", and "-infinity" (see the line above)
  • show_debug_message() formatting when displaying a struct on HTML5 is now consistent with how it has always behaved on Windows, etc.
  • Added a "stack overflow" error on YYC when turning an array pushed to itself into a string (VM already showed an error)
  • Multiplication of a float by an int64 (in this specific order) no longer results in the float being cast to an int first
  • HTML5 will also now not truncate int64 numbers when using postfix/prefix increment/decrement operators (as Windows, etc., already do)
  • Fixed that results of maths operations which involved enums set to float values were rounded to integer
  • Fixed that you previously got inconsistent results for "self" and "[self]" when using "with" on a struct, both will now warn that this is recursive
