2.3.2 introduces Nine Slice support for your sprites, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And in combination with IDE 2.3.2 you can also build the new macOS .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

For more info on some of the big additions listed below, please see our "What's new in 2.3.2" Helpdesk post

Fixes since runtime 420

  • Fixed that if you tried to build iOS using the Windows IDE it could error with "The variable Xcode is not defined" (when the Mac IDE worked fine with that same Xcode install)
  • Fixed a CPU usage issue with the garbage collector, so now usage values should be much lower again on all platforms and also gives a slight performance boost compared to 2.3.1
  • Fixed an issue stopping ARM builds of Ubuntu YYC
  • Fixed an issue where projects which contain a large number of audio files could fail to build
  • Added a compiler optimisation to speed up texture page generation during builds
  • Added a small optimisation to speed up loading projects
  • Re-fixed that the Animation End event does not trigger reliably when the sprite frames and game speed result in very small values

Runtime 420

Optimisations to Reduce Project Build Times

  • We have made a number of fixes and changes to the build processes on all platforms in an attempt to reduce compile times, including:
  • A fix to stop very large comments in your scripts from slowing down compiles
  • Pre-compiled headers have been added for every platform
  • Lots of fixes for cached builds actually making full use of the cache rather than re-writing files more often than required
  • Ternary expressions are now calculated at compile time to see if we can optimise these
  • A number of speed-ups have been made for the compiler itself to reduce the amount of redundant work it was going
  • The sounds change mentioned below...

Asset Compiler Changes for Sounds

  • Carrying on from the above change, we made a further optimisation for sounds:
  • If you have any .ogg files in your sounds and you have set these to remain compressed in the sound editor, these will now not be recompiled during every build and instead the original file will just be passed through to your package, as it will be assumed you have created the sound with the desired values. This speeds up builds, but also stops an issue where occasionally small amounts of silence were added to the .ogg files
  • Similarly, if you have any .wav files and you have set these to remain uncompressed in the sound editor, then the asset compiler will first quickly check if the values you set in the sound editor match the contents of the .wav, and again if they already match your source .wav it will just be passed through to your package. If they do not match, then the file will be recompiled as before
  • Note that using a .mp3 will still always result in a recompile, as will providing an .ogg but then requesting it becomes an uncompressed sound or providing a .wav but then requesting it becomes a compressed sound

Nine Slice Support

  • Nice Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between
  • Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Mac DMG Export Package

  • If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
  • A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
  • Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ IDE also when building your project

Improvements to Windows Timer Accuracy

  • We have added a couple of new functions and tweaked the Windows runner in response to the recent Windows 10 timer resolution change, which should result in smoother and more accurate FPS values - especially on high-refresh monitors
  • As part of this, the scheduler's resolution is now set to 1ms on startup and there are two new functions scheduler_resolution_set() and scheduler_resolution_get() which will let you alter this value dynamically
  • Note that whilst they're not listed individually below, multiple ticket samples were fixed at once by this change

Changes to image_index behaviour regarding Sprite Broadcast Messages

  • Following recent GMC feedback, modifying image_index manually to set new values will not modulo the resulting image_index value until the following frame (as 2.2.5-and-older used to do it)
  • Now, you will NOT get any sprite broadcast message(s) if you set image_index directly
  • Animation End events will still be fired as before if you set image_index to the final frame or beyond, there's no change here

Changes to when static variables are actually created by the compiler

  • Multiple fixes have been made on VM (YYC was usually correct) for multi-layer inheritance of constructor methods, especially if the method was redefined/uses static
  • As part of this change, each individual static variable in a given script/function are now handled first when compiling that script/event, so that their value can be used by the rest of your code
  • Note that you may still get a silent crash beyond our ability to prevent if you redefine a static method and you forget to declare each definition as a static also
  • Also fixed an issue where Static variables would get re-initialised when a function is called recursively

Misc changes to function behaviours to be aware of

  • array_length() now returns "undefined" when evaluating anything which is not an array. You may need to refactor your code to account for this change, as we have found several ticket sample projects checked array_length(0) when controlling game logic
  • buffer_load() now supports loading Included Files directly into buffers on HTML5 (same as you could already on Windows, etc.)
  • camera_set_begin_script() and camera_set_end_script() now have support for manipulating your surfaces
  • debug_get_callstack() now has an optional "maxDepth" argument, allowing you to control the size of error log you receive
  • exception_unhandled_handler(undefined) can now be used to remove any currently-set custom exception handler and return to the default GMS2 handler
  • json_parse() no longer ignores keys where the value is "null", "undefined", "nan", "infinity", or "-infinity" (note it will read the last three in as strings you will need to handle yourself later, as the JSON standard doesn't actually have rules for handling these)
  • json_stringify() now supports map keys which are set to "nan", "infinity", and "-infinity" (see the line above)
  • show_debug_message() formatting when displaying a struct on HTML5 is now consistent with how it has always behaved on Windows, etc.
  • Added a "stack overflow" error on YYC when turning an array pushed to itself into a string (VM already showed an error)
  • Multiplication of a float by an int64 (in this specific order) no longer results in the float being cast to an int first
  • HTML5 will also now not truncate int64 numbers when using postfix/prefix increment/decrement operators (as Windows, etc., already do)
  • Fixed that results of maths operations which involved enums set to float values were rounded to integer
  • Fixed that you previously got inconsistent results for "self" and "[self]" when using "with" on a struct, both will now warn that this is recursive

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Runtime 2.3.1.406

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
  • Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
  • Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

Multiple New Package Formats

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.
  • game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now
  • ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.
  • There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

Misc Other Changes

  • Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
  • Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual
  • Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

2.3.1 is another evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we've added Bezier curve support, new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and added broadcast messages to Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also some very important fixes/additions for garbage collection and configs support, plus updated SDKs/external tools for many of the platforms.

Introduced Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, and UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types also.

See below for runtime changes/fixes (there are a lot of very important ones, so please review thoroughly) and check the IDE Release Notes for IDE changes/fixes.

Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements

  • Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
  • Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
  • Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
  • Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
  • Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
  • And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

Support for Android 11

  • Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
  • Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
  • Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
  • Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

Support for recent Apple platform releases

  • Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
  • Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
  • Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
  • Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

Multiple New Package Formats

  • Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
  • ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
  • UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
  • Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac
  • If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

Important Changes To Be Aware Of

  • Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.
  • game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now
  • ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.
  • There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

Misc Other Changes

  • Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
  • Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
  • Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
  • Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual
  • Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

2.3.0 is a huge new release and there is a lot changed, as this version now contains everything we announced in the "Upcoming Changes to GML" blogs that we published last year as well as a very sizeable list of bug fixes and new additions to match changes to asset types now in the 2.3.0 IDE, so please read these notes carefully and check out the guide linked-to below. (For the IDE release notes, see this page.)

Because this version is so big and contains so much new stuff these notes will be brief, but for more information on everything below please see this detailed introduction to all the new features and some important notes about moving your projects from 2.2.5 to 2.3.0. Please also be aware that opening an existing project in 2.3.0 the first time will ask you to convert the project and save it out again with a new name. This is because the project format has now been changed quite extensively. You will not be able to open newer-style projects in 2.2.5 or older, and similarly 2.3.0 does not allow you to set 2.2.5 or older runtimes as active.

You should check out the all-new manual for specifics on the new/changed functions and if your project requires any modifying post-conversion, as it is likely at least some small changes will need to be made.

Scripts now contain functions

  • A script asset is no longer limited to being just one custom function - instead, you will find a new function declaration is added whenever you create a script, and you can add your own below this and call these functions as required elsewhere in your game
  • Scripts are also now processed on startup, which means if you create a script which contains lines which are not wrapped in a function declaration, those lines will always run on game start, allowing you to very easily create initialisation scripts and control functionality
  • NOTE: You should review your scripts after importing any 2.2.5 projects in case you need to remove/tweak these function declarations so that your game initialises correctly.

Methods

  • You can also now bind functions to your instances and call them in a natural way

All arrays are now 1D

  • However, they can actually now be chained, so you can create arrays three (or more) deep if you require by chaining the declaration - e.g. array[0][0][0]
  • The 2D array functions have now been deprecated, but if you have these in your 2.2.5 projects they will still work due to the compatibility layer

Sequences and Animation Curves

  • There are new functions to allow you to create entirely new assets at runtime or to return and modify existing ones created in the IDE

Structs

  • You can now declare structs, which are (in very simple terms) one variable holding a collection of other variables, and create instances of these on-demand, allowing you to manage your data more clearly

Garbage Collector

  • The runner now has a multi-stage garbage collector to clean up in-game memory and maintain performance
  • This is all automatically done for you, but there are functions to allow you to call it on-demand also and even to turn it off if you wish

Handling exceptions via Try/Catch

  • You can now Try() a bit of code and Catch() if it gave any errors, allowing you to hopefully recover from a bad situation
  • If things aren't recoverable, you can also Finally() a last bit of code before your game shows an error and ends
  • You can also Throw() an exception at any time, allowing you to create your own custom errors
  • And you can handle runner exceptions also by declaring your own unhandled exception handler

And much, much more!

Bugs

  • For the full list of public in-game issues fixed in this version since 2.2.5, see the Change Log
  • Note, however, that this is a very small list compared to the full private change log and you will no doubt find a lot of old issues have been fixed

2.2.4 is a big update of the Android toolchain to match the requirements of API 29 (Android 10), and the same on macOS/iOS/tvOS to match Apple's announcements in their new releases - please update to this version if you're using macOS Catalina.

IAP support has been greatly updated - including subscriptions support and receipt verification functionality!

There has been another big push on making HTML5 games work more closely to how they do on other platforms, and we also added Websockets support so now you have much more scope for networked games.

For IDE release notes, see this page.

Updated IAP Support For Google Play, Amazon, and all Apple platforms

  • Updated the Google IAPs extension and created new Amazon IAPs and Apple IAPs extensions - you now need to use these for all IAP functionality (these won't work with older runtimes)
  • Added support for subscriptions on all of these platforms
  • Added support for communication with external payment verification servers (note that Amazon requires you to use your own web server for verifying all IAPs)

  • Changed to a current version of Gradle (5.1.1), so now you can use current versions of JDK and more easily implement some of your own extensions
  • Removed the change of title to "[Game Name] (as Yoyo runner)" when doing a run (Create exe never did this)
  • Please note that our Google Play Services and Google Play Expansion extensions have been updated to match these changes and so won't build with older runtimes!

Noteable macOS Changes

  • Notarisation support has been added during builds - you will need to submit your archive in Xcode to Apple to complete the process
  • Mac: Fixed gamepad_test_mapping() did not override the mapping properly when the pad was one which already had a default mapping in the database

Noteable iOS Changes

  • Fixed legacy splash screen info and startup code in packages were stopping the updated splashes from 2.2.2 from working properly in current Xcode builds
  • Note: This does remove the old functionality where the runner would try to download the game over wifi - you have to use USB between the iDevice and your Mac (as we have actually documented for a while)
  • Fixed an iOS 13 issue where landscape games incorrectly launched in a portrait view, so only a portion of the game view was visible and was also rotated
  • Fixed achievement_load_leaderboard() on Game Center, plus added the updated "team_player_id" and "game_player_id" variables in iOS 12.4 and above (all of this on tvOS also)
  • Fixed the building of frameworks in your project which have a "+" sign in its name
  • Fixed the "Defer Home Indicator Input" option so on iOS 13 this option isn't effectively ignored by the OS
  • Note: If enabled, the home bar will always be shown at low alpha, the first swipe wakes the bar and the second takes you home; If disabled, the bar is not shown in-game, but the first edge swipe will take you home
  • Added PS4/Xbox One gamepad support and the updated "menu" and "options" buttons support Apple added for iOS 13 / tvOS 13 (and macOS Catalina)
  • Added the plist flags required for TestFlight submissions, following recent-ish requirement changes
  • Note that there is currently no mention of ipadOS in our docs/the IDE and no new target has been added - this is because iOS packages still work absolutely fine on ipadOS also

Notable UWP Changes

  • UWP: Fixed window_set_size(), window_set_fullscreen() and the "start in fullscreen" option so you can now control the game window size as you'd expect
  • UWP: Added implementations of window_set_caption(), window_mouse_set(), window_get_x() and window_get_y()
  • UWP: Added debug output of failed DPDeploy return values - now exposes more information when there is a device connection error
  • Note that following changes to Device Portal in Windows 10 v1903, please make sure you do not require authentication in Device Portal, otherwise DPDeploy will fail (0031273)

Misc

  • Gamepads: Gamepad functionality is now only bundled-into your app package if you actually use gamepad functions - be aware only having Async events for the pad found/lost events isn't enough to cause pad support to be added
  • Buffers: Fixed a memory leak in buffer_compress() with handling the source buffer
  • Buffers: Fixed various issues where the "usedsize" value of the buffer was not being updated properly or was mistakenly being initialised to the full size of the buffer
  • Buffers: Changed buffer_base64_decode() to return -1 if it can't decode a string, rather than throwing an error
  • Collisions: Fixed a couple of issues where disabling "solid" for an instance caused collisions to think the instance was in a previous position when you re-enabled "solid" later
  • Collisions: Fixed a crash checking collisions against an instance which has an empty sprite set as its sprite_index (and it won't detect a hit)
  • Functions: Fixed the OpenGL implementation of gpu_set_texrepeat(true) (0031303)
  • Functions: Fixed json_decode() so a json "null" becomes a GML "undefined" and json_encode() so it turns a GML "undefined" into a json "null"
  • Functions: Fixed json_encode() so encoding a map containing an array key will now throw a code error rather than silently crashing
  • Functions: Fixed room_assign() so Create events in the new room are fired as expected
  • Functions: Fixed room_duplicate() so it uses the "object following" value set in the source room
  • Functions: Added support for buffer_f16
  • Functions: Added variable_instance_names_count()
  • General: Removed the Output Window debug text for alleged max/min/avg FPS values, as this always showed odd and incorrect results when using game_end()
  • General: Fixed that a constant of 0.5 evaluates to true when part of a boolean expression
  • Networking: Fixed http_request() on macOS, iOS/tvOS, UWP and some consoles so when using a buffer body so it doesn't always do a POST and instead does what you asked for
  • Physics: Games now throw a code error if physics_fixture_add_point() is called when you haven't already set the polygon/chain shape
  • Ubuntu: Fixed the game window position on multiple-monitor setups so it's launched/leaves fullscreen in the middle of the primary monitor, not across the bezels of both monitors

  • See the bug database's Change Log for the full list of public issues.
  • Known Issues can be found on the bug database also - for the current in-game headline list see this page.

2.2.3 sees the release of tvOS as a new platform, Android using OpenGL ES 2 by default, and being able to turn off the sandbox and using subst'ed drives on desktop platforms. It also comes with a whole bunch of important bug fixes and the extending of a number of functions which were only implemented for very specific platforms to now work properly on all applicable platforms.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Runtime 344 Hotfix Change

  • 0031135 Compiling: Asset Compiler gets stuck in an infinite loop "Reading config delta" trying to process overriden instance variables

New tvOS export target

  • Added tvOS as a new supported target platform
  • Also adds support for the Siri gamepad/remote
  • See the manual and our setup guide on the Helpdesk for more info
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Mac Build Tools Updated

  • Worked around the version of Mono installed by Visual Studio 2019 For Mac having a broken certificate-checker and causing errors when trying to compile projects in GMS2
  • Fixed an OpenSSH issue which stopped some Mojave users from being able to build projects on their Ubuntu machines even though Target Manager said the connection was successful
  • Fixed that iOS builds always failed to run project from the IDE due to i386 architecture error during the Tests phase, causing you to have to run the project in Xcode
  • Fixed the Mac build settings which were causing the "icon" vs "Icon" filename issue when building Mac VM packages and submitting these to the App Store

Changes to layer system for persistent instances and particle systems

  • Fixed/changed persistent instances/particle systems to now preserve their layer information as they move between rooms, creating a new layer of that name and depth in the new room if required
  • If a layer of the correct name already exists in the new room, then the instance/particle system will be placed on that layer (even if the depth value differs)
  • Fixes issues with the instance's layer information changing to just be "-1" after moving between rooms

Changes to Android support/behaviours

  • Changed the runner to always use OpenGL ES 2 if the device supports it. Fixes "inconsistency" bugs reported for older Android devices.
  • Changed to now only pause the runner on explicit "onPause" messages from the OS and not pause on "focus lost" messages also - fixes issues where dragging down the tray would pause your game
  • Fixed an issue with Lint analysis failing builds during the gamepad checking stage if your Minimum API value was set to 18 or lower

Ability to launch Steam-enabled games via alternative launcher on Windows

  • Added new Game Option > Windows > "Use alternative launcher for Steam application"
  • Only valid if using the Windows Steam IDE, as this fixes the issue where Steam now detects GMS2's own app ID instead of the real ID of your game if you simply ran the project inside the IDE
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Ability to turn off the file-system sandbox on desktop OSes

  • Added Game Options into Windows/macOS/Ubuntu for disabling the file-system sandbox restrictions, so you can save/load files from anywhere not protected by the OS or other security software
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Ability to turn off using subst'ed drives when building for some platforms

  • Preferences > General Settings > Compiling now has a new setting "Use subst for drive paths" - disabling this will stop GMS2 mounting temp build folders as extra drives
  • Note: Has no effect on building for Android or tvOS, as Google's/Apple's build tools frequently exceed Window's maximum filepath length, so without this on you likely couldn't build these platforms
  • Note: Has no effect on runtime downloads/installs either, so if your machine simply doesn't allow subst to run, this option won't stop you needing to resolve that before GMS2 can work properly
  • Note: Requires 2.2.3+ IDE also

Better support/logging of custom errors on Windows builds

  • Added support for both VM and YYC builds to pass debug_event() messages to show_debug_message()
  • Added support for debug_event() to make YYC games actually finish crashing before showing the error dialog which caused the crash - useful when debugging your YYC game in Visual Studio
  • See debug_event()'s manual page for full info on both changes and how to use this new functionality

Misc

  • Fixed the FPS cap/sync on Ubuntu if using an Nvidia GPU, so now your games won't run at turbo speed
  • Fixed that the iPhone X "home indicator" bar was remaining slightly visible at all times - it now fades away from sight
  • Fixed a couple of issues with touches and VKeys not working at the very edges of iOS device screens - however, remember Apple's guidelines are to not have UI here anyway!
  • Fixed a memory leak when returning to a persistent room
  • Fixed layer_destroy_instances() on HTML5 so it now works as expected
  • Fixed http_request() so it always returns headers on Windows 7
  • Fixed a number of collision issues with re-activated instances
  • Fixed a HTML5-only issue with sometimes only using one Spine sprite for all objects
  • Fixed that an unwanted READ_PHONE_STATE permission was being added by the compiler into projects which used Google Play Licensing
  • Fixed texture_global_scale() on Windows to confirm the texture page has not disabled scaling before doing any scaling operation - stops Windows/macOS inconsistencies with this function
  • Fixed a number of inconsistencies with date_... functions on HTML5 so they now work the same way as Windows
  • Fixed an issue with textures/fonts occasionally being lost in-game if you used mipmapping support on macOS
  • Fixed an issue with Spine animations not moving smoothly if you were drawing the skeleton yourself
  • Fixed an issue with gamepad support not working in Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers (Opera, Vivaldi, etc.)
  • Changed YYC's default epsilon value to be the same as VM's (0.00001), stops issues with floating point precision differing between VM and YYC
  • Changed (whenever the compiler determines it's safe to do so) i++ to always be ++i as this is much faster to perform, especially when using YYC
  • Extended surface_depth_disable() so it now works on all platforms
  • Extended the runner's mip-mapping functionality to support HTML5 also
  • Added four-byte wide Unicode character support, so now emojis, etc., can be drawn in-game if they are added to your fonts
  • Added new functions/constants for NaN and infinity, so you can handle these better and avoid errors

Bugs

  • See the bug database's Change Log for the full list of public issues.
  • Known Issues can be found on the bug database also - for the current in-game headline list see this page.

This release has the long-awaited Spine update, which brings support for the recent 3.7 version of Spine. We have also revamped our font-handling and updated the FreeType library. Our HTML5 audio-handling has been improved in line with browser changes and we have addressed issues with streaming audio on Android and iOS browsers.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Spine Support Updated to v3.7

We have used a public fork of the spine runtimes (see our Github). We plan to use this repository going forward, so if you are interested in seeing which changes we have had to make, or which changes/fixes we have taken from the original Esoteric repository, you can.

As well as fixing a few Spine collision issues, we have added support for several Spine features, and you can find the detail for these in the manual (and the guide linked-to in the heading above):

  • Clipping attachments - These are attachments assigned to Spine slots which clip away parts of the sprite
  • Per-attachment colours - We now support tinting attachments based on their assigned colours
  • Per-slot blend modes - We now support per-slot blend modes as specified in the Spine IDE
  • Partial tint-black support - Note that this requires the use of a custom shader (see our manual)
  • Multiple texture page support - We now support Spine sprites which use atlases referencing multiple image files (see this guide)
  • Floating point frame indexes - so you get super-smooth animations, especially noticeable for slow-mo or speed-up effects

FreeType library update

  • All platforms now use v2.9.1 of FreeType (was 2.8.0). Fixes incompatibilities with some fonts and should improve rendering quality of others - requires 2.2.2+ IDE also, otherwise your font might not look as expected!

GML Consistency

  • Changed many string-handling and constant/variable conversion behaviours to match how VM works
  • Made YYC ignore empty scripts the same as VM does, which stops in-game code errors
  • Fixed that ternary operators did not work in YYC
  • See this blog post for further info

Facebook Support Change

  • Created a new Facebook extension for implementing up-to-date FB functionality, replaces our legacy version released a long time ago
  • Removed all the old "facebook_..." functions and constants from the runner, so now if you don't add the FB extension your game has no FB code in it
  • Any project using the old integration now needs to be updated to use the new extension and new function names, etc.
  • See the Marketplace for the new extension and this Helpdesk guide on implementing the extension in your projects

In-Game GIF File Creation

  • Added a new family of functions to allow you to create .gif files from surfaces: gif_open(), gif_add_surface(), gif_save(), and gif_save_buffer()

Extra Tileset Management Functions

  • tileset_get_texture(tileset_id) - get the texture for the given tileset
  • tileset_get_uvs(tileset_id) - get the array of UVs for the tileset (in the same format as sprite_get_uvs() returns its info)
  • tileset_get_name(tileset_id) - get the name of the tileset

macOS

  • Fixed an issue with ffmpeg support for El Capitan, which fixes sounds not converting during builds and games crashing
  • Fixed an issue with "icon"/"Icon" in the Xcode project meaning that AppStore icons were not always showing in submissions
  • Fixed building a Steam game for VM throwing an "image not found" error when using the Mac IDE
  • Fixed an issue where Gamecenter, push notification and IAP support were not being detected and set properly in the Xcode project's Entitlements section
  • Fixed in-game output logs showing properly if you're using the Windows IDE (Mac IDE has been fine for a while)

Ubuntu

  • Fixed an issue with project building which meant some users saw issues with fonts and/or particles
  • Fixed an issue with the CPU usage being 100% as soon as your game started, as our sleep code was not working correctly

HTML5

  • Fixed an issue with layer begin/end scripts not being called during the Draw event
  • Fixed the check for detecting if Opera supports WebGL or not (it does)
  • Fixed errors/crashes when calling ini_key_delete() or variable_instance_get_names()
  • Fixed layer_get_all_elements() not handling an "undefined" value properly
  • Fixed various issues with buffer_base64_decode() and made them more consistent with native
  • Android and iOS browsers no longer wait for streaming sounds to download during the loading screen - they now download async and are later queued and decompressed as required
  • Added audio_sound_is_playable() so you can query if a sound is actually ready to be played in browsers which require touch permission from players before streamed audio can be used

    • Note: There is no change to audio-handling on non-HTML5 platforms (though the new function will work on those platforms too), but for HTML5 we have changed how audio is loaded and played back to match the rules on the executing platform. The general rule of thumb is that a touch (or mouse) event has to be recorded on the canvas for the game before any audio is played, and on iOS we need to decompress any audio before playback (as Apple have disabled streaming audio) which can introduce a delay. Again, see the manual for further details.

Android

  • Added os_check_permission() and os_request_permissions() for handling if your player wants to allow the functionality you have included in the game (e.g., microphone recording)
  • Added os_get_info() now returns an extra key called "android_tv", set to true if the runner thinks it is an AndroidTV platform and false otherwise
  • Changed/Removed Push Notifications support on Google Play to be a new Marketplace "Google Play Push Notifications" extension using Firebase - requires 2.2.2+ IDE also!

iOS

  • Fixed YYC builds failing if you have included push notification support
  • Fixed an issue where Gamecenter, push notification and IAP support were not being detected and set properly in the Xcode project's Entitlements section
  • Fixed that in-game console output was not being sent back to GMS2 properly during the game
  • Fixed an issue where display_get_height/width did not give the correct values on some new iOS devices
  • Fixed issues with splash screens not being set correctly in Xcode projects, so didn't work on certain devices
  • Fixed an issue with virtual keys firing twice per touch, and multiple Vkeys using the same character to bind to was only detecting one Vkey as pressed, not all of them
  • Fixed http_request() crash on iOS if you used buffers as the body of your request
  • Added support for iPhone XR/XS splash screens - requires 2.2.2+ IDE also!

Misc

  • Fixed the runner not starting if you are using the WARP software renderer on your PC in place of an actual graphics card
  • Fixed/Changed ffmpeg to ignore video or image streams in audio files to stop ogg conversion errors (but we would always say to remove these streams anyway...)
  • Fixed asset compiler errors if a single large sprite fills/exceeds an entire texture page and doesn't leave enough space for the border to be applied
  • Fixed/optimised an issue with building very large sprites, so now compiles require less resources for these projects - added an error message for when a sprite is simply too large and you must reduce it
  • Fixed colour_get_red/blue/green() gave the wrong value if the colour had an alpha value also
  • Fixed collision issues with place_empty() and also added support for an optional argument for the object type to check for (defaults to "all" if you don't provide the argument)
  • Fixed variable_global_get() to return "undefined" when no such variable was found
  • Fixed instance_number() so it now counts the same number of instances that with() does
  • Fixed a runner crash with instance_deactivate_all()
  • Fixed audio_emitter_velocity() to also change the pitch of the sound as has always been documented it would

Bugs

  • See the bug database's Change Log for the list of public issues fixed in this version
  • Known Issues can be found on the bug database also - for the current in-game headline list see this page.

This release sees a huge number of bug fixes, but also a few new features. Please thoroughly read the change log using the link at the bottom of these notes, and see the manual for more info on the new functions

For IDE release notes, see this page


Performance Optimisations

  • A number of areas of the asset compiler and runner have now been optimised so your games will run faster and use less memory
    • Runner
      • Camera performance and handling has been improved - this has significant changes when surfaces are set and reset
      • Sped up room change operations
      • Sped up Graphics::SetMatrix, which affects many sprite, views and surface operations
      • When creating Surfaces the runner now doesn’t recalculate matrices if not required
      • Draw event optimisations on sparse layers
      • Memory optimisations on several internal structures for instances and events
      • Optimised the search for and handling of events, particularly for objects with parents
      • Sped up hashing functions used for all maps and internal dictionaries
      • Sped up Instance variable look-ups
      • Smaller collision tree - only instances that have collision events or are marked as solid are added by default. Others are added if a collision query is made that would/could return them
      • Note: If any collision call is made with "object_all" everything gets added to the tree, so it is best to avoid doing this
      • Now only add timeline and path structures for each instance if they are actually used by that instance
    • Asset Compiler
      • Sped up constructing texture pages from texture groups
      • Handling of cropped textures has been improved
  • We have also added new texture page management functions so you can better control your game's memory allocation:
    • texture_prefetch(), texture_is_ready() and texture_flush()
    • texturegroup_get_...() for returning arrays of assets ids on a given page - added variants for textures, sprites, fonts, and tilesets
    • texture_debug_messages() toggles whether the runner writes texture fetch\flush debug output
    • Spine sprites listed as part of a texture page are also included when the above functions are called (SWFs are already on the texture page, so work anyway)
    • See the manual for specifics
  • Please test your games thoroughly, and let us know if you have issues

FPS timing fixes

  • Fixed the newer sleep timer so it now works more accurately when monitor refresh rate is greater than 60 (and Gsync/Freesync monitors)
  • Should also see fewer issues with power-saving optimisations causing FPS drops

macOS

  • Fixed Xcode 10 changing the minimum required OS for running your games to be 10.12 - is now 10.7
  • Fixed pressing the Stop button in the IDE would give an error message when building/running using VM

Ubuntu

  • Fixed building and running games on 18.04.01 LTS
  • Please note this is the Ubuntu version we now develop using and offer customer support for

iOS

  • Push Notification support is no longer always included, stops submission emails from Apple - enable this in Game Options > iOS > Social in 2.2.1+ IDEs
  • Added support for custom App Delegates in your extensions
  • Changed our iPhone X home bar override to a system which requires a double-tap to wake, rather than a single tap - toggle this in Game Options > iOS in 2.2.1+ IDEs

Android

  • Fixed calling the NDK tools when using Windows 7 and building with YYC
  • Added Adaptive Icons support into the build tools - enable this in Game Options > Android > Adaptive Icons in 2.2.1+ IDEs
  • Updated the gamepad functionality to use the pad mappings system used on Windows/macOS/Ubuntu in recent GMS2 versions, so now a lot more pads are supported
  • Fixed Android gamepads being lost on change of app focus away from your game and not being detectable when coming back to the game
  • Please note that the old Moga integration has been removed, so there is no longer a game option for this in 2.2.1+ IDEs

HTML5

  • A massive number of bugs have been fixed or missing functions have been implemented - see the change log for details
  • Fixed the change of layer names to lowercase in the runner to stop issues with accidental duplicate layers in your project and make HTML5 consistent with native
  • Added an in-built font system to avoid issues drawing text when using WebGL (when you have always had to include a font yourself) - enable this in Game Options > HTML5 > Graphics in 2.2.1+ IDEs
  • Added cross-origin type helper functions for HTTP requests: http_set_request_crossorigin() and http_get_request_crossorigin()
  • Changed asset compiler to launch multiple FFmpeg instances to build your sounds, speeding up compile times

Audio Initialisation Changes

  • In response to Chrome changing again in December, we've now made GMS consistent with the browsers expecting a touch/click before all HTML5 audio playback
  • A new audio_system_status System Event will be fired when audio playback becomes available or stops being available in the browser - you can also query this status using audio_system_is_available()
  • Note that this applies to all browsers on all platforms, not just Chrome, and we recommend you always use this system even though some browsers may allow sounds to play without touches having been made
  • Note also that all non-HTML5 platforms will fire this audio availability system event once at Game Start, so they will always return true to audio_system_is_available()
  • See the manual for specifics

Collision Fixes

  • Fixed an issue with "rectangle with rotation" collisions not working on macOS
  • Fixed several issues with collision_...() functions not always detecting collisions with rotated rectangles

Gamepad Functions

  • Added new functions to allow the mapping of hardware buttons/axes/hats to logical GML buttons/axes for Android, Mac, Ubuntu and Windows (Direct Input)
  • Added new functions for reading the hardware 'hat' values and the guid of the device
  • See the manual for specifics
  • Added support for the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller on Windows/Mac/Ubuntu

Misc

  • Fixed game_restart() to make it reset gamespeed to the value set in Game Options
  • Fixed game_restart() to stop changing your random seed if you had changed the room before restarting the game
  • Fixed inconsistency with return key events for virtual keyboards on iOS and Android
  • Fixed vertical tiling issue on texture page with cropping - fixes bug 0030065 but can add extra padding into your tpages
  • Fixed shader compiler so that shader attributes maintain their order - fixes bug 0015841
  • Added more checks to prevent modifying the active surface, which became disallowed in 2.1.5 - clarifies 0030169

This release sees important fixes for Switch project-building, plus fixes for audio falloff not working in 2.1.5 and various emitter/listener issues.

For IDE release notes, see this page.


Android

  • Adaptive icons are currently not supported and we are working on a solution for this in a future release, however we have an FAQ for users to workaround this issue in the meanwhile.

HTML5

  • Layer names are now converted to lowercase in the runner to stop issues with accidental duplicate layers in your project (and make HTML5 consistent with native).

  • Fixed the game window size so it is now as per your room/view settings and no longer locked to a fixed resolution but instead will render at the size you specify.
  • Fixed issue in 2.1.5 where GML errors didn't hold the game running long enough for you to read and confirm the dialog.

Bugs

  • Known Issues can be found on the bug database also - for the current in-game headline list see this page.

This release sees important fixes for Mac submission packages, fixes for iOS audio crash issues, and a number of memory protection fixes on all platforms. New in this release:

  • Collision List Functions
  • New collision type for sprites: Non-axis-aligned bounding box
  • Virtual Keyboard Functions

For IDE release notes, see this page


Collision List Functions

  • Added ..._list() versions of the collision functions (e.g., collision_line_list(), instance_position_list()) to return a list of all colliders, not just the first one found
  • Can also choose to order the list by instance position or leave at the default of instance-creation order, as per the non-list functions()
  • Tends to be much faster than the single-return functions if you need multiple colliders, as there is much less overhead and duplicated checking of instances required
  • See the manual for more information

New collision type for sprites: Non-axis-aligned bounding box

  • Is more accurate than Rectangle collisions because it rotates the bounding box with the sprite rather than making the bounding box bigger
  • Gives better performance than having to use precise collisions (if this new type is applicable for your needs, of course)
  • See the manual for more information

Virtual Keyboard Functions

  • Functions have now been added to show, configure the type of keyboard, get data back, and hide the virtual keyboard
  • Also added system events for when a keyboard is shown or hidden
  • Works on iOS, Android/Amazon (including the TV versions), and UWP
  • Note that these functions will not work when a physical keyboard has been detected
  • See the manual for more information

Changed the default size of the GUI layer

  • Changed the default GUI size for Draw GUI events to match the application_surface size so it is more consistent cross-platform
  • Fixes various issues, such as text placement on some platforms (e.g., Mac)
  • Note if you use a Draw GUI event to scale your GUI and draw the application_surface, you might need to change your project to maintain your expected results:
  • In your first object's Create/Game Start, you could do "var pos = application_get_position(); display_set_gui_maximise(1, 1, pos[0], pos[1]);"
  • Depending on your project, you might find also that simply changing your Draw GUI event to be a Post Draw gives the intended result
  • See the manual for more information

General

  • Fixed various issues with Spine collisions
  • Fixed various issues with collisions when an instance had been deactivated
  • Fixed sprite_add_from_surface() to now show a code error if the sprite has not already been duplicated (as is required), rather than crashing the game
  • Fixed a number of 2.1.4 audio function issues and a few audio memory leaks (see the change log for specifics)

Mac

  • Fixed an issue with Mac builds incorrectly writing out the "friendly name" version of the application type to the package, which caused inability to submit packages to the AppStore
  • Removed 32bit support from packages, which caused recent inability to submit packages to the AppStore
  • Deprecated the synchronous developer get_...() dialog functions, so they now do nothing in-game (avoids errors) - use the ..._async() versions instead

Ubuntu

  • Fixed the name of the audio library the runner looks for on starting the game - fixes lack of audio for some users
  • Fixed "Error deleting sources + buffers" error when trying to close games
  • Fixed sounds popping when stopped if another sound is played directly afterwards

HTML5

  • Fixed Mouse Pressed events not working on scaled canvases because the collision mask is offset
  • Fixed mouse coordinates aren't scaled to match when your window or view is scaled
  • Fixed functions to set the gain on an audio resource so they work as per native platforms
  • Fixed an issue where in-built particles were not shown in 2.1.4
  • Fixed an issue where projects that use Viewports do not render correctly
  • Fixed camera_set_view_angle() to remove various clipping and backbuffer-clearing issues
  • Fixed high refresh rate monitors cause the game to run quicker than intended in Chrome and Firefox

Android

  • Added support for building Android 64bit architectures when using current SDK/NDK versions
  • Note 1: Current SDK/NDK versions have deprecated the older MIPS and ARMv5 architectures, so be careful which settings you use when building
  • Note 2: If you use third-party extensions, these might now need to be updated to support 64bit before you will be able to build them
  • Fixed support for enabling Google Cloud Sync in your manifest
  • Fixed memory leak when using HTTP functionality and also a memory management issue which could have crashed the game if lots of HTTP traffic

iOS

  • Fixed playing music externally and then running your game could crash the game or result in broken audio
  • Fixed getting a call or other system notification sound crashed your game
  • Fixed the iPhone X home bar being visible all the time
  • Fixed an iPhone 6+ audio issue which caused games to crash on this specific device
  • Fixed message dialogs to stop crashes when trying to show code errors on iOS 11+ because the OS has changed how message dialogs work
  • Fixed trying to launch your project when targetting a simulator on the Mac gives an Igor crash report
  • Removed Game Options' "Minimum Time to Display" to fix black splash screen on startup if you had set this option greater than 0
  • Removed 32bit support from packages, which caused recent inability to submit packages to the AppStore

  • NOTE: If you are using a custom index.html you will need to add that new line, otherwise you'll just get a black screen on startup
  • Fixed 28227 - tilemap_clear() no longer skips some tilemap cells
  • Fixed 24947 - ds_list_sort() does not work in HTML5 (now works generally close to Windows's behaviour)
  • Fixed 25723 - window_get_cursor() returns cr_none by default, in spite of GGS setting
  • Fixed 28626 - load_csv() throws a reference error when used
  • Fixed 28765 - ds_map assumes pairs with "undefined" values to be nonexistent
  • Fixed 22247 - pointers are not identified by is_ptr()
  • Fixed 22248 - ds_list_find_value() unable to return a stored pointer
  • Fixed 15450 - window_has_focus() is incorrect at game launch
  • Fixed 17677 - HTML5 module cannot read INI entries stored from ds_grid_write()
  • Fixed 28774 - buffer_delete() does not fully free up the buffer data
  • Fixed 28331 - Drawing a # using draw_text breaks your alignment
  • Fixed 23271 - sprite_delete() doesn't release VRAM in HTML5
  • Fixed 24669 - High DPI Support
  • Fixed 28821 - Some ds_ functions don't return "undefined" on out-of-bounds access like native ones
  • Fixed 20399 - keyboard_key behaves differently in HTML5 than Windows
  • Fixed 19081 - Obfuscated function crashes application after cutscene plays
  • Fixed 25628 - string_count(chr(13), " " + chr(13)) yields 0
  • Fixed 25577 - file_text_write_string() turns "#" into newlines
  • Fixed 21165 - background_get_height() returns cropped texture height instead of asset height
  • Fixed 16924 - game_end() causes an error
  • Fixed 15608 - Destroy Map HTML5 does not remove nested maps
  • Fixed 24070 - texture_set_interpolation is not supported on 2d
  • Fixed 28817 - Select functions replace "#" with newlines while they don't on native
  • Fixed 28309 - Using skeleton_animation_set_frame() freezes your animations permanently
  • Fixed 19994 - 'Destroy instances at position' action does not work as expected
  • Fixed 28760 - Function.arguments is deprecated
  • Fixed 28627 - Keyword "undefined" handling fixed
  • Fixed 28620 - Object Variable definitions do not work on HTML5

Android

  • game_end() will send the game to the background and return the user to the Android desktop, as per Google's specification
  • Debug dialogs show_question(), show_message(), get_string() and get_integer() have been deprecated - please use the '..._async()' versions instead
  • Fixed 29109 - Android package names with a '.' anywhere in the string are disallowed
  • Fixed 28863 - "Always do full install of APK" setting in Preferences in Android tab doesn't work
  • Fixed 28846 - 'APKExpansion' extension does not create a .zip
  • Fixed 25340 - Android SDK 25.2.3+ has no separate "Support Library" package - update Andriod options
  • Fixed 28484 - Uncaught TypeError: _uC1.getParameter is not a function when setting collision mask in GML
  • Fixed 28643 - Runner crashes if you use draw_text_ext with string_width
  • Fixed 28065 - Does not actually disable Lint analysis when this game option is set
  • Fixed 22689 - YYC builds fail if folder path contains special characters

iOS

  • Fixed showing the correct splash screens for iPhone SE, 7, 8 and X
  • game_end() won't do anything on iOS now
  • Debug dialogs show_question(), show_message(), get_string() and get_integer() have been deprecated - please use the '..._async()' versions instead
  • Fixed memory leak when calling extension functions
  • Fixed 27752 - iOS debug should connect without requiring the device's IP to be provided by the user

UWP

  • Added support for the Microsoft 2017 stats and achievements system
  • Added xboxlive_matchmaking_join_session to join a specific session handle
  • Fixed 28400 - Fullscreen switching on Alt+Enter now works
  • Fixed 28398 - Disable cursor on windows now works
  • Fixed 28742 - Windows UWP splashscreen background colour only shows blue on build
  • Fixed 26092 - Remote Worker: Unable to use UWP as a target since no target for UWP can be provided
  • Fixed 28613 - Games crash upon being restored after the OnSuspended event has been fired

Release Notes for 2.1.4

General

  • The audio engine has been consolidated across all platforms and audio synchronisation issues have been fixed
  • Support for IPv6 has been introduced within the networking functions - if you find any issues, please send a sample project to the Helpdesk
  • Async network connection events now contain a new 'other_port' variable
  • #macro definitions now support configs. Use the syntax #macro CONFIG:MACRONAME to override #macro MACRONAME for a given config
  • Buffer-management functions buffer_compress() and buffer_decompress() added
  • Tilemap-management functions tilemap_set_width() and tilemap_set_height() added
  • Fixed an asset compiler crash when a SWF is imported over an existing sprite
  • Instances now correctly inherit Object Variables from parent instance
  • Fixed issues with startup sequence when launching a Steam game outside of the Steam client
  • Fixed issue where a view was not updated first when calling camera_apply()
  • Fixed issues with gamepad support on mcOS and Ubuntu
  • Fixed issues with some string comparisons failing in YYC
  • Fixed issues with screen_save() on several platforms
  • Fixed issues with physics bodies when removing all fixtures and then adding a new fixture
  • Fixed 28482 - Asset Compiler crashes if you have /* as your last line
  • Fixed 21791 - Memory leak when loading/unloading Audio Groups
  • Fixed 28894 - Global variables created using the variable_global_set function don't show up in the watches
  • Fixed 28933 - Steam: Leaderboards - Emojis in usernames cause runner crash
  • Fixed 27413 - GM_version returned only 3 parts of the version number on several platforms
  • Fixed 28946 - font_add_sprite_ext(spr, str, true, 0) when using SWF for "spr" crashes the runner
  • Fixed 28376 - Sprite Editor: [Precise overrides Manual mask values, but the editor does not communicate this properly]
  • Fixed 28723 - steam_set_stat_float doesn't work correctly
  • Fixed 28610 - Object variables of type "Colour" don't seem to work on certain platforms
  • Fixed 28759 - Added new function bool(val) - returns val as a boolean, if val is a number then if it is >0.5 then it is true, if it is a string it will be converted to a number and if >0.5 then it is true, if a ptr it is treated as a number, otherwise it is false.
  • Fixed 28716 - Asset compiler crashes when building this project as there are empty views
  • Fixed 28698 - instance_deactivate_layer doesn't deactivate instances on a layer as they still move using built in variables
  • Fixed 28636 - Having a comma in your YoYo Account name causes a 'Permission Error' compile error when running
  • Fixed 28632 - Issues with instance depth when importing from 1.x
  • Fixed 28358 - Spine: Event information only takes the default value and ignores the value at individual keyframes
  • Fixed 28483 - Debugger: Breakpoints in Clean Up event not triggered if event called by game_end()
  • Fixed 28494 - Configurations: Swapping configs on new projects doesn't work, uses first run config instead

  • Fixed 27564 - Remote Worker: There is no way to set the Steam SDK location
  • Fixed 28367 - Runner titlebar is thinner and uses 1.4's runner icon if built using YYC
